OF THE POL. DEPT. OF QUEENSLAND ON ITS SEPARATION FROM N.S.W., FEB., 1860; IMMIGR. AGT., JAN., 1866, INSPR. OF BENEVOLENT ASYLUM AND ORPHANAGES, ALSO VISITING JUSTICE TO H.M.'S GOAL AND LUN. ASYL., AS WELL AS CH. INSPR. OF DISTILLERIES; UNDER-SEC. AND PERMANENT HEAD OF THE POST AND TELEGRAPH DEPT. IN 1870; MAJOR-COMDT. OF THE QUEENSLAND VOLR. FORCES, 1877; Lieut.-Comdt. IN 1878; RET., NOV., 1879, AND PLACED ON THE STAFF WITH HIS RANK AS Lieut.-Comdt.; AG. COMDT. OF THE DEFENCE FORCES IN FEB., 1883, TO 1884; MEM. OF IMMIGR. BD. SINCE 1865.



McDOUGALD, JOHN.—B. 1848; EDUC. GRAM. SCHL., NEW GLASGOW, NOVA SCOTIA; MERCHANT; REPRESENTED PICTON IN H. OF C., 1881-1896; COMSR. OF CUSTOMS, CANADA, 1896.



MACDOUGALL, KENNETH.—IMP. BRIT. E. AFRICA CO., 1889; COLLR., E. AFRICA PROT., 1ST JULY, 1885; SUB-COMSR., 1901; IMP. BRIT. E. AFRICA CO. MEDAL, AFRICA GEN. SERV. MEDAL (MAZURI REBELLION), AFRICA GEN. SERV. MEDAL (JUBALAND), 2ND CLS. ORDER OF STAR OF ZANZIBAR; REGIST. OFFR. IN CONNECTION WITH SLAVE COMPENSATION CLAIMS, 1ST SEPT., 1907.



McDOWELL, DONALD KEITH, C.M.G. (1901).—PRIN. MED. OFFR. OF W.A.F.F.; ACCOMPANIED ASHANTI EXPEDN., 1900, IN THAT CAPACITY; PRIN. CIV. MED. OFFR., STRAITS SETTLEMENTS, MAR., 1903, AND INSPR. OF HOSPITALS, F.M.S., 1905; PRIN. MED. OFFR., F.M.S., JAN., 1910; RETIRED, 1911.



McELDERRY, SAMUEL BURNSIDE BOYD.—B. 1885; ED. AT CAMBELL COLL., BELFAST, AND TRIN. COLL., DUBLIN; MATH. SCHLR., B.A., SEN. MOD. IN MATHS., SEN. MOD. IN EXP. SCIENCE; CADET, HONG KONG, 27TH OCT., 1909.



MEWEN, THOS. SMITH—ASSOC. M.I.C.E.; AST. ENGR., CAPE GOVT. RLYS., 19TH OCT., 1874; AST. ENGR., 9TH JULY, 1877; MAINTENANCE ENGR., 19TH OCT., 1878; AST. RES. ENGR., PORT ELIZABETH, 15TH MAY TO 29TH SEPT., 1881; MAINTENANCE ENGR., 30TH SEPT., 1881; DIST. ENGR., 1ST DEC., 1881; AST. MAINTENANCE ENGR., 20TH MAR., 1883; DIST. ENGR., UITENHAAG, 27TH SEPT., 1883; DIST. ENGR., CRADOCK, 1ST FEB., 1889; RES. ENGR., IN VARIOUS DISTRICTS, 1891 TO 1897; CHIEF RES. ENGR., TO SUPERVISE LINES BEING CONSTRUCTED BY THAMES IRONWORKS AND SHIPBUILDING CO., 1ST APR., 1899; AST. ENGR.—IN-CHIEF, 15TH MAR., 1901; AST. GEN. MAN., 16TH MAY, 1901; GEN. MAN., 12TH AUG., 1902; MEM. OF RLYS. AND HARBR. BD., UNION OF S. AFRICA, 1910.



MACFARLANE, HAROLD, L.R.C.P., L.R.C.S. (Edin.), D.P.H. (Oxon.), D.T.M. AND H. CAMB.—B. 1876; ED. AT SEDBERGH SCHL., YORKS., EDIN. UNIV., AND ROYAL COLL.; AST. MED. OFFR. OF HEALTH, HONG KONG, SEPT., 1903 TO SEPT., 1909, AND MED. OFFR. IN CHARGE OF GOVT. MORTUARY, KOWLOON, OCT., 1903, TO SEPT., 1905, AND APR., 1906, TO MAR., 1909; GOVT. BIOCHEMIST, OCT., 1909, AND MED. OFFR. IN CHARGE OF MORTUARY, VICTORIA, APR., 1910; LECT. IN PATHOLOGY AND BIOCHEMISTRY IN THE HONG KONG COLL. OF MED.



MACFARLANE, WM. HOLDSWORTH, M.B., CH.B., B. 1850; HOUSE SURG., GEN. HOSP., HOBART, MAY, 1874, TO JUNE, 1877; AST. MED. OFFR., HOSP. FOR INSANE, NEW NORFOLK, NOV., 1878, TO SEPT., 1880; SUPT. AND MED. OFFR., DITTO, 1ST OCT., 1880.



McGOWEN, HON. J. S. T.—M.L.A., WALES, SINCE 1891; PREMIER AND COL. TO 21ST OCT., 1910.



MACGREGOR, D. S.—FELLOW OF SOC. OF AUDITORS; CH. AUDIT CLK., LEEWARDS, 1895; AND FEDERAL ASCNT., JAN., 1896; AG. TREAS. OF LEEWARDS AND ANTIGUA LEG. COUNS. AND ASCNT. COUNS., SEPT., 1897, TO JAN., 1898; ON MISSION TO INVESTIGATE AND ADJUST ASCNT. OF DAD, DEC., 1899, TO MAY, 1900; AUDITOR, HONDURAS, JUNE, 1900; AG. REG. GEN. AND SUP. CT. ON FIVE OCCASIONS IN 1904-5; ASCNT. OF BELIZE, MAR.-APR., 1906; ASCNT. OF MAURITIUS, 11TH OCT., 1905; CHMN., WIDOWS' ORPHANS' FUND, MAY, 1906; COL. AUDITOR, 8TH APR., 1909.



McGREGOR, HON. GREGOR.—B. 1848; M.S. AUSTRALIA, 1894-1901; ELECTED TO SENATE, A. 1901; IS NOW VICE-PRES. OF THE EXEC. C. OF A.



McGREGOR, JAMES COMYN.—2ND LIEUT. BATTN. K.R.R., 1881; LIEUT., 1881; SUB-BATAILLON MTD. POL., 1884; AST. COMAN.



McGREGOR, HON. JAMES DRUMMOND.—1838; SENATOR, NOVA SCOTIA; TWICE NOVA SCOTIA LEGIS., AND ONCE DEFEATED; USEFUL CANDIDATE FOR H. OF C., 1900; TWICE OF NEW GLASGOW; LIEUT.-GOV. OF NOVA SCOTIA.



McGREGOR, JOHN GRANT, M.B. (Aberdeen).—MED. OFFR., S. STILTMILLS.



MacGregor, Sir William, (1907), K.C.M.G. (1889), C.M.G. (1897).—B. 1847; ED. AT ABERDEEN, BERLIN, PARIS, AND FLORENCE; M.B. (Aberdeen), 1874; F.F.P.S.G., 1905; LL.D.; Watson gold medallist, 1872; former med. and res. physician, Glasgow Roy. Inf. Res. Physician, Roy. Lun. Asyl., Ast. Govt. Med. Offr., Seychelles, 1873; Lun. Asyl. and Res. Surg., Civil Hosp., Port Mauritius, 1874; Ch. Med. Offr., Fiji, Also Receiver-Gen., and Mem. of the Exec. Couns., Jan., 1877; Has acted as Reg. Gen. of Immigr. and Comsr. of Lands, 1876, in the suppression of the disturbances in the mountains of Viti Levu, for which he was given a gratuity of 200l.; Joint Coman. of Settlement of debts due from natives of the islands, and for the settlement of all claims against the late Govt. of Fiji; Mem. Native Regulation Board, 1877; Pres. Tonga, 1879, to report on the financial state of that country; Ag. Col. Sec., Nov., 1880, 1884, and Oct., 1874, to Jan., 1875; Adm. of the Govt., and Ag. High Commr. and Officer for the W. Pacific, Jan. to Aug., 1875; Representative of Fiji at the first session of the Federal Australasia, at Hobart, Jan., 1880; Medal of the 2nd Class (1884), with the gold medal of the Roy. Hum. Soc. of Australia, 1885, for saving life at sea; Dep. Med. Offr., Fiji, Sept., 1885, and Aug., 1886; Declared Queen's Sovereignty over Br. New Guinea, 1888; Adminstr., Br. New Guinea, 1888; LL.D., 1896; Gov. Lagos, 1899; Represented African Colonies and Protectorates at Congress, 1902; Gov., Newfoundland, 23rd July, 1902; Queensland, 6th May, 1909; Assumed Office, Dec., 1909.



McGuire, Wm.—B. 1864; Appd. to Compet., Clk. in the Lower Div. of the Civil Service, Assigned to the Audit Office, Nov., 1884; Valuation Office, Ireland, Nov., 1890, and June, 1891; Temp. Staff Officer, 1903.

McHardy, W.—Asst. local auditor, E.A.P., 09.



Machin, Henry Turner.—B. 1832; ed. arm. Schl., Brockville, and Upper Canada Coll., Toronto, Ontario; served in office of British American Land Co., 1849; commercial business, 61; asst. provin. treas., Quebec, 1874.



MacIntyre, Duncan Charles.—Comdr. N.R. (retired); b. 1864; ed. at City of London hl. and Felsted gram. schl.; served 19 years Brit. India Co.; lieut., R.N.R., 1894; promoted to comdr., 1904, in spec. trooping twice; offr. and comding. transports under govt. r 12 years; transport work during S. African st.; commd. depot ship at Taku Forts, during his expd. force; R.H.S. medal for saving fe.; China and S. African medals; senr. offr. N.R. in charge of Hove battery, Sussex; offered pec. survey of Mutla River by E. India rly. co.; arb.-our master and marine mag., Penang, S. Isthm., Sept., 1903.



McIntyre, Hon. John.—Apptd. puisne judge, Tasmania, 1898.



McInnis, Lieut.-Col. Edward Bowater (late 8th Lancers), C.M.G. (1890).—B. 1847; entd. army, 1847; adjt. 9th Lancers for several years, including campaigns of 1878-9-80; Khyber Pass, under Lt.-Gen. Sir F. Maude, K.C.B., 1878; actions of Dei Kaza Killa, Dec., 1879; Siah Sung, Dec., 1879; thres. at Kabul; siege of Sherpur under Lt.-Gen. Sir F. Roberts, K.C.B.; with the 9th Lancers on the march from Kabul to Kandahar; at battle of Mazra (Kandahar), Sept., 1880; twice mentd. in despatches; bronze star, med. and two clasps; inspr.-gen., G. Coast constab., Mar., 1887; mentd. in despatches by Sir R. B. Griffith, K.C.M.G.; comdt. local forces, Trinidad, June, 1890; mem. exec. coun., Sept., 1890; inspr.-gen. of Br. Guiana pol., May, 1891; comdt. Br. Guiana militia, Nov., 1892, with rank of col.; on special duty to Uruan on Venezuelan frontier, Jan., 1896; commanded cavalry of the colonial contingent at J.M.'s Diamond Jubilee, June, 1897; ret., 1902.



Mackay, Alexander Howard, B.A., B.Sc., J.D., F.R.S.C.—B. 1848; ed. at Pictou Academy, Provl. Normal Coll., and Dalhousie Juv., Halifax, 1873; principal, Annapolis Roy., 1873, Pictou, 1873-1889, and Halifax, 1889-1891, academies; lectr. in biology, Dalhousie Univ., 1889-1910; pres. teachers assoc. of Nova Scotia, 1874-1876; of Canada, 1898, of N. Scotia inst. of science, 1900, 1901, and 1902, of summer schl. of science, Atlantic provs., 1887 and 1888, of Victoria chl. of art and design, of biological sect. of roy. oc. of Canada; vice-pres. of religious educn. assoc. (America), of simplified spelling board (America); mem. of geographic bd. of Canada, & marine bd. biological laboratories of Canada, & American and British assoc. for advancement of science, etc.; sec., botanical club of Canada; ov. of Dalhousie univ., of Halifax ladies' coll., tc.; memb. of exec., Strathecona trust for Canada; editor of Dalhousie Gazette, 1870-1873, Educational Review, 1887-1891; Journal of Education, 1891 to date; supt. of educn. for gov. of N. Scotia, since 1891.



Mackay, George, M.A. (Hons.), Aberdeen, 902.—B. 1830; asst. master, Victoria schl., Lechelles, 23rd Aug., 1903; ag. headmaster, Ditto, and ag. inspr. of schl., Nov., 1903; headmaster, Victoria schl., and inspr. of schl., Dec., 904; principal, King's Coll., 1911.



McKay, George Alexander.—B. 1860; federal land tax commr., C. of A., 1st Dec., 910.



McKean, Lieut.-Col. Alexander Chalmers, C.M.G. (1891).—B. 1852; cornet, Inniskilling Dragoons, Oct., 1871; A.D.C., Bengal, 1880; served in Transvaal war, 1881; staff offr., Zululand war (Eshowe column), 1883; D.A.A. and Q.M.G., S. Africa, 1884; ag. D.A.A.G., Natal, 1886; survr. to Zululand and New Republic boundary comm., 1886; asst. commr., Zululand, 1887; commr. of Basuto levies in Zulu disturbances, 1888; was honourably mentioned and made brevet lieut.-col. for services; asst. mil. sec. to gov., Malta, 1889.



Mackenzie, Duncan Stewart.—B. 1868; ed. pub. schl. and coll., Ontario; principal of schls., Strathcona, Alberta, 1895-1903; ch. clk. of dept. of educn., N.W.T., 1904; dep. commr. of educn., N.W.T., 1905; dep. min. of educn., Alberta, since 1905.



McKenzie, Hon. Roderrick.—B. 1852; entd. New Zealand parlmt., 1893; chmn. of comtes., H. of R.; min. of pub. wks. and min. of mines, N.Z., 1910.



Mackenzie, Hon. Thomas.—B. 1854; J.P.; F.R.G.S.; entd. New Zealand parlmt., 1887; min. of industries and commerce, and min. of agricul., N.Z., 1910.



McKeown, Hon. Harrison Andrew, B.A., LL.B., K.C., D.C.L.—B. 1861; ed. at Fredericton coll. schl., and Mt. Allison univ.; called to the bar, New Brunswick, 1880; elec. to legis., N.B., 1890; re-elec., 1899, 1903, and 1908; solr.-gen., 1903; atty.-gen., 1908; judge of sup. ct., N.B., 1909.



Mackey, Hon. John Emanuel, M.A., LL.B.—M.L.A. for Gippsland W., Victoria, since 1902; barrister-at-law, lecturer in equity in Univ. of Melbourne, late ag. prof. of logic and philosophy; min. without portfolio, Victoria, 1904; afterwards commr. of crown lands and survey, and pres. of bd. of lands and wks.



McKinley, John.—Served with I.Y. in S. African campaign, 1900-1; prin. of govt. schl., prisoners of war camp, Simonstown, Jan., 1902; acctnt., educn. dept., O.R.C., 1st July, 1902.



McKinney, E. H.—B. 1877; ent. Bahamas civ. ser., 1898; Out Island commr. (2nd div.), 1909.



McKinstry, Walter Leonard.—B. 1863; barrister-at-law, Lincoln's Inn, 1899; clk. in pub. library, Barbados, 1884; acted in col. secretariat, audit off., sec. to poor law bd., 1885-1889; clk. to inspr.-gen. of pol., 1889; acted inspr. of pol. and asst. supt. of fire brig., 1889-91; int. rev. offr., 1892; transfld. to cust., 1896; ag. gov., Glendairy prison, May to Nov., 1904; ag. pol. mag., 1906-7-8; read. a comm. in volunteer force, Jan., 1902; treas. and collr. of cust., Br. Hond., Apr., 1909; harb.-mast., reger. of shipping, pres., quarantine bd., chmn., pauper relief comte., chmn. of bd. for exam. of pilots, mem. of exec. and legis. coun., J.P., 1909.



Mackintosh, J. A., M.D.—Pub. physician, Inagua, Bahamas, 1907; ditto, Abaco, 1911.



MacLaren, Hon. John James, D.C.L., LL.D.—B. 1842; ed. at Huntington academy and Victoria and McGill univs.; British sec. of British and American joint comm. on Hudson Bay claims in Oregon, 1867-1869; called to the bar, Quebec, 1868; memb. of bar counc. and law examiner; Q.C., 1878; called to the bar, Ontario, 1884; Ontario and Dominion Q.C.; just. of appeal, Ontario, 1902; senator, Toronto univ., and vice-chancellor, Victoria univ.; author of "Bills and Notes," 4th ed., and "Banks and Banking," 3rd ed.

MACLEAN, ADRIAN JOHN.—Ed. at Selwyn Coll., Camb., B.A., 1895; M.A., 1901; asst. collr., E. Africa Prot., 14th May, 1901; collr., 1st Apr., 1906; recorder of titles, 1911.



MACLEAN, JOHN DOUGLAS.—B. 1865; ent. civ. ser., Canada, 1876, as 3rd cl. clk.; promoted to junr. 2nd cls., 1878; senr. 2nd cls., 1882; 1st cls., 1887; ch. clk. and sec. of the dept. of Indian affairs, 1897; asst. dep. supt. gen. and sec., 1908.



MACLEAN, SIMON JAMES, M.A., LL.B., Ph.D.—B. 1871; comsnr. of the Canadian govt. to report on rly. rate grievances, 1901; advsr. to comm., of govt. to draft Railway Act, 1903; prof. of polit. econ., Toronto Univ., 1906-1908; apptd. a mem. of rly. comm., Canada, 1908.



MCLEOD, HON. DONALD.—M.L.A. for Daylesford, Victoria, since 1900; min. without portfolio, 1902-4; min. of mines and water supply, Feb., 1904; min. of mines and forests, Nov., 1904; ag. treas., June to Sept., 1907; mem. of coun. of Melbourne Univ.



MCLEOD, HON. EZEKIEL, B.C.L. (Harv.), LL.D. (New Brunswick univ.)—B. 1840; ed. at high schl., King's co., New Brunswick; called to the bar, 1868; Q.C., 1882; atty.-gen. of N.B., 1882-1883; mem. of senate of univ., N.B., since 1869; elec. to H. of C., Canada, 1891; judge, sup. ct. of N.B., and judge of N.B. v.-a. dist., 1896.



MCLEOD, HON. HARRY F., K.C.—B. 1871; ed. at univ. of New Brunswick (B.A.); admitted barrister, 1893; mayor of Fredericton, N.B., 1907-1908; lieut.-col. 71st York regt., 1908; elec. to legis., N.B., 1908; solr.-gen., 1908.



MACLEOD, KEITH WILLIAM BRUCE.—B. 1865; ed. at Christ's Hosp.; cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Oct., 1888; pol. mag., Panadura, Aug., 1891, Apr., 1893; off. astt. to gov't. agt., S. Prov., Mar., 1892; dist. judge Ratnapura, June, 1894, Feb., 1896; landing survr., customs, Colombo, Mar., 1895; dist. judge Kurunegala, Apr., 1899, Batticaloa, Oct., 1899, Matara, Nov., 1899; pol. mag., Colombo, Mar., 1900; asst. gov't. agt., Matara, Dec., 1901; dep. collr. of cust., Colombo, Aug., 1902; gov't. agt., prov. of Uva, Apr., 1906; dist. judge, Kurunegala, Aug., 1906; pol. mag., Colombo, Sept., 1906; ag. dist. judge, Galle, Apr., 1907; addl. dist. judge and comsnr. of requests, Kandy, Mar., 1909; ag. chmn., mun. coun., and mayor, Colombo, May, 1910.



MCLEOD, MURDOCH JAMES.—Clk. of the exec. coun., and dep. prov. treas. of the prov. of Alberta, Canada, 1905.



MACLEOD, NEIL.—Called to the bar, P.E.I., 1872; mem. of house of assem. since 1879; prov. sec. and treas., 1879 to 1882; atty.-gen. and premier, 1889; judge, Prince county ct., P. E. Island, 1893.



MACLEOD, NORMAN MAGNUS, C.M.G. (1880).—B. 1839; late capt. 74th Highlanders; was commdnt. of Swazi contingent against Sikukuni, 1879.



MACLURE, WILLIAM GRANT.—Admtd. Bahamas Bar, 1889; asst. clk., House of Assem., 1890; J.P. for col. and prov. res. just., Gov.'s Harbour, 1894; acted as stip. and circuit mag. and coroner, Is. of New Providence; registr., sup. ct., Bahamas, 1898; ag. stip. and circuit mag., Sept. to Dec., 1909.



MCMILLAN, SIR DANIEL HUNTER, K.C.M.G. (1902).—B. 1846; ed. Canada; served with Canadian Volunteers on Niagara frontier, 1864; during Fenian raid, 1866; Red River expdn., 1870; N.W. rebellion (medal), 1886; mem. for Winnipeg in Manitoba legislature, 1889; mem. of Manitoba govt., 1889; lt.-gov. of Manitoba, 6th Sept., 1900; re-apptd. for second term, audit dept., retired 1911.



MCMILLAN, EWEN JUDSON.—B. 1852; govt. sta., Charlottetown Business Coll., Guelph Agric. Coll., received degree of B.S.A., June, 1900; O.R.C., R.U.I., govt. experiment farm and lecturer in Canada, 1901-4; chief of experimental farms, Prince of Wales' Coll., Prince Edward Island, Canada, 1901-4; chief of experimental farms, live stock division, O.R.C., June, 1904; agr. instr., div. of agric., July, 1905; ag. dir. of agric. inst., 1906-1908; ag. dir., 1908-1910.



MCMILLAN, L. B.—B. 1873; ed. phil., Charlottetown, Prince Edward Is.; clk., P.E. Is. govt., 1890; clk., 1893; sec. to wks., P.E. Is., 1900.



MCMILLAN, ROBERT FURSE.—Queen's Westminster school; scholar, Trim Hall; senior in law tripos, 1879; holder of law ship at Trim Hall; Inn of Court student, Inner Temple common law scholarship; called to the bar, 1881; joined western circuit and Exeter sessions; puisne judge, W. Ireland, 1903.



MCGAB, ARCHIBALD P.—B. 1864; ed. high schl., Vankleek Hill; elec. to parl., Saak., 14th Aug., 1908; min. of mun., 10th Dec., 1908; re-elec. by acclamation, elec., 24th Dec., 1908.



MACNAUGHTEN, LESLIE HAY.—Wellington Coll., and Truro Survey Coll.; astt. engrnr., P.W.D., E. Ald., 15th May, 1906.



MACNAUGHTEN, T. C.—B. 1873; ed. house and Oxford; scholar of Hertford 1st class classical moda., 1894; B.A., after compet. exam., 2nd class clk., Leg., Bd., Feb., 1896; 2nd class clk., C.O.S., priv. sec. to Earl of Selborne, Dec., 1896; of Onslow, Nov., 1900, to Duke of Marlborough, July, 1903; 1st cl. clk., 24th Mar., 1904.



MCEWEN, MAJ.-GEN. SIR JOHN (G.C.B. (1882), K.C.M.G. (1880), C.M.G., V.C., B. 1831; served during campaign in India as A.D.C. to Sir E. Lugard, siege and capture of Lucknow; in 1860-61, Tipperary flying column during Fenian affances, 1866-67; served on the staff of the expdn. under Sir G. Wolseley in 1870 Ashanti war, 1873-74; A.D.C. to H.R.H. Duke of Cambridge, Jan., 1874, and as Her Majesty in Aug. following; served Egyptian expdn., 1882, personally attached to Duke of Connaught; served in the Sevastopol expdn., 1855; commanded troops at the action for which clasp was granted.



MCDONALD, THOS. SYDNEY.—B. 1870; Marist Coll., Sydney; clk., acco. dept., Perth, W. Australia, 1886; ditto, 1897; mem. mun. coun., 1901-3; sec. to goldfields water super., 1903; under-secr. for agric. and industr., 1903.



MCDOWAN, ISLAY.—3rd clk., col. Fiji, Sept., 1892; stip. mag., astt. comsnr., and tax inspr., Lau, Matavai, mag. and tax inspr., Navua, and astt. comsnr., Namasi, Feb., 1900; stip. mag. Lautallevu; comsnr. and tax inspr., Lautallevu in charge, Levuka gaol, Jan., 1904; inspr. constab. and prisons, and sheriff, 15th Nov., 1904.



MACPHERSON, A.—Ed. at Keith, Scotland; served during S. Afric. war, Lord Dunraven's sharpshooters; clerk, off. and paymaster, Imperial res.

to 14th Dec., 1902; ch. clk. and sen. examr. of its., audit dept., O.R.C., 15th Dec., 1902; store tnt., govt. stationery and printing off., O.R.C., ly., 1904.



McPHERSON, JOSEPH CLARKE, M.B., B.Ch., A.O., R.U.I.—Ed. at Queen's coll., Belfast; graduated, 1904; medical scholarships, Queen's I., Belfast, 1899, 1901; honours, Roy. univ., Lond., 1899, 1900, 1901; asst. med. offr., Edmonton infirmary, 1904-1905; private practice, 06-1908; ag. med. offr., dist. 3, St. Kitts, Edward Is., 1909; supt. med. offr., Leeward Is., ay., 1910.



McROBERTS, B.A.K.—Ass. supt. of police, A.P., 1911.



McTURK, MICHAEL, C.M.G. (1897).—B. 1843; venue offr. and asst. survr., Essequibo, 1872; assmnr. of taxation, Essequibo dist., 1873; special ag. and supt. crown lands and forests, Essequibo, 1878; govt. gold mining offr., Br. Guiana, 1887; assmnr., Essequibo and Pomeroon districts; sen. assmnr., B. Guiana bdry. survey; prot. of bor.-signal Indians for the col.; trav. mag., 90-95.



MACWILLIAM, DONALD KIRTON.—2nd clk., reasym., St. Kitts, 1894; rev. offr. and quarantine mfr., Apr., 1894; rev. offr. and harb. mast., 1906.



MADDEN, HON. SIR FRANK, Kt. Bach. (1911).—M.L.A. Victoria since 1894; has been hmn. of bd. of examiners for attorneys, and pres. of law institute; speaker of legis. ass., Victoria, since June, 1904.



MADDEN, HON. SIR JOHN, K.C., G.C.M.G. (1906), K.C.M.G. (1899), K.T. BACH. (1893).—B. 1844; d. justice of Victoria, 1893; administered the govt., 1893, 1895, 1897, and 1898, and again, as leut.-gov., Jan., 1900-1.



MADDEN, W.—Pres. bd. of land and wks., and assmnr., crown lands and survey, Victoria, Aug., 1881, to Mar., 1883.



MAGRATH, THOS. HENRY.—Jun. clk., P.O., Tasmania, 1853; ch. clk., 1869; comptroller of money orders, 1879, and of savings bank, 1882; ec. to P.O., 1888.



MACRO, PROF. ENRICO, M.D.—B. 1854; grad. falta Univ., 1877; examr. in arts and sciences, 882; examr. in med. and surgery, 1884; prof. of math. and physics, Oct., 1885; examr. in land surveying and archi., Oct., 1885; ag. princ. and sec. o the univ., 1887; ag. asst. dir. of educn. and tc. to the senate, 1888-97; ag. inspr. in charge of elem. schls., Jan., 1898; sec. to Oxford exam. cells in Malta, 1898; dir. of elemen. schls., 1899; mem. ex. coun. and of coun. of ovt., 1902; dir. of pub. instr. and rector of the univ., 1904.



MAHAFFY, ARTHUR WM.—B. 1869; ed. at Marlborough, and Magdalen Coll., Oxford, demy, 889; B.A., Dublin Univ. (Trin. Coll.); 2nd ent., 1st Batt. Royal Munster Fusiliers, 1892-93; gov. agt. Gilbert Is. Prot., Oct., 1896; asst. res. commnr., Solomon Is., 1897; res. mag., W. division, Solomon Is., and dep. commnr. for W. Pacific, 1899; col. sec. and recvr.-gen., Fiji, Oct., 1904; asst. to high commnr. for W. Pacific, 1908; st. high commnr. for Solomon Is., 1908; ag. res. commnr., Gilbert and Ellice Is. Prot., Jan.-June, 1909; sent on spec. mission to New Hebrides, ov., 1909; invited by Commonwealth govt. to attend conference on wireless telegraphy at Melbourne, Jan., 1910; asst. high commnr., 24th dec., 1910, to 20th Feb., 1911, and from 6th to 8th Sept., 1911.



MAIN, T. W.—Supt., pub. gardens, Selangor, lay., 1906; supt. of govt. plantations, Perak, Sept., 1906; asst. curator, botanic gardens, Singapore, Mar., 1908.



MALTAND, ANDREW GIBB.—B. 1864; read. his educn. as a geologist and civil engr. at Yorkshire Coll. of Science, Leeds; asst. govt. geologist, Queensland, 1888; his official duties taking him as far afield as Br. N. Guinea; govt. geol. of W. Australia, 1896; has written several works on the geology, features, and mineral resources of Queensland, British New Guinea, and W. Australia.



MAJOR, SIR CHARLES, Kt. Bach. (1911).—Called to the Bar (Mid. Temp.), June, 1887; mem. of Leeward Is. bar, Sept., 1887; chancellor of the diocese of Antigua, Oct., 1889; nominated mem. of legis. coun., Antigua, 1895 to 1899; nominated mem. of gen. legis. coun., Leewards, Nov., 1896, and pres. of same, Dec., 1896, to 1899; mem. fed. ex. couns., Leewards, Mar., 1897, to June, 1901; vice-pres. legis. coun., Antigua, May, 1897; ag. sol.-gen. and atty.-gen., Leewards, 1897, 1898, 1899; capt. commanding Antigua volunteer defence force on its establishment, 1897; J.P., 1897; ag. 2nd puisne judge, Leewards, June, 1899; atty.-gen. of Grenada, 1901; ch. just. of Fiji, and chief judicial commnr. of Western Pacific, 1902; admstd. govt., Mar.-Oct., 1904.



MAJOR, FRANCIS WM., I.S.O. (1910).—B. 1863; 5th clk. treas., Trinidad, Oct., 1885; 2nd clk. to supt. of prisons, Jan., 1886; 9th clk., audit office, Aug., 1887; 8th clk. ditto, 1888; sec. to road and crown lands commnr., agri. contracts commnr., and civ. ser. commnr., Trinidad, between 1887 and 1890; acted on various occasions as 3rd clk., surg.-gen.'s off., 1887 to 1890; 3rd clk. of cust., priv. sec. to Sir W. Robinson, 1888; supervisor of cust., G. Coast, 1891; asst. compt. of cust., 1891; asst. treas., Aug., 1891; ag. compt. of cust., on various occasions, 1891 to 1895; compt. of cust., Nov., 1895; sent by govt. to W. bndry. of col. to inquire into and report on necessity for estabtmt. of prev. ser., 1896; sent by govt. to Volta river to organise prev. ser., 1897; recvr.-gen., Bermuda, June, 1899; prepared scheme (which was approved by S. of S.) for improvement of finanl. adminstr. of Bermuda; chief of customs, B. E. Africa, 11th Mar., 1908; M.L.C., 1910.



MALAN, HON. FRANCOIS STEPHANUS.—B. 1871; ed. in S. Africa and Camb.; B.A. Science, Cape univ.; LL.B., Camb.; advocate of sup. ct., Cape Colony, 1895; M.L.A. for Malmesbury, 1900; re-elected, Feb., 1904; min. of agric., Cape Colony, 1908; min. of educn., Union of South Africa, 1910; attended Imp. Conf., 1911.



MALCOLM, DOUGAL ORME.—B. 1877; ed. at Eton and New Coll., Oxford; 1st cl. mods., 1897; 1st cl. lit. hum., 1899; B.A., 1899; Fellow of All Souls, 1899; M.A., 1902; apptd., after compet. exam., 2nd cl. clk., C.O., Oct., 1900; priv. sec. to Earl of Selborne, high commnr. for S. Africa, Mar., 1905; sec. to Earl Grey, govt. gen. of Canada, 1910; retd. to C.O. as ag. 1st cls. clk., Dec., 1911.



MALCOLM, HARCOURT GLADSTONE.—Priv. sec. to Sir Henry Jackson when admnstr. of Bahamas, 1892, 1893, 1895; ditto to Sir W. F. Haynes-Smith, govt. of Bahamas, 1895; called to the bar, Lincoln's Inn, June, 1899; ditto, Bahamas, July, 1899; mem. of house of ass., Bahamas, 1900; deputy-speaker, 1901; re-elected, 1904 and 1911; ag. atty.-gen., Aug. to Nov., 1905; Sept., 1906 to Feb., 1907; July to Nov., 1910; and from Apl. to Dec., 1911; K.C., 1910; thanked by S. of S. for assistance to atty.-gen. in drafting bills;

thanked by legis. for obtaining copies of early records.



MALCOLM, SIR ORMOND DRIMMIE, K.T. BACH. (1898).—B. 1839; called to the bar of the Bahamas, July, 1861; ag. pol. mag. in 1864 and 1866; elected mem. of house of assem. in 1865; speaker, 1868; ag. judge, court of common pleas, 1873; Q.C. in 1876; ag. atty.-gen., Mar., 1882; ag. admnstr., June, 1895; ch. just. of Bahama Is., 1897; retired, Jan., 1910.



MALING, CAPT. IRWIN CHAN., C.M.G. (1892).—B. 1841; ed. at Wimbledon schl. and Roy. Mil. Acad.; late 23rd Roy. Welsh Fus.; dep. mag. and collr., Nuddea dist., Bengal, 1857; served throughout the Indian mutiny, 1857-59; present in many engagements (medal); ensign, 1861, 89th Princess Victoria's Regt.; priv. sec. and A.D.C. to the gov., W. Coast of Africa, 1868; lieut. 35th Roy. Sussex Regt., 1870; priv. sec. to the Marquis of Normanby, gov. of Queensland, 1871, and New Zealand, 1874; col. sec. and regir.-gen. of Grenada, 1879; adminstd. the govt. in 1880, 1882, 1884-7; ag. col. sec., Leeward Is., 1888-9; and represtve. at quarantine confe. at Demerara, 1888; ag. administr., 1889; administr. of St. Vincent, 1889; ret. 1893.



MALONE, CLMENT.—Ag. jnr. audit clk., Antigua, July and Aug., 1901, and Mar. to Nov., 1902; ag. 2nd clk., registr. office, Aug. to Oct., 1902; ag. cashier, St. John's savings bank, Jan. to June, 1903; ag. acctnt., treas., Dec., 1902, and July to Dec., 1903; acctnt. of treas., Antigua, Dec., 1903; clk. to income and trade tax assessors, Jan., 1905; acctnt., treas., St. Kitts, June, 1909.



MALONEY, JOHN O'DONALD.—B. 1878; asst. for sugar cane experiments, Barbados, 1904-1906; tempy. cotton instructor, Nevis, Oct., 1906, to Jan., 1907; ag. instructor, Nevis, April, 1907.



MANN, MAJ.-GEN. J. R., R.E., C.M.G. (1881).—B. 1823; entered R.E., 1840; survr.-gen. of Mauritius, 1856 to 1861; dir. of roads and survr.-gen. of Jamaica, 1867; resig. 1873, and re-apptd. in Feb., 1874; official, M.L.C., 1874; ret., 1886.



MANNING, GEORGE FREDERICK.—B.A., Trin. Coll., Dublin, 1898; joined Bechuanaland div. B.S.A. pol., 1898; served through S. African war until 1901; chief constable, Nyasaland Prot., 1901; asst. collr., Mar., 1901; 2nd grade res., Aug., 1907.



MANNING, BRIG.-GEN. SIR WM. HENRY, K.C.M.G. (1904); C.B. (1903).—B. 1863; ed. at Camb. and Roy. Mil. Coll., Sandhurst; heut., 2nd batt., S. Wales Bord., 24th Foot, 1886; capt., 1897; brevet-major, 1898; brevet-lieut.-col., 1899; brevet-col., 1904; joined Indian army, 1888; 51st Sikhs, frontier force, 1891; 2nd Burmese war (wounded, medal and clasp); Samana and Hazara expds., N.W. frontier of India, 1891 (clasp); C. Africa, 1893-4 (medal); C. Africa and Rhodesia, 1894-98 (clasp); Somaliland campaign (medal and 2 clasps); dep. comsnr. and cons.-gen. for B.C. Africa, 1897; acted as comsnr. and cons.-gen., Dec., 1897, to Dec., 1898, and also from July, 1900, to Apr., 1901; raised, and commd., C. Africa regt.; commd. Somaliland field force, 1902-1903; commd. 1st brig., Somaliland field force, 1903-4; inspr.-gen., K.A.R., 1901; ag. gov. of Nyasaland Prot., 1907; gov., Somaliland Prot., 7th Jan., 1910; gov. Nyasaland Prot., 5th Nov., 1910; assumed gov., 6th Feb., 1911; rec. Coronation medal, 1911.



MANSEL, GEORGE, C.M.G. (1891).—Served in Weenen Yeomanry through the Langalibalele rebellion in 1873; served as sub-inspr. and inspr. in Natal mounted pol. through Zulu war (medal with clasp), and Boer war, 1880-1; raised and commanded the Reserve Terminus bineers from 1883 to 1887, when the force changed into the Zululand pol.; served force through all disturbances in Zululand 1883 to 1888; twice mentioned in despatches having shown conspicuous coolness and action; asst. comsnr., Natal pol., 1891; commdt., 1902; ch. comsnr., pol., Jan., ret., 1906.



MANSERGH, CORNEWALL LEWIS WHITNEY, I.S.O. (1906).—B. 1863; clk. comsnr. office, Capetown, 1880; 2nd cl. clk. and asst. to comsnr. of crown lands and pub. works, 1st cl. clk., 1892; ch. clk. to the ass't. comm'd. rlyv. and pub. wks., Oct., 1892; sec. prov. July, 1898; asst. prov. sec., Cape, 1911.



MANSERGH, JOHN LOPTUS OTWAY, Haileybury Coll.; S. African war, 1899; Queen's and King's medals; 3rd King's rifles, E. Africa Prot., Apr., 1902; ret., 8th June, 1906; dist. comsnr., 1911.



MANSON, SIR PATRICK, K.C.M.G. C.M.G. (1900); F.R.S., M.D., F.R.C.P.L. 1844; late dean and lect. on med. coll. Chinese, Hong Kong; phys. Seamen Soc. at Albert Docks branch; lect. diseases, Charing Cross Hosp., and ser. London schl. of trop. med.; apptd. med. to C.O., 1897; mem. of hon. med. sleeping sickness bureau, 1908.



MANTLE, ALFRED FRANK.—B. London and Watford, England; fac. Canada, 1898 to 1908; agric. editor, "Free Press," Dec., 1907, to Nov., 1908; stats. branch of the Saskatchewan agric., Nov., 1909; dep. min. of agric., 1st Sept., 1910.



MARKS, OLIVER.—B. 1866; supt. Perak, Mar., 1891; 2nd cls. mag., Apr., asst. mag., Kinta, July, 1894; asst. mag., July, 1896; ag. asst. sec. to govt., Perak, May, 1896; asst. sec. to govt., Perak, May, Malay, Mar., 1898; 1st cl. mag., asst. sec. to res. gen., Fed. Malay Sep., 1898; ag. sec. to res. gen., F. M. S., sec. to high comsnr., F. M. S., priv. sec. to gov. S. Stlmta, in adm., 1904; ag. dist. offr., Lower Perak, ag. sec. to res., Perak, Mar., 1910; ag. in addition, July to Sept., 1910.



MARCEL, HON. CHARLES, LL.D., Univ.—B. 1860; elec. to H. of C. Bonaventure, 1900; dep. speaker 1905-1908; re-elec. at gen. elec., 1908; h. of C., 1909.



MARLBOROUGH, 9TH Duke of (1702), CHARLES RICHARD JOHN CHURCHILL, P.C., K.G.—B. 1871; Primrose League, 1897 and 1898; yeomanry cavalry, S. Africa, 1900; Lieut.-Gen. Sir Ian Hamilton, K.G., master-general, 1899; under-secr. of colonies, July, 1903, to Dec., 1905.



MARRIOTT, HAYES, B.A., B. Math. tripso, Cantab.—Cadet S. Sin., 1896; ag. 3rd mag., Singapore, May, fin. exam. in Malay, May, 1898; Malacca, Feb., 1899; ag. 2nd mag., 1902; asst. P.M.G., Penang, Sept., 2nd mag., Penang, July, 1904; ag. Sing., Feb., 1905; ag. 2nd mag., Sing., ag. collr. of land rev., Sing., Mar., 1907; col. sec., 1st May, 1907, but conti-

llr. of land revenue, Singapore; ag. inspr. of isons, S.S., June, 1908.



MARSDEN, ARTHUR.—Ed. at Bowden coll.; tief of cust., E. Africa Prot., 6th Aug., 1895; Apr., 1908; gov. of Mombasa jail, 1st Sept., 1895; 31st Mar., 1903; collr. of cust. for Uganda rot., 1st July, 1896; prot. of immigrts., 18th ov., 1896, to 31st Mar., 1904; vice-consul, (mombasa, 13th Jan., 1899; held marriage warrant, 1st Apr., 1902, to 31st Mar., 1903; Ashanti medal (1895-96), for Mazrui rebellion, Sept., 1903; ptd. by S. of S. for foreign affairs to visit S. Africa to report on the prospects of trade between I. and S. Africa as well as to make known the suitability of the E. African Highlands for white immigrants and to encourage their colonisation by desirable settlers, Sept., 1904; Waki. omsntr., 1st Apr., 1906; currency comsrr., 2nd May, 1908; apptd. col. emigtn. agt. in Calcutta for Trinidad, Jamaica, Fiji and Mauritius.



MARSH, EDWARD HOWARD, C.M.G. (1908)—B. 1872; ed. at Westminster and Cambridge; scholar, Trin. Coll., 1891; 1st cl. classical tripso, 1893; sen. chancellor's medal for classics, 1895; 1st cl. with distinction classical tripso, Part II., and B.A., 1895; M.A., 1897; apptd., after compet. exam., 2nd cl. clk., C.O., Sept. 29th, 1896; ast. priv. sec. to Mr. Chamberlain, July, 1900; to Mr. Lyttelton, Oct., 1903; 1st cls. clk., 1st Apr., 1905; priv. sec. to Mr. Winston Churchill, U.S. of S. for the Colonies, Jan., 1907; priv. sec. to Mr. Churchill as Pres. of B. of T., 1908; priv. sec. to Mr. Churchill as Home Sec., 1910; priv. sec. to Mr. Churchill as first Lord of the Admiralty, 1911; accompanied Mr. Churchill on his visit to E. Africa and Uganda, 1907-8.



MARSH, T. R., C.M.G. (1901), on retirement from post as head of the contract branch, Crown agents office; B. 1847.



MARSHALL, DUNCAN M.—B. 1872; ed. Walkerton high schl. and Owen Sound coll., inst.; farmer, journalist; formerly propr. of "Thornbury Standard," "Clarksburg Reflector" and "Bracebridge Gazette"; now propr. of "Olds Gazette"; owns and operates large farm in Olds dist.; unsuccessful cand. for H. of C., in Muskoka, Ont., 1904; el. to Alberta legislature, e.g., Mar., 1909; min. of agric. and prov. sec., Nov., 1909; re-apptd. min. of agric. in Sifton admstr., 1910.



MARSHALL, COLONEL ROBERT SETON.—B. 1864; lieut. 3rd brig. Scottish div. R.A., 1882; (lieut. reserve of offs., 1883); capt., 1885; instructor of artillery, 1887; (capt., res. of offs. 1896); major Edin. artill. militia, 1896 (hon. major in the army, 1900); hon. lt.-col., 1903; lt.-col., 1903; retired with hon. rank of col., 1903; served with the 1st brig. W. div. R.A., 1885; staff off. local forces, Trinidad, Sept., 1888, to Dec., 1891; sec local defence comte., 1888; command of Trinidad artill. volrs. for purpose of organising the corps, 1888; A.D.C. to offr. adminstr. govt. of Trin. and Tobago, May to Dec., 1889; ag. commdt. Trinidad local forces, 6th-19th Nov., 1890; adjt. and musketry instr. Br. Guiana pol., Dec., 1891; ag. adjt. Br. G. militia, May to Oct., 1894; and Aug. to Sept., 1897; ag. inspr. of Br. G. pol. during period of special employment at Ururan frontier station, Oct., 1895, to Mar., 1896; adjt. of Br. G. militia and police, Dec., 1897; ag. commdt., Br. G. militia, 9th May to 22nd Aug., 1900; sent to frontier to hand over Amacura and Barima Sands to Venezuela, Oct., 1900; sent to Trinidad for special duty with police, after the riot, 2nd to 27th May, 1903; adjt., B.C. vols., 26th Feb., 1906; ag. comdt., ditto, in 1906 and 1907; also dep. inspr. of pris., 10th July to 22nd Nov., 1906; and ag. H.M. inspr. of pris. from 6th July, 1907; dep. inspr.-gen. of constab., Trinidad, 1907; ag. inspr.-gen. and comdt. of local forces, 1909.



MARTIN, HON. ARCHER.—B. 1865; called to the bar, 1887; apptd. counsel for Dom. govt. and representative of minis. of just. in Vancouver Island, 1896; spec. com. to investigate affairs of B.C. crown timber lands agency, 1897; puisne judge of sup. ct. of B.C., 1898; deputy judge in Admiralty for B.C., 1899; spec. comsn. to settle mining disputes in Porcupine district arising out of Brit. and U.S. treaty on Canada-Alaskan boundary, 1900; judge in Admiralty for B.C., 1902; just. of appeal for B.C., 1909; author of "The Hudson Bay Co.'s Land Tenures"; "Chart of the Judges of B.C. and V.I."; "Genealogy of Martin of Ballinahinch Castle"; "Martin's Mining and Water Cases" (2 vols.).



MARTIN, CHARLES MACDERMOT.—B. 1865; ed. privately and Univ. Coll., London; B.A., Lond. Univ. (honours English language), 1893; inspr. of schls., Jamaica, Apr., 1895; ag. examr., educn. dept., Jamaica, July-Oct., 1895; inspr. of schls., Leeward Is., Apr., 1900.



MARTIN, GEORGE GOZARD.—Cik., audit off., South Australia, Mar., 1873; clk., marine bd., Jan., 1874; clk. ch. sec.'s off., Sept., 1874; clk., lands titles off., Aug., 1877; clk., law officers dept., July, 1880; ch. clk. and acctnt., law officers' dept., Nov., 1888; sec. to atty.-gen. and min. of educn., Jan., 1905; sec. to atty.-gen., July, 1905.



MARTIN, HENRY—Sub-inspr., Bechuanaland Prot., Police, 1896; ag. asst. res. mag., Serowe, 1906-07; inspr., Bech. Prot. pol., 1909.



MARTIN, H. A.—Ag. clk. to auditor, Grenada, Aug., 1884, to June, 1885; clk. to pro-marshal, June to July, 1885; ag. ch. to audr., May to Nov., 1887; ast. clk., treasy., Jan., 1889; ag. wks. acctnt., Jan. to Oct., 1890; ch. clk., regisr., Nov., 1891; treasy. acctnt., St. Lucia and Grenada, Apr., 1894; supt. prisons, Feb. to May, 1897; 2nd financial asst., P.W.D., Ceylon, June, 1897; acctnt. and fin. asst., gen. treasy., May, 1905.



MARTIN, HORACE.—B. 1864; entd. C.A. office, 2nd Feb., 1881; ast. head of shipping dept., 1893; head of miscellaneous dept., 1900; ast. sec., 1st July, 1909.



MARTIN, S. B.—Ed. Wesleyan Mission Schl., G. Coast; 6th class offr., customs, G. Coast, Sept., 1890; clk. to dir. of telegraphs and storekeeper, Aug., 1891; clk. and acctnt., July, 1893.



MARTIN, V. J.—M. Eng. (Liv. Univ.), A.M.I.C.E.; ast. supt. of wks., S. Settmts., Mar., 1904; transf. to F.M.S., 1909.



MARTIN, W. P.—Treasy. ast., E.A.P., 1910.



MARTINS, FREDERICK GERMANO.—B. 1866; ed. C.M.S. Coll. Inst., Lagos; jun. bailiff, sup. ct., June, 1884; clk. to Queen's advoc., Aug., 1886; storekeeper, P.W. dept., Jan., 1891; audit clk., Jan., 1896; ch. clk., audit off., Jan., 1908.



MARTINS, G. N.—Ed. C.M.S. Grammar Schl., Lagos; messenger, audit, and P.O., 1889; customs, outdoor offr., 1890 to 1893 (during which time attached to revenue office); ag. clk., P.O., 1893; 4th clk. of customs, 1893; 3rd clk. and statistician, Mar., 1894; transf. to the revenue dept., 1900; deputy for cashier and ch. clk. on various occasions;

2nd cl. clk., customs, 1901; chief examining offr. of cust., Lagos, 1st Mar., 1905.



MARWICK, Allan Graham.—Served in Natal civ. serv., 1895 to 1899; sub. native commr., Mbabane, Swaziland, Jan., 1903, to Mar., 1907; asst. commr., ditto, 22nd Mar., 1907.



MARWOOD, Horace Richard, M.I.C.E.—B. 1857; junr. asst. engr., Taff Vale rlyw., 1877; supernumerary 2nd cl. asst. engr. Cape Govt. rlyws. (Eastern system), 1882; 1st cl. asst. W. system, 1883, also in charge of district, 1884; asst. engr. rlyw. service of H.H. the Sultan of Selangor, S.S. 1885; chef-de-division, Pyraeus Lavissa rlyw., Greece, 1890; engr. of wks. and maintenance, Trinidad govt. rlyws., 1894; acted as gen. man. on eight occasions between 1895 and 1906; gen. man. and ch. engr., 1906.



MASKELL, Thos. Augustus Cornelius.—Cler. asst. to inspr. of schls., B. Guiana, June, 1878; clk., Apr., 1891; 3rd cls. clk., Apr., 1893; sec. to educn. commr., 1902.



MASON, Arthur Wier, B.A.—Puisne judge, sup. ct., Natal, 1896; ag. ch. just., 1900-01; commr. of spec. treason ct., 1900-01; pres. of ditto, 1901-02; puisne judge, sup. ct., Transvaal, 1902.



MASON, Gerald Bovell.—Ed. Harrison Coll., Barbados; matric., London Univ., 1890; joined London hosp., 1890; passed prelim. scientific, 1892; M.R.C.S. (Eng.), L.R.C.P. (Lond.), 1896; jun. asst. med. offr., St. Marylebone infirmary, 1896; clin. asst., aural and ophthalmic depts., Lond. hosp., 1897; house physician, Brompton hosp., 1898; ag. med. offr., Three Counties asylum, 1899; civ. surg. in charge, Station hosp., Woking, 1902; apptd. med. offr., No. 4 dist., Antigua, 1903; ag. commr., Virgin Is., 1904; surg.-lieut., Antigua def. force, 1904; mag. and med. offr., Anguilla, and dep. judge of sup. ct., Leeward Is., Jan., 1905, to Sept., 1906; med. offr., No. 6 dist., Nevis, 1906; med. offr., dist. "D," and mag. dist. "F," Dominica, 1907.



MASON, James Scott.—B. 1873; ed. at Manchester Gram. Schl. and Brasenose Coll., Oxford; cadet, F.M.S. civ. serv., 6th Nov., 1896; ag. collr. of land rev., Batang Padang, Perak, 1st May, 1897; ag. asst. dist. mag., Tanjong Malim, 25th Aug., 1897; passed final exam. in Malay, 29th Mar., 1898; ag. collr. of land rev., Natang, 1st Apr., 1898; ag. asst. mag. and collr. of land rev., Krian, also ag. Indian immigr. agt., Perak in addition, 4th Dec., 1898; passed exam. in law, 11th Jan., 1899; received thanks of govt. for services in connection with Krian smallpox riots, Mar., 1899; ag. collr. of land rev., Lower Perak, 19th Mar., 1899; asst. dist. offr., Raub, Pahang, 1st Jan., 1900; dist. offr., Raub, 1st Jan., 1902; passed bonus exam. in Tamil, 18th Apl., 1902; dist. offr., Jelebu, Negri Sembilan, 1st Oct., 1905; continued as dist. offr., Raub, until 2nd Apl., 1907; ag. dist. offr., Klang, Selangor, 7th Aug., 1907; State treas., Perak, 15th May, 1908; continued as ag. dist. offr., Klang; ag. asst. supt. of Indian immigr. in addition, 3rd Sept. to 6th Nov., 1908; British adviser to the govt. of Kelantan, July, 1909.



MASSON, John Leslie.—Acting clk., survr.-gen.'s off., Natal, 15th Dec., 1881; 1st cl. clk. and chief clk., survr.-gen.'s off., 1st Jan., 1889; asst. survr.-gen., 1st July, 1890; survr.-gen., 16th Jan., 1894; was ohmn. of the civ. serv. bd. of exams.



MATHERS, Frederick Francis, K.C., LL.B.—B. 1871; ed. schl. in Halifax, Nova Scotia, Dalhousie law schl. and Harvard law schl.; called to the bar, 1892; dep. prov. sec. and clk. of exec. coun., N.S., 1902; also registr. of joint companies, 1909.



MATHERS, Hon. Thos. Graham.—Ed. pub. and high schl., Lucknow and Edin., Ontario, and privately; editor, "Liberal," 1883; called to the bar, Mar., 1889; min. of just., Manitoba, 1896-1905; judge, ct. of King's Bench, 1905; ch. King's Bench, 1910.



MATHEWS, Charles Llandaff, G.P.O., S. Australia, Aug., 1873; cadet commr. of pub. wks., Apr., 1875; clk. dept., Sept., 1877; clk., atty.-gen. of, 1881; clk. local cts., Strathalbyn and W., Aug., 1883; clk., local cts., local ct. of ins. and licensing bench, Mount Gambier; reg. of births, deaths and marriages, 1888; also clk. representing offr., dist., Aug., 1896; returning offr. for the state, 1896.



MATHEWS, Henry Adolphus—Through govt. training instr., B. Guiana, certificated schl. instr.; head-master-in-aid schl., B. Guiana, 93 yrs.; educ. offr., 15th Nov., 1893; acted as 2nd ass't schools on various occasions, 1895-1903.



MATHEWS, Thomas Vincent, I.S.O.—Outdoor offr., receiver-gen. and treas. dist., mas., Oct., 1874; 3rd clk., Mar., 1875; ag. admstr., E. B. A. Taylor, from Sept., 1879; ag. collr. of customs, 1883; 2nd book-keeper, 1885; ag. rec-gen. on occasions, 1898-1904.



MATTEL, Charles, L.R.C.P. (Edin.), L.M., F.P.S.G., D.P.H.—Australian army medical corps, reserve of offr., N.S. Wales, 1891; ditto, W., 1897; govt. med. offr., quarantine med. mag., chrmn. of quarter sess., chrmn. of W. Australia, 1899; med. offr., Imperialists cont.; S. African war, 1901 (Cape Col. clasp); sec. for permits, E.S. Africa, 1902; med. offr. in charge of constructions, C.S.A.R., 1903; med. offr., Malta, 1907.



MATTHEWS, Sir John Brownlee Bach (1911).—B. 1864; barrister-at-law, Temple, 1890, N.E. circuit; ag. sol. Settlmts., 1902, to May, 1903; M. Settlmts., 1901 and 1904; pres. of charities commr., S. Settlmts., 1903; Bahamas, 1907; M.L.C., Bahamas, K.C., Bahamas, 1909, atty.-gen., S., Oct., 1909; ch. just., Bahamas, Jan., 1910.



MATTHEWS, Maynard Reginald—B. 1865; J.P. for Natal; jun. clk. telegraph, Durban, Natal, 1878; and postmr., Beaufort West, 1879; 3rd cl. clk. office, Durban, 1880; field cornet, Durban wreck commr.'s off., 1886; 2nd class clk., clk., mag.'s ct. and registrar, circuit ct., Durban, 1886-7; clk., mag.'s ct., registrar, sub-distributor of stamps, and dep. clk., Ladysmith, Dec., 1887; J.P., Klip River, has frequently acted as R.M., Klip River ag. mag., Verulam, Feb., 1896; J.P. for asst. mag., Durban, Nov., 1896; mag., June, 1896, to May, 1897; mag. and nat. for the div. of Newcastle, 23rd Sept., 1897; Dundee div., 9th Dec., 1901; received Sir Redvers Buller for services as an offr., during S. African war, 1899-1902; Dundee cott. hosp., bd., 12th Jan., 1902; chief leader, Dundee militia reserv., comm'd of Dundee under martial law, ag. ch. mag., Durban, 31st May to 11th...

MATTHEWS, WM. HENRY.—Inspector of mines, S. Aust., 1899; warden of mines, 1900.



MATURIN, K. W.—Asst dist. supt. of pol., E.A.P., Feb., 1909; staff offr. to inspr.-gen. of police, 1911.



MAUGER, HON. SAMUEL.—B. 1867; M.L.A. of Victoria, 1898-1901; elected to 1st house of rep., Commonwealth of Aust., 1901; re-elected, 1903 and 1906; min. without portfolio, 13th Oct., 1906; P.M.G., July, 1907.



MAURITIUS. BISHOP OF, RIGHT REV. FRANCIS AMBROSE GREGORY.—B. 1848; ed. Corpus Christi Coll., Oxford; 2nd cl. mod., 1869; B.A. (3rd cl. lit. hum.), 1871; M.A., 1883; D.D. (Hon.Causa), 1904; deacon, 1873, Win.; priest, 1874, Win.; formerly curate of Cheam, 1873-4; warden of St. Paul's (S.P.G.) Coll. and S.P.G. mission at Ambatoharanana, Madagascar, and chap. to Bp. of Madag, 1874-1900; chand. of cathedral of St. Laur., Antananarivo, 1889-1901; chap. of St. Jo., Mentone, 1901-4; Lord Bishop of Mauritius, 25th July, 1904.



MAVROGORDATO, ALEXANDER STEPHEN.—B. 1859; apptd. to med. dept., Nicosia, Cyprus, June, 1879; clk. to prin. forest offr., June, 1881; acted as forest offr., May, 1883, to Dec., 1884; was engaged on the locust destruction as paymr., 1883 to 1886; and as ast. to comsnr., Famagusta, 1889-92; examr. of acts, audit dept., May, 1886; transfd. to rec-gen.'s dept., Apr., 1891; ast. in survey and forest depts., Dec., 1892; pres. surv. delimitation comsnr.; supt. locust destruction operations, 1895-6; ast. in forest and agricultural depts., June, 1895; financial ast., P.W. Dept., October, 1896; finan. ast., recvr.-gen.'s dept., 1896; supt. of Cyprus census, 1901.



MAVROGORDATO, ARTHUR STEPHEN.—B. 1866; ed. at Oakham Schl., Rutland; clk., pol. headqrs., Cyprus, Nov., 1903; inspr. of mil. pol., Cyprus, May, 1906; in charge of pol. detachment, Kyrenia, 1907.



MAVROGORDATO, THEODORE ETIENNE.—Ed. at Berlin; clk. to comsnr., Famagusta, 1881; clk. and interp. to Nicosia detachment of pol., 1882; ast. inspr., pol., Limassol, 1883; inspr. pol., Kyrenia, Sept., 1884; joined metrpol. pol., London, for six months' course of instrm., 1894; in charge special pol. force, 1895; local comdt. of pol., ast. comsnr., gov. of prison and dep. cornr., 1895; ast. comsnr., Papho, May to Nov., 1897; ast. comsnr., Limassol, May to Dec., 1900; ast. comsnr. of pol. and J.F., Johannesburg, Dec., 1901; command. to draw up scheme for dest. of locusts in Transvaal, and had charge of locust dest. dept., in addition to other duties, Oct., 1902, to June, 1904; in charge of crimi. invstgn. dept. from June, 1903; deputy comsnr., Transvaal pol., 1st Aug., 1908.



MAXWELL, SIR FREDERIC MACKENZIE, Kt. Bach. (1911). Called to the bar, Linc.'s Inn, 1884; 1st cl. studentship (Equity), Linc.'s Inn, 1884; 1st cl. scholarship (Equity), Linc.'s Inn, 1884; M.A. (Oxon), 1891; 1st cl. jurisprudence, 1885; ag. atty.-gen., Br. Hond., Feb. to Dec., 1890, and May to July, 1896; atty.-gen., Br. Hond., July, 1896; K.C., Br. Hond., Apr., 1906; ag. chief just., Br. Hond., 21st Feb. to 29th Dec., 1899, Mar. to Oct., 1902, Apr. to Nov., 1904, and Apr., 1906, to Jan., 1907; chief just., Br. Hond., Jan., 1907; lieut.-commdg. mtd. section of Br.Hond.vol. force, Feb., 1905; attended schl. of musk. inst., at Bulford Camp, and recl. certif. of qualification to command a company of M.I., Sept., 1905; qualified at ashl. of musk., Hythe, Dec., 1905; capt., Br.Hond.vol. force, Jan., 1906; major, commdg. ditto, Apr., 1906; ret. from vols., Sept., 1908, with permission to retain rank and wear uniform of the force; chancellor of the diocese of Br. Hond., and Cent. America, 1896-1907.



MAXWELL, GERALD VERNER.—B. 1877; ed. Cheltenham and Camb. Univ.; cadet, Fiji, Apr., 1898; ag. reg.-genl., ag. reg. of titles and ag. dep. comsnr. of stamps, Dec., 1898, to June, 1899; ag. stip. mag., Macuata, Dec., 1900; ag. comsnr., Naitasiri, and stip. mag., Rewa, July, 1901; ag. ch. clk., C.S.O., Mar., 1902; ag. P. I., Nadroga, Feb., 1903; ast. nat. comsnr., Jan., 1904; nat. lands comsnr., 1906; stip. mag., etc., Lautoka, 1906; ag. comsnr., Lomaiviti, 1907.



MAXWELL, JOHN.—B. 1875; ed. at Dumfries and Glasgow; passed final exam. in law, Apr., 1899; ast. dist. comsnr., G. Coast, 21st Mar., 1902; travelling comsnr., 28th Jan., 1905; prov. comsnr., 18th May, 1907; has acted as solr.-gen. and atty.-gen. of the colony.



MAXWELL, THOMAS DOVETON.—B. 1873; ed. Tiverton, Blundell scholar, Balliol Coll., Oxford, 1892; B.A. (honours, jurisprudence), 1896; called to the bar (Gray's Inn), 1903; ast. dist. comsnr., So. Nigeria, 1902; ag. dist. comsnr., Degema, 1903; ditto, Calabar, Mar., 1904; polit. and transport offr., Ibibio patrol, Nov.-Dec., 1904 (W. African medal); ag. ast. sec., Calabar, Jan., 1906; ag. pol. mag., Calabar, Apr., 1906; comsnr. of lands, S. Nigeria, 9th Aug., 1906; crown solr., S. Nigeria, 1st Sept., 1908; pol. mag., June, 1910.



MAXWELL, WM. GEORGE.—B. 1871; ed. at Clifton Coll.; barrister-at-law, Inner Temp.; jun. offr., Perak, F.M.S., 15th Mar., 1891; ast. mag., Kinta, 25th Apr., 1892; ag. collr. and mag., Kuantan, Pahang, 16th Aug., 1895; ag. supt. of Ulu Pahang, 9th Aug., 1896; regist. of cts. Kinta, Perak, 1st Feb., 1899; ag. ast. sec. to govt., Perak, 6th Feb., 1900; ag. collr. of land rev., Larut, regis. of titles, Perak, North, and warden of mines, Perak, North, 8th Mar., 1901; ag. sen. mag., Selangor and Negri Sembilan, 1st Jan., 1903; ag. sen. mag., Perak, 1st Aug., 1903; ag. sec. to res., Perak, 6th Apr., 1904; ag. comsnr. of the ct. of requests, Singapore, 3rd Nov., 1904; dist. offr., Dindinga, 3rd Aug., 1905; dep. pub. prosecutor, Singapore, 1906; sol.-gen., S. Settnitsa, 22nd Aug., 1906; ag. atty.-gen., S. Settnitsa, Mar., 1908; adviser to govt. of Kedah, July, 1909; publications, "Terak Land Laws (past and present)," "The Laws of Perak, 1877-1903;" "The Laws of the S. Stiltnits, 1827-1907," "In Malay Forests."



MAXWELL-LYTE, LIEUT. JOHN.—B. 1875; F.R.G.S., F.R.H.S.; ed. at Radley and Merton Coll., Oxford; reserve of offr. (late Northumberland Fusiliers); ast. horticulturist, dept. of agric., Transvaal, 1st Feb., 1902, to May, 1907; ast. res., N. Nigeria, Nov., 1907; cantonment mag., Mar., 1911.



MAY, A. W. J.—B. 1862; entered col. office after exam., May, 1882; ast. clk., May, 1892; ast. to supervisor of copying, Mar., 1900; supervisor of copying, 1st Oct., 1911.



MAY, BARRY.—Ck. to res. mag., Vryburg, Brit. Bech., 1st June, 1888; ck. to res. mag., Kuruman, 1889; ck. to civ. comsnr., Vryburg, 1890; acctnt. to recvr.-gen., 1894; acctnt. to res. comsnr., Bech. Prot., 1895, govt. sec., 1902; ag. res. comsnr., Nov., 1908, to May, 1909 and from Apl. to Oct., 1911.



MAY, CECIL.—B. 1868; clerical ast., treasy., B. Guiana; 4th cl. clk., Apr., 1889; 3rd cl. ditto, June, 1892; 2nd cl. ditto, 6th Mar., 1899; ag. 1st cl. clk., cent. bd. of health, Oct., Dec., 1900; 1st cl. clk., audit dept., 1st Jan., 1901; pay and

quartermaster, B.G. pol., 15th Apr., 1901; 2nd lieut., B.G. militia, 29th Dec., 1896; 1st lieut., 18th Nov., 1897; capt., 18th Mar., 1898; ag. adjutant, 8th May to 22nd Aug., 1900; seconded for service with B.G. pol., 7th Aug., 1901; rejoined B.G.M., 24th Feb., 1902; major, 27th Feb., 1902; ag. comdt., 26th Aug. to 23rd Oct., 1904.



MAY, CHAS. GALL.—B. 1870; apptd. asst. supt. of works, Straits Settlements, May, 1899; ag. supt. of works and surveys, Malacca, June, 1899, to Sept., 1901, and Oct., 1902, to Apr., 1903; supt. of works and surveys, Sing., July, 1903; ag. dep. col. engr. and survr.-gen., Penang, Nov., 1904, to Feb., 1905; ag. supt., wks. and survey, Malacca, May to Dec., 1906; ag. dep. col. engr. and survr.-gen., Penang, Jan., 1907 to Apr., 1908, and from July, 1908; confirmed, Dec., 1909.



MAY, SIR FRANCIS H., K.C.M.G.(1909), C.M.G. (1855).—B. 1860; ed. at Harrow and Trin. Coll., Dub.; 1st honour-man and prizeman in classics and modern languages; apptd., after compet. exam., to a Hong Kong cadetship, 1881; ag. asst. regir.-gen., Apr., 1886; ag. asst. col. sec., Jan., 1887; sec. to bd. of examrs., Jan., 1889; asst. col. sec., Jan., 1891; priv. sec. to Gov. Sir W. Des Voeux, to Admstr. Sir F. Fleming, and Maj.-Gen. Barker, Apr., 1889, to Dec., 1891; ag. col. treas., Apr. to Oct., 1892; mem. legis. coun., May, 1895; capt. supt. of pol. and fire brigade, 1893, and of Victoria gaol, 1897; ag. col. sec., Feb. to Sept., 1900; col. sec., 1902; admtd. the govt., Nov., 1903, to July, 1904, 15th Dec., 1906, to 24th Jan., 1907; 20th Apr. to 28th July, 1907; and from 30th Apr. to end of Oct., 1910; gov., Fiji, and high commr. for Western Pacific, 9th Jan., 1911; assumed govt., 21st Feb., 1911.



MAY, GEORGE HERBERT.—B. 1873; ag. apptmt. in regir.'s off., Br. Guiana, Nov., 1889; admtr.-gen.'s off., on staff, June, 1892; pol. dept., Apr., 1893; 2nd lieut., Br. Guiana militia, Sept., 1894, and obtained certif. for drill and musketry from schls. of instruc., Chelsea Bks., Lon. and Hythe; ret. from mil. as lieut., and apptd. sub-inspr. of Br. Guiana pol., May, 1897; adjt. and musketry instr. of local forces, Fiji, with rank of capt., Oct., 1898; supt. of pol., ag. sheriff, 12th Dec., 1900; dep. comdt., armed constab., 24th Apr., 1901, also commanded volunteers; comdt., armed constab., supt. of pol., ag. sheriff, 24th June, 1902; A.D.C. to O.A.G., Fiji, July, 1901, to Sept., 1902; A.D.C. to Sir Henry M. Jackson, K.C.M.G., gov. of Fiji, 4th Nov., 1902; inspr. of constab., Trinidad, 1905.



MAY, HENRY FREDERICK PORTER.—Ex-tracy., treasy., B. Guiana, 1877; clk., savings bank, 1880; 3rd clk., ditto, 1881; 2nd clk., ditto, 1884; ag. acctnt., savings bank, 1887; in charge of sub-treasy., Suddie, 1888; 2nd clc. clk., 1889; 1st clc. clk., 1893; acctnt., savings bank, 1893; cashier, treasy., 1895; in charge of Belfield sub-treasy.; ag. dep. rec-gen., 1903; hon. sec. of shipping charges comm., 1904; in charge of savings bank, Mar., 1906; clk. to widows' and orphans' fund; pub. offrs' insurance fund, May, 1906; ag. asst. rec-gen., 1st July, 1906; interprets Hindustani for treasy. and savings bank.



MAYSTON, GEORGE.—Collr. of cust., Natal, 29th Jan., 1898; controller of excise, on amalgamation of the two depts., 1st Feb., 1903.



MAZÈRE, LOUIS JOSEPH.—Clk., survr.-genl.'s dept., Mauritius, 4th Jan., 1873; pay clk., ditto, 26th Mar., 1884; ch. clk. and acctnt., 3rd Dec., 1902.



MBA, ISAAC OKETSHUKU.—B. 1860; Polit. agt. for Okrika in Bonny, New Calabar dist., Oil Rivers Prot., 11th Feb., 1892; storekeeper, int. and postmr. at Bonny; customs preven. at Idu; treasy. clk. and court interpr. Degama; transf. to treasy. dept., Old 7th Mar., 1894; clk., audit off., Nig. Prot., 8th Dec., 1894; ch. clk. jud. dept., S. Nigeria, 20th Sept., 1900; temp. attached to secretariat, 17th Jan., 1902; audit off., 1st Apr., 1902; title altered to clk., 1903; ast. ch. clk., P.W.D., War Prov., 1st June, 1907.



MEADE, A. R.—B. 1887; ed. at St. Nevis gram. sch.; jun. ast. mast. St. Nevis gram. sch., Jan. to Apr., 1907; London Univ., 1908; copyist, treasy. dep. Kitts, June, 1907; 3rd treasy. clk., 16th Nov., 1907; ag. 1st treasy. clk., 1st to Jan., 1910; ag. 2nd treasy. clk., Mar., 1910; 2nd treasy. clk., July, 1910.



MEADEN, C. W.—14th Hussars and goon Guards, 1870-6; convict service, 1877; supt. of Chaguanas convict depot, 1885; J.P. for co. Caroni, 1887; ast. sup., 1890; mem. cent. agricult. bd.; carried out agricul. experiments by prison labour, twice ag. supt. of govt. farm and pastures, cent. agricult. bd.; warden of Chaguanas adjt., Trinidad Light Horse, Dec., 1894; stock farm, and supt. of pastures, Mar., 1895; adjt., Trinidad Light Horse, Dec., 1894.



MEIRING, E. J.—Apptd. acctnt., nat. dept., O.R.C., 1st July, 1902; clk. treasy., Nov., 1903.



MELBOURNE, ARCHBISHOP OF, HENRY LOWTHER CLARKER, D.D.; vicar, Hull, 1876-1883; St. Martin, York, Dewsbury, Yorks, 1890-1901; Huddersfield, 1902; hon. canon of Wakefield, episcopal canon of St. George's, Jerusalem, of Melbourne, 1902-1905; archbishop of and Metropolitan of Victoria from 1905.



MELBOURNE, CHARLES ALEX. In privately and Trin. Hall, Camb.; called Inner Temple, Nov., 1891; admitted in Brisbane, Queensland, Nov., 1892; Hong Kong, Nov., 1895; apptd. 1st clk. treasy., Hong Kong, Sept., 1900; ag. ast. supt., Victoria gaol, 1903 and ast. land offr., 1905; commr. for oath, 1905; ag. 2nd pol. mag., Oct., 1905 to 1907; ag. dep. regir. and appraiser, 14th Aug., 1907; ag. 2nd pol. mag., Oct. to Dec., 1907; ag. ast. supt., Vict., 15th Jan., 1908, to 13th Jan., 1909; regir. and appraiser, 8th Apr., 1909; Mar., 1909, and from 30th June, 1909; appraiser, 21st Sept., 1909.



MELVILLE, SIR GEORGE, K.C.M.G. C.M.G. (1894).—B. 1842; late lient. K. militia; ed. Edinburgh Acad.; clk. in dept., inland rev., after compet. exam., afterwards in the legacy and succ. dept.; ch. clk., treasy., S. Leone, acted as col. treas., Dec., 1874, to 1875, during which period also acted as col. to Sept., 1875; acted also as collr. of col. survr., and held comm. as de J.P.; 1st clk., govt. sec.'s office, 1877; ast. govt. sec., 1879; acted as 1881, 1882, 1887, and 1888, and also as col. sec. audr. gen., and regir.-gen., 1889; admstr. of govt., 1890 and 1891; of govt. of Falklands, 1893; col. sec. 1894; adminstr. govt., 1894 and 1895.

Leewards, 1895; admnstd. govt. under dormant commission, 1895, 1896, 1897, 1898, 1900; admnstr. and col. sec., Saint Lucia, Sept., 1902; ret., 1905.



MELVILLE, THOMAS ALEXANDER.—B. 1880; apptd. after open compet. exam. for home civ. ser., to G.P.O., Dec., 1895, and served in different depts.; supt. of mails, G.P.O., Singapore, Oct., 1905.



MENENDEZ, SIR M. RAYMOND, KT. BACH. (1904).—Ed. Emman. Coll., Camb.; LL.B., Camb., 1890; barrister-at-law, Inner Tem.; ag. stip. and circuit mag., etc., and judge of com. pleas, Bahamas, 1892-4; dist. comanr., Lagos, Aug., 1894; ag. Queen's advocate, Lagos, Dec., 1896, to Aug., 1897; ch. judicial offr., Niger Coast Protectorate, Aug., 1897; puisne judge, S. Nigeria, 1st Jan., 1899; ag. ch. just. on several occasions; recd. thanks of gov., for spec. services in reorganising native courts of prot., Jan., 1903; ch. just., N. Nigeria, 1905.



MENSAH, ALFRED, I.S.O. (1907).—Extra clk., cust. and treasy. depts., G. Coast, 18th May, 1874; 3rd clk., 1st Dec., 1874; 2nd clk., 1st July, 1876; clk. and warehouse keeper, 13th Mar., 1878; sub-collr. of cust., Winnebah, 15th Oct., 1880; Cape Coast, 1st May, 1882; Winnebah, 16th Nov., 1882; transf'd to Appam as sen. sub-clrk. and examg. offr. for Winnebah dist., 12th Oct., 1883; Cape Coast, 22nd Feb., 1886; offr.-in-charge of treasy., Cape Coast, 5th May to 11th June, 1904, and 11th July, 1904, to 15th Jan., 1906; sub-asst. treas., G. Coast, 16th Jan., 1906; transf'd to Kumase, 1907 and 1908.



MERCER, WILLIAM HRPWORTH, C.M.G. (1902).—B. 1855; open scholar and Hody exhibtr., Wadham Coll., Oxford; 2nd cl. classical mods.; 2nd cl. final classical schl.; 2nd cl. clk. in the C.O. after open compet., 30th June, 1879; awarded 1st prize in common law offered by council of legal education, 1883; and a pupil scholarship of 100 guineas, in real property law, by the soc. of the Inner Temple, 1885; called to the bar, 1886; sec. to the Earl of Jersey, when ag. as Br. delegate at col. confece., Ottawa, 1894; on special mission to Hawaii with Mr. (now Sir) Sandford Fleming, Sept. to Nov., 1894, negotiating for lease of landing station of proposed Pacific cable; asst. priv. sec. to Lord Ripon, Apr., 1895; to Mr. Chamberlain, June, 1895; 1st class clk., May, 1896; sec. to Pacific cable comttee., 1896; prin. clk., Oct., 1898; sec. to Pacific cable comttee., 1899; crown agt. for the cols., June, 1900; mem. of Pacific cable bd., 1901; dep. chmn. of ditto, 1907; apptd. dir. of scholars sent to England from certain crown cols., 1902; joint editor of C.O. List since 1898.



MERCIER, GUY HENRY VIFNOT.—2nd clk., registr. and provost-marshal's office, Antigua, 1895; 4th clk., col. sec.'s office, 1897; clk. to registr. and provost-marshal, Nevis, 1898; dep. coroner, Nevis, 1901; rev. offr., Nevis, 1901; clk., British vice-consulate, Chinde, Apr., 1905.



MEREDITH, RICHARD MARTIN.—B. 1847; judge of high ct., Ontario, chancery div., 1890; ct. of appeal, 1905.



MEREDITH, HON. SIR WM. RALPH, KT. BACH. (1896).—B. 1840; called to the bar, 1861; Q.C. (Ontario), 1875; (Dominion), 1880; bencher, law society of Upper Canada for many years; represented London in legis. assem., 1872 to 1894; leader of opposition, 1879 to 1894; ch. just. of the common pleas, Ontario, 1894; chancellor of Univ. of Toronto.



MEREWETHER, SIR EDWARD MARSH, K.C.V.O. (1907); C.V.O. (1903); C.M.G. (1902).—B. 1858; ed. Harrow; cadet, S.S., Oct., 1880; passed final exam. in Malay, May, 1882; ag. collr. of land rev., Singapore, and J.P., S.S., May, 1882; confirmed, Jan., 1883; Malay interp. with H.M.S. "Pegasus" to Tenom in connection with the "Niseru" case, June, 1884; ag. mag. and offr. in charge treasy., Malacca, 1886; dist. offr., Dindings, 1886; ag. 2nd mag., Penang, 1888; ag. 1st mag., Penang, 1888; 2nd asst. col. sec., June, 1890; supt. of census, 1891; ag. asst. col. sec., Aug., 1891; collr. of land rev., and in charge of treasy., Malacca, July, 1892; ag. res. coun., Malacca, Sept. to Dec., 1893; inspr. of prisons, S.S., 1893; asst. col. sec. and clk. of couns., May, 1897; ag. res. coun., Malacca, May, 1897, to June, 1898, and Sept., 1900; ag. col. treas., S.S., Jan., 1900; ag. res. coun., Malacca, Sept., 1901; ag. Br. res. Sélângor, Oct., 1901; confirmed, Dec., 1901; lieut.-gov. and ch. sec. to govt., Malta, Aug., 1902; gov., Sierra Leone, 24th Nov., 1910; assumed govt., 29th April, 1911.



MERRICK, CAPT. F. S.—Joined 3rd Batt. Innis, Fus., 1906; Natal police, 1897-1902; lieut., 29th I.Y., Mch., 1902; served in S. African war (2 medals); dist. supt. of pol., N. Nigeria, May, 1903; ag. asst. comanr. of pol., July-Aug., 1905; ag. staff offr., Aug.-Dec., 1905; 1st cls. dist. supt. of pol., Apl., 1908; deputy I.G. of pol., Dec., 1910; ag. I.G., Apl.-Oct., 1911.



MERRIMAN, THE RIGHT HON. JOHN XAVIER, P.C. (1909).—Comanr. of pub. wks. and crown lands, C. of Good Hope, 1875-8; has for several years represented the electoral div. of Dordrecht in the Cape legis. assem.; again comanr. of crown lands and pub. wks., 1881 to 1884; treas.-gen., 1890-3; mem. of Jameson raid comttee., 1896; treas.-gen. in the Schreiner ministry, 1898 to 1900; mem. for Victoria West, since 1904; treas. and prime min., 1908; mem. of Impl. Conf. on naval and mil. defence, 1909; mem. of S. African national convention and of delegation to England in connection with S. Africa Bill, 1909.



MERRY, GEORGE ALEXANDER.—Paymaster, Bechuanaland Prot. police, 1900; ag. mag. N'Gami, 1904-6; inspr., Bechuanaland Prot. police, 1907; is also asst. res. mag., Serowe.



MESSER, CHAS. MCILVAINE.—B. 1874; ed. Merchant Taylors' schl., and Emmanuel Coll., Camb.; exhibitioner, 1892; scholar, 1893; 16th wrangler math. tripos, 1896; B.A., 1896; M.A., 1905; cadet, Hong Kong, 1897; ag. land offr., New Territory, 1899; J.P., 1900; ag. col. treas., 1901; passed cadet, 1902; ag. registr.-gen., 1902; asst. land offr., N.T., 1903; and mem. of land ct., 1903-4; ag. col. treas., 1907; ag. postmr.-gen., 1907; head of sanitary dept. and pres. of sanitary bd., 1908; postmr.-gen., 1908; ag. col. treas., 1910, to Feb., 1911.



METHUEN, FIELD-MARSHAL THE RIGHT HON. BARON, G.C.B., G.C.V.O., C.M.G. (1866).—B. 1845; entered the Army, 1864; served in Ashanti expedn., 1873-74; mil. attache at Berlin, 1878-81; served with expdny. force in Egypt, 1882; rendered special services in Bechuanaland expedn., 1884-85; served on the staff in S. Africa, 1888-90; lieut.-gen. comldg. a div., S. Africa, 1899-1902; mem. of Royal Patriotic Fund Corporation, 1905-7; G.O.C., S. Africa, 1908; gov. of Natal, 1910.



METZGEN, CARL ALEXANDER.—B. 1860; temporary clk., surry.-gen.'s office, Br. Honduras, 1886; clk. to att.-gen., 1887; ag. clk. to clk. of ct., Sept. to Nov., 1887; rev. offr., 1888; 3rd clk., treasy., customs, and post office, 1889; 2nd clk., treasy., etc., Feb., 1891; capt., Belize fire brigade, June, 1889, to Feb.,

1891; clk. to auditor, Dec., 1891; 4th clk., treasy., Sept., 1892; ag. 3rd clk., Nov., 1893; audit examnr., col. sec. dept., Feb., 1894; ch. clk., treasy. and customs dept., May, 1897; ag. registr.-gen., and ag. auditor, 30th May, 1905, to 6th Jan., 1906; auditor, 11th Oct., 1905.



METZGER, SAMUEL AIRIN.—B. 1858; J.P., S. Leone, 1897; apptd., after compet. exam., asst. mast., govt. model schl., S. Leone, 1875; resigned and joined merc. serv.; extra offr., H.M. customs, July, 1884; extra clk. gov.'s office, June, 1885; with Sir S. Rowe to Yonni expedn., 1885; clk. sup. ct. and sheriff's offr., 1886; dep. and ag. mast. of sup. ct. since 1892; licensed solr., sup. ct., 1895; ag. registr.-gen., 1895-6; ag. curator of intes. estates, 1906-8; under-sheriff, 1897; ag. dist. comsrr., Waterloo, 1899; dep. coroner, Freetown, 1901; sen. clk., sup. ct., 1905; ag. mast. and registr., sup. ct., S. Leone, 1900 to 1907.



MEWS, ARTHUR.—Asst., gov. telegraphs, Newfndld., 1893; clk. to final. sec., 1894; final. clk., col. sec.'s office, 1895; dep. col. sec., 1898; reger. of joint stock companies, 1899.



MICALLF, SIR RICHARD, K.C.M.G. (1906), C.M.G. (1902).—B. 1846; entd. the Malta serv., Nov., 1863; clk. in office of charitable institutions, Dec., 1864; clk., sanitary office and sec. to the med. bd., Jan., 1881; dep. recr.-gen., dep. comptroller of charitable institns., and dep. comsrr., Monte di Pietà, Gozo, Apr., 1884; asst. sec. to govt. for Gozo, Sept., 1885; comptroller of charitable institns., with seat in coun. of govt., Nov., 1886, and a seat in the exec. coun., Mar., 1888.



MICHELL, ROLAND LYONS NOSWORTHY, C.M.G. (1911).—Ed. Chr. Ch., Oxford (open studentship, 1865); tutor to Prince Ibrahim Pasha, son of the Khedive of Egypt, 1870; received decoration of the Osmanieh (4th class) from the Khedive Ismail, 1878; and of the Medjidieh from the late Khedive Tewfik, 1879; chief of statistical dept., cadastral survey, Egypt, 1879; comsrr., Limasol, Cyprus, Aug., 1879; also dep. comsrr., high court, and pol. mag.; is sheriff of dist.



MICHELL, WALTER CECIL.—Ed. Godolphin schl. and Merton Coll., Oxon.; B.A., 1887; cadet, S. Stlttns., Oct., 1887; ag. collr. and mag., Ulu Pulang, 1888; passed Malay final, Sept., 1889; dist. offr., Balik Pulau, Oct., 1891; ag. dist. offr., Dindings, June, 1895; also dep. registr., sup. ct., Penang, Oct., 1896; 2nd mag., Singapore, May, 1897; ag. 2nd asst. col. sec., S.S., Aug., 1897; also collr. of ld. rev., Singapore, Sept., 1897; ag. sen. dist. offr., P.W., Dec., 1898, to Dec., 1899; official assignee, S.S., Dec., 1901; ag. comsrr., et al. requests, Singapore, Jan., 1902; ag. 1st mag., Sing., Aug., 1903; comsrr., et al. requests, Sing., Sept., 1903, but continued to act as 1st mag.; 1st mag., Penang, Feb., 1907, but continued to act at Singapore; ag. aud.-gen., Dec., 1907; ag. dist. judge and 1st mag., Sing., Feb., 1910; ag. treasr., S.S., Apr., 1910.



MIDDLETON, JOHN PAGE, B.A.—Ed. Uppingham and Trin. Hall, Camb.; called to the bar, Mid. Tem., June 1874, Norfolk and S.E. circuits; ag. Queen's advoc., G. Coast, Jan., 1882; pres. of dist. ct., Limasol, Cyprus, Sept., 1882; puisne judge, sup. ct., 1892; ag. ch. just., June and July, 1893; ag. judge of consular ct., Constantinople, May to July, 1894; ag. ch. just., May to Oct., 1895; received thanks of S. of S. Foreign Affairs in connection with Ottoman Dominions (Courts) O. in C., 1895; puisne judge, Ceylon, 1902.



MIDDLETON, HON. WM. EDWARD.—B. 1860; ed. Toronto Coll. Inst. and Toronto Univ.; admitted solr., 1884; called to the bar, 1885; K.C., 1908; judge of high ct., Ontario, 1910.



MIGEOD, GEORGE EDWARD HENRY.—Clk. pav. and acct. dept., W.A.F.F., Niger Territory, 1889; ch. clk. and cashier, treasy., Jan., 1901; subsequently asst. treasurer, N. Nigeria; col. of customs, N. Nigeria, 1st Apr., 1903.



MILLAR, HON. JOHN ANDREW.—Comsrr. of trade and customs, min. of labour, and min. of charge of marine dept., New Zealand.



MILLARD, ALFRED SUTTON.—B.Sc., M.B., Ch.B. (Edin.); med. offr., S. Settmts., May, 1907.



MILLENN, HON. EDWARD DAVIS.—B. 1861; Senator for N.S. Wales, in Commonwealth parl.; leader of the opposition, 1907; vice-pres. of exec. coun., C. of A., June, 1909.



MILLER, F. A.—Ch. clk. crown law office, S. Leone, 1891; dep. master, sup. ct., Sept., to Oct., 1895; 1st clk. col. secretariat, July, 1896; ch. clk. col. secretariat, Apr., 1879; gov.'s clk. and clk. of legis. coun., 1898; J.P. for colony.



MILLER, WM. AKERMAN.—B. 1869; Assoc. M.I.C.E.; ed. King Henry VIII.'s school, Coventry, and Mason's Coll., B'ham.; pupil and asst. to E. Pritchard, M.I.C.E., B'ham., 1887-91; 2nd cls. supt., P.W.D., Jamaica, 1891; 1st cls. ditto, 1896; col. engrnr. and survr.-gen., Dominica, 1902; chrmn., telephone bd., Roa., 1902; mem. of Roseau town bd., 1902; superintendant of crown lands, 1903; on spec. serv. in Antigua, Aug., 1903; received thanks of S. of S. for services in connection with Impl. grnt., Dominica, Sept., 1903; offl. M.L.C., May, 1904; recev. of crown rev., 1905; pres., Dominica defence reserve, 1905; comsrr., ordnance property, Feb., 1906.



MILLIGAN, HERBERT WARD.—B. 1884; ed. Bromsgrove schl. and Worcester Coll., Oxford (B.A.); cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Nov., 1907; asst. collr. of cust. and landing surv., Trincomalee, Nov., 1908; off. asst. to govt. agt., L. prov., Dec., 1909.



MILLINGTON, EDWARD TURNER.—B. 1881; ed. Victoria Univ., Manchester (B.A.); cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Nov., 1904; extra offr. asst. to govt. agt., N. Prov. and asst. collr. of cust., Jaffna, Jan., 1906; pol. mag., Avisawella, Apr., 1906; off. asst. to govt. agt., N.W. Prov., Nov., 1906; Cent. Prov., Aug., 1908; ag. dist. judge, etc., Nuwara Eliya-Hatton, Jan., 1910.



MILLINGTON, WM. MILNES, B.A. (Oxon.).—Cadet, S. Stlttns., Jan., 1907; ag. dist. offr., Alor Gajah, Nov., 1908; ag. dist. offr., Jan., May, 1910.



MILLS, JAMES, B.A., M.A., LL.D.—B. 1849; headmaster, Stanstead Academy, Quebec, Canada, 1868; classical mast., Cobourg Coll., Inst. Ontario, 1869-73; headmaster, Brantford Coll. Inst., 1873-79; pres., Ontario Agric. Coll., Guelph, 1879-1904; mem. of the rlyw. comsrr., 1904.



MILLS, SIR RICHARD, K.C.B. (1901), C.B. (1893); V.D.—B. 1830; acctnt. to the treasy., 1859-72; treasy. offr. of accs., 1872-88; asst. comptroller and auditor, Sept., 1888; comptroller and auditor-gen., Apr., 1896, to 1900; late lieut.-col. comdg. (hon. col.) 12th Middlesex (Civ. Ser.) R.V.; was hon. auditor of certain crown cols. ag. on behalf of the S. of S. forCols.; retired 1900.



MILNE, ARTHUR DAWSON.—Ed. Gymnasium, Aberdeen; M.B., C.M., Aberdeen Univ., 1902; med. offr., Uganda Prot., 6th Jan., 1898; sen. med. offr., 1900; asst. prin. med. offr., 1st Apr.,

MILNER, THE RT. HON. VISCOUNT (1902), 1st Baron (U.K., creat. 1901), P.C., G.C.B. (1901), Scholar Balliol; 1st class lit. hum., 1876; Hertford scholar, 1874; Craven scholar, 1877; Eldon scholar, 1878; Derby scholar, 1878; Fellow of New Coll.; called to the bar, Inner Temp., 1881; priv. sec. to Rt. Hon. G. J. Goschen, Chanc. of Excheq., 1887-9; under-secr. of finance in Egypt, 1889-92; chmn. bd. inland rev., 1892; author of "England in Egypt"; gov. Cape (1897-1901) and High Comsnr. S. Africa, 1907; administrator of Transvaal and Orange River Colony, as well as High Comsnr. S. Africa, 1901-1905.



MILNE, P.A. — B. 1882; apptd., after compet. exam., clk. of the 2nd div. of the civil ser., and assigned to the C.O., July, 1900.



MILTHORP, BERNARD THOMAS. — Asst. collr., B.C.A. Prot., Dec., 1896; Fort Johnston, Apr. to Nov., 1897; Blantyre, Dec., 1897, to Jan., 1899; Chiromo, Aug., 1899, to Jan., 1900; Mlanje, Jan., 1900, to Apr., 1901; Blantyre, Apr., 1901, to Apr., 1902; Liwonde and Fort Hill (Nyasa-Tanganyika Plateau), 1903; Chikwawa, Sept., 1903, to Dec., 1904; Chikwawa, Aug., 1905, to Mar., 1908; Chikwawa and Neno (West Shire Dist.), Dec., 1908; 2nd cls. res., Feb., 1902.



MILTON, Sir W. H., K.C.M.G. (1903), K.C.V.O. (1910), C.M.G. (1901). — B. 1834; clk., col. sec.'s office, Cape, Apr., 1878; 3rd class clk., 1st Jan., 1879; 2nd class clk., Jan., 1881; 1st class clk., Apr., 1883; sec. to the tender bd., 1881; clk. to exec. coun., 1885; ch. clk. and acctnt., col. sec.'s office, 1891; sec. to prime min., Mar., 1894; detached for serv. in Rhodesia as ch. sec. and sec. for native aff., Aug., 1896; transfd. to Rhod. serv., Oct., 1897; ag. admnr. Rhod., July, 1897, to Nov., 1898; apptd. admnr. Mashonaland and senr. admnr. S. Rhodesia, Dec., 1898; admnr., S. Rhodesia, 26th Dec., 1902.



MINTO, THE RIGHT HON. THE EARL OF (4th Earl, cr. 1813), VISCOUNT MELGUNO (U.K.), BARON OF MINTO (1797, Grt. Brit.), Bart. (1710, Scot.), P.C. (1902), G.C.M.G. (1898), G.C.S.I., G.C.I.E. (1911), GILBERT JOHN ELLIOT. — B. 1845; succeeded 1891; ed. at Eton and at Trin. Coll., Camb.; B.A. 1856; ensign and lieut. Scots Guards, 1867-70, is col. comdg. S. Scotland inftry. vol. brig. (V.D.), and a D.L. for cos. of Roxburgh and Selkirk, served in Kurram Valley, Afghan campaign, 1879 (medal); accompanied Sir Freckl. (now Lord) Roberts to S. Africa as priv. sec., 1881; served in mound. inftry. in Egyptian campaign, 1882 (wounded Aug. 24th); afterwards commanded mntd. inftry. in Cairo (mentioned in despatches, medal and 4th class Medjidie); was sec. and mil. sec. to Marquis of Lansdowne, gov. gen. of Canada, 1883-6; served as ch. of staff in N.W. rebellion, Canada, 1885 (mentioned in despatches and medal); gov.-gen. of Canada, 1898-1904; viceroy of India, 1905.



MITCHELL, GEORGE PHILIPONE STEPHEN. — B. 1869; asst. clk., educ. dept., Trinidad, Aug., 1880; 2nd clk. to asst. dir. of pub. wks., Feb., 1884; clk., N. div. of the P.W.D., May, 1886; clk. to warden of St. Ann's and Diego Martin Ward Unions, July, 1893; bandmr. Trinidad Field Artill. Vol. band, June, 1896, to 1899.



MITCHELL, H. H. — Entd. col. sec.'s office, Grenada, 1878; 2nd clk., treasy., 1879; ag. rev. offrr., 1880; audit clk., St. Lucia, Apr., 1881; ag. ch. clk., treasy., 1881-2; 2nd clk. and checking offrr. of invoices, 1882; ag. audrr., 1882, and again during 1883-4; ch. clk., treasy., 1887; ag. ch. clk., col. sec.'s off., and dist. regist. of births and deaths, St. George's, Grenada, 1889; ag. acctnt., treasy., Grenada, 1890; regis. offrr., 1st dist., St. Lucia, under "Minor Products Protection Ordinance," 1899; mem. of quarantine authority, St. Lucia, 1900 to 1903; ag. regist. of royal court and of deeds and mortgages, sheriff, regist.-gen. of births and deaths and admstr.-gen. of vacant succession, June to Sept., 1903; ag. col. treas., compt. of cust., regist. of shipping and man. of savings bank, St. Lucia, on several occasions from 1900-6; ex-officio mem. of exec. and legis. couns.



MITCHELL, O. — Customs asst., E.A.P., 9th Jan., 1905; asst. compt. of cust., G. Coast, 1910.



MITCHELL, SAMUEL JAMES. — M.H.A., S. Aust., 1901; attorney-gen., 5th June to 22nd Dec., 1909; govt. res. and judge of Northern Territory, 1st Apr., 1910; transf. to service of C. of A., 1911; ag. admnr. N. Territories, 1911.



MITCHELL, WM. HEISBERT, M.A. (1894), B.A. (1890). — Ed. at Bristol Gram. Schol. and Sydney Sussex Coll., Camb.; headmnr., gram. and agric. schls., St. Kitts, 1901; apptnt. confirmed, 1904.



MITCHELL, SIR WM. WILSON, KT. BACH. (1900), C.M.G. (1895). — B. 1840; apptd. M.L.C., Ceylon, 1875; unoffl. M.L.C., 1881-1900; represtd. Ceylon at Paris Exhibn., 1900.



MOFFAT, JOHN BRUCE. — B. 1863; priv. sec. to col. sec., Cape, 1890; prin. clk. col. sec.'s off., 1894; ag. ch. clk., 1895, and again 1896; ch. clk., native affairs off., and accounting offrr., prime minister's dept., Oct., 1897; civ. comsnr. and res. mag., Mafeking, Nov., 1900; comsnr. of taxes, July, 1904; and civil comsnr., Cape, Sept., 1908.



MOFFAT, REV. JOHN SMITH, C.M.G. (1890). — B. 1835; native comsnr. N. W. Border, Transvaal, 1880-1; R.M., Basutoland, Mar., 1882, to Apr., 1884; R.M., Taungs, Br. Bechuana land, Oct., 1885; asst. comsnr. for the protectorate, 1867.



MOFFAT, ROBERT UNWIN, C.M.G. (1899). — B. 1866; med. offrr., Uganda Prot., 19th Dec., 1892; prin. med. offrr., 3rd Jan., 1898; ditto, East Africa and Uganda Prots., 1st Apr., 1903; sen. med. offrr., Uganda Prot., 21st Feb., 1904; ret., 1906.



MOGGIDGE, LEWIS TRAHERNE. — B. 1874; ed. at Clifton Coll. and King's Coll., Camb.; apptd. ch. constable, B.C.A. Prot., Apr., 1899; asst. postmr.-gen., Zomba, Oct., 1899; asst. collr., 1900; collr. and dist. mag., Blantyre, Mar., 1901, to 1903; 2nd cls. dist. res., Apr., 1906; dist. res. and mag., Chiromo, 1906 and 1907.



MOIR, CHAS. EDWARD. — Ag. 4th landing waiter, customs, St. Kitts, July, 1873, to Jan., 1875; 3rd landing waiter, May, 1875; 2nd ditto, Dec., 1878; rev. offrr. and quarantine offrr., Aug., 1883; rev. offrr. and harbour., St. Kitts, 1906.



MOIR, S. E. — Clk., P.O., St. Kitts, Mar., 1905; rev. offrr., Nevis, Apr., 1906.



MOLONEY, SIR C. ALFRED, C.M.G. (1882), K.C.M.G. (1890). — B.1848; entered Mil. Coll., Sandhurst, 1866; ensign, Feb., 1867; lieut., Dec., 1868; capt., Nov., 1874; acted as civil comdt. of the Quiah dist. S. Leone, 1867-8; A.D.C. to Sir James Walker, C.B., gov., Bahamas, Feb., 1871; priv. sec. to Capt. G. C. Strahan, admnr. Bahamas, Apr., 1871, to May, 1873; priv. sec. and A.D.C. to Gov. Hennessy, June to Nov., 1873, when he embarked for service on the G. Coast; served in the Ashantee

campaign, 1873-4 (medal); priv. sec. and A.D.C. to Gov. Strahan, July, 1874; ag. auditor, G.C. Col., Feb., 1875; ag. inspr.-gen. of constab., 1875; asst. col. sec., 1877; col. sec., 1879; admnstr. gov't of Lagos, 1878 to 1880, and again in 1881; admnstr. of the gov't of the col., 1882; resumed the admnstr. of Lagos, 1882-3; admnstr. of the Gambia, 1884; admnstr. of Lagos, 1885; gov', 1887; gov', Br. Honduras, 1891; gov' of Windward, 1897; gov' Trinidad and Tobago, 1900-1904; ret., 1904; author of "Forestry of West Africa."



MOLTEANO, HON. SIR JAMES TENNANT, K.T. BACH, (1911), B.A., LL.B., M.L.A.—B. 1865; ed. at Diocesan Coll., Rondebosch, and Trin. Coll., Camb.; called to the bar, Inner Temple; entd. Cape parlmt., 1890; speaker of Cape H. of A.; speaker of H. of A., Union of South Africa, 1910.



MOPPLE, FRANCOIS JOSEPH ROBERT.—M.B., C.M., D.P.H. (Edin.)—health offr., Mauritius, 7th Sept., 1898; ag. asst. sanitary warden, 4th Apr., 1900; 1st san. warden, 11th Apr., 1904; ag. asst. dir. and chief sanitary offr., in 1908 and 1909.



MONCKTON, NOEL.—Asst. collr., Uganda Prot., 4th Feb., 1905; asst. collr., E. Africa Prot., 1st Apr., 1905; dist. comsnr., 1910.



MONCRIEFF, ALEXANDER BAIN, C.M.G. (1909), M.L.C.E., M. Ann. S. E. —B. 1848; Entered pub. wks. dep. of S. Australia as engnrng. draftman, Nov., 1874; rly. res. engnr., Dec., 1879; engnr.-in-ch. for rlys. and waterwks.; also engnr. for harbours and jetties, 1888-1909; rlyws. comsnr., 1909; also mem. of rly. advisory bd., 1895; and chmn. of supply and tender bd., 1895-9; chmn. of Mun. Tramways Trust, 1907.



MONK, HON. FREDERICK DEBARTZCH, K.C., D.C.L.—B. 1856; ed. Montreal Coll. and McGill Univ. (Law); D.C.L. of Laval Univ.; prof. of constitutional law, Laval; schl. commsnr. of Montreal for 12 years; an advocate practising in Montreal; elec. to H. of C., Canada, at g.e., 1896; re-elec. 1900, 1904, 1908 and 1911; opposition leader for Quebec, 1901-1903; mem. of the privy council for Canada and min. of pub. wks. in Mr. Borden's cabinet, Oct., 1911.
