SOC.; ISA J.P.; AUTHOR OF PAPERS ON NATURAL HISTORY, GEOGRAPHY, AND MINING INDUSTRIES OF BR. GUIANA; ASST. CROWN SURVR., JULY, 1889; AG. CROWN SURVR., 1890, 1892, AND 1893; APPTD. A COMMR. ON SCHEME FOR SETTLEMENT OF INDIAN IMMIGRANTS, APR., 1895, AND MEM. OF COMTEE. TO SETTLE IMMIGRANTS; AG. COMMR. OF MINES, JULY, 1895, AND AG. CROWN SURVR. IN ADDN., SEPT. TO DEC., 1896; JOINT AUTHOR WITH PROF. HARRISON, IN REPORTS OF GEOLOGY OF BARIMA, BARAMA RIVERS, 1897, ESSEQUEBO, POTATO, AND DEMERARA RIVERS, 1898, AND MAZARUNI RIVER, 1899; F.R.G.S., 1898; COMMR. ON DELIMITN. OF BR. GUIANA BOUNDARY, NOV., 1900; SURVR.-GEN., B. HONDURAS, 1905; MEM. OF EXEC. COUN., 1908; SOMETIMES MEM. OF INSTITUTION OF MINING AND METALLURGY, LONDON.



PERKINS, ROBT. CLERK, D.S.O., M.R.C.S., L.R.C.P.—MED. OFFR., S.A.C., AND AG. DIST. SURVR., SWAZILAND, 1902 TO 1907; IS NOW MED. OFFR. TO SWAZILAND ADMSTR.



PERKINS, THOS. LYFF.—DIVSNL SURVR. AND ENGRNR. FOR COUNTY OF MIDDLESEX; DIST. ENGRNR. FOR CITY DIST. OF BRISTOL; DITTO FOR CLIFTON DIST., BRISTOL; EXEC. ENGRNR., P.W.D., HONG KONG, 1904.



PERLEY, HON. GEORGE HALSTEY, B.A.—B. 1857; ED. OTTAWA GRAM., SCHL., ST. PAUL'S SCHL., CONCORD, N.H., AND HARVARD UNIV.; B.A., 1878; ELEC. TO H. OF C., CANADA (ARGENTEUIL) 1904; RE-ELEC., 1908 AND 1911; CHIEF CONSERVATIVE WHIP, 1911; MEM. OF PRIVY COUN., FOR CANADA AND MIN. WITHOUT PORTFOLIO IN MR. BORDEN'S CABINET, OCT., 1911.



PERRETT, H. F.—SERVED IN MET. POL., LOND., 1882-1889; CHIEF DECT. INSPR., S. STTLMTS., MAR., 1899; ASST. SUPT. OF POL., JULY, 1907.



PERRY, SIR ALLAN, KT. BACH (1904); M.D. (DURHAM); D.P.H. (LON.); M.R.C.S. ENG.; L.S.A. (LOND.); B.1860; PRIN. CIV. MED. OFFR. AND INSPR.-GEN. OF HOSP., CEYLON; PRIN. OF CEYLON MED. COLL., 10TH DEC., 1897; MAJOR R.A.M.C. (RETIRIED); MEM. MUNICIPAL COUN., COLONBO; LATE PRES. CEYLON BRANCH BR. MED. ASSOC.; DEL. FOR CEYLON TO INTERNAT. LEPROSY CONF., BERGEN, 1909.



PERRY, B.C. G.—B. 1886; APPTD. AFTER COMPET. EXAM., CLK. OF THE 2ND DIV. OF THE CIV. SERV., AND ASSIGNED TO C.O., 9TH APR., 1906.



PERRY, GEORGE McREDIE, M.B., C.M., GLASGOW, AND ST. MARY'S HOSP., LONDON, F.R.G.S.—AST. COL. SURG., LAGOS, OCT., 1893; AG. COL. SURG., FEB. MAR., 1894; AG. AST. COL. SEC., MAY, 1894; MED. OFFR. TO EXPEDN. TO IDANAN MOUNTAINS; SEN. AST. COL. SURG., AUG., 1895; AG. COL. SURG., 1895.



PERRY, HON. JOHN.—B. 1845; M.L.A. RICHMOND DIST., N.S.W., SINCE 1889; MIN. OF PUB. INSTR., 1898; CH. SEC., 1904; MIN. OF AGRIC., 1907.



PERTH, BISHOP OF, RIGHT REV. CHAS. OWEN LEAVER RILEY, D.D., CANTAB.—B. 1854; VICAR OF ST. PAUL'S, PRESTON, LANCS., 1883-1894; BISHOP OF PERTH, W. AUST., 1894.



PETERS, JAMES EDWARDS.—B. 1858; ED. ANTIGUA HIGH SCHL.; APPTD. 2ND CLK., REGISTR.'S OFF., ANTIGUA; PERFORMED DUTIES OF 1ST CLK. IN 1878 AND 1880; AG. CLK. OF MAG.'S CT., DIST. "A" IN 1883 AND 1884; SEC. TO RECORD COMMR., IN 1885; APPTD. A COMMR. TO ADMINISTER OATHS IN 1894; AG. DEP. CORONER FOR DIST. "A" IN 1894; CLK., MAG.'S CT., AND DEP. CORONER, DIST. "A," 1895; AG. CH. CLK., REGISTR.'S OFF., IN 1897, 1898, 1899 AND 1900; PERFORMED DUTIES OF REGISTR. AND PROV. MARSHAL IN 1901; CLK., MAG.'S CT., DISTS. "A" AND "B"; AND DEP. CORONER, DIST. "B," JULY, 1907.



PETHEBRICK, EDWARD AUGUSTUS.—B. 1847; F.L.S., F.R.G.S.; EMIGRATED TO MELBOURNE IN 1852; EDUC. PRIVATELY, AND IN MUNICIPAL OFFICES, COLLINGWOOD; ENTD. PUBLISHING HOUSE OF GEORGE ROBERTSON, MELBOURNE, 1862; AGENT FOR COLONIAL BOOKSELLERS IN LONDON, 1870 TO 1894; DEVOTED HIS ATTENTION TO BIBLIOGRAPHY AND RESEARCH IN ENGLISH AND EUROPEAN LIBRARIES, AND COLLECTED AN EXTENSIVE LIBRARY RELATING TO AUSTRALASIA AND POLYNESIA, WHICH HE OFFERED TO THE COMMONWEALTH GOVT. AS THE NUCLEUS OF AN AUSTRALASIAN HISTORICAL MUSEUM. THE COLLECTION WAS TAKEN OVER AND THE DONOR APPTD. ARCHIVIST TO THE COMMONWEALTH, 1909; HE IS NOW CORRESP. SEC. TO ROYAL COL. INST. AND MEM. OF THE LIBRARY ASSOCIATION, U.K.



PHELIPS, HUGH RICHARD.—ED. WEYMOUTH COLL. AND QUEEN'S COLL., OXFORD; LOCAL AUDITOR, NIGER COAST PROT., 27TH OCT., 1894; AST. AUDITOR, E. AFRICA PROT., 9TH DEC., 1896; LOCAL AUDITOR, UGANDA, 29TH APR., 1897; SERVED IN UGANDA MUTINY (MEDAL AND CLASP); LOCAL AUDITOR, E. AFRICA AND UGANDA RLY., 26TH DEC., 1901; LOCAL AUDITOR, HONG KONG, 1ST NOV., 1904; J.P., 1905.



PHILBRICK, ARTHUR JAMES.—ED. RUGBY, 1879-1884, TRIN. COLL., CAMB., 1884-1887; B.A.; L.I.B., CAMBS.; CALLED TO THE BAR, MIDDLE TEMP., 1889; AST. DIST. COMMR., G. COAST, 16TH NOV., 1901; PROV. COMMR., 14TH APR., 1902.



PHILLIPS, HAROLD ERNEST.—B. 1877; TEMPORARY CLK. TO AUDITOR, B. HONDURAS, 6TH OCT., 1892; 5TH CLK., TREAS., CUSTOMS AND P.O. DEPTS., 23RD JUNE, 1893; 4TH CLK., 1ST FEB., 1894; 3RD CLK., TREAS., AND CUST. DEPT., 16TH MAY, 1897; 2ND CLK., 7TH JUNE, 1898; 2ND CLK., C.S.O., 1ST SEPT., 1900; AG. CHIEF CLK., C.S.O., AND CLK. OF COUNCILS, 12TH APR. TO 30TH SEPT., 1901, 15TH MECH., 1902, TO 24TH JULY, 1904, AND FROM 14TH DEC., 1904, TO 28TH JUNE, 1905; AG. DIST. COMMR., STANN CREEK, 22ND JULY, 1905, TO 14TH JAN., 1906; CH. CLK., C.S.O., AND CLK. OF COUNS., 17TH JAN., 1906; PRIV. SEC. TO GOV. SIR E. SWAYNE, 16TH MECH., 1909, TO 31ST JULY, 1910; AG. COMMR. OF CURRENCY, 18TH FEB., 1911; AG. TREASURER, COLL. OF CUST., HARBOUR MASTER, REG. OF SHIPPING, CHRMN. OF BD. FOR EXAMTN. OF PILOTS, PRES. OF QUARANTINE BD., CHRMN. OF BD. FOR POOR RELIEF COMMITTEE, DIR. OF P.O.G. FUND, MEM. OF BD. OF EDUC., MEM. OF EXEC. AND LEGIS. COUNS., 9TH APR. TO 13TH AUG., 1911; J.P. FOR THE COLONY, 8TH MAY, 1911; PRIV. SEC. TO AG. GOV., 5TH AUG., 1911.

PHILLIPS, HENRY DENBIGH.—B. 1872; supernum. clk., col. sec.'s office, Br. Honduras, 1887; ag. clk., col. engrnr.'s office, 1888; ag. rev. offr., July, 1888, to Feb., 1889; clk. to att.-gen., May, 1889; ag. clk. to regis. of sup. ct. and keeper of records, 1889, 1890, 1891, 1892, 1893 and 1894; clk. to regis., sup. ct., 1894; comsnr. of sup. ct. and a comsnr. of deeds, Aug., 1894; ag. regis.-gen., Feb. to Sept., 1898; ag. dist. comsnr., Stann Creek, Apr. to Oct., 1899; ditto, Toledo, Mar. to Dec., 1900; dist. comsnr., Toledo, 1st Jan., 1901; dist. comsnr., Stann Creek, 28th Aug., 1905; ag. dist. comsnr., Belize; offl. recvr. in bankruptcy and offl. admtr., 11th Mar., 1907; ag. regis.-gen. in conjunction with duties as dist. comsnr., Apr. to Dec., 1907; and again from 6th Apr. to 22nd Oct., 1908; a comsnr. of currency, 24th Sep., 1908; ag. treas. and collr. of cust., harb.-master, etc., pres., quarantine bd., chmn. of pauper relief comte., 23rd Oct., 1908, to May, 1909; ag. dist. comsnr., Belize, etc., and regis.-gen., 21st May to 12th Aug., 1909, and from 22nd Jan., 1910, to 3rd Dec., 1911; in charge of audit dept., 4th Dec., 1911.



PHILLIPS, THOMAS B.—5th clk., treasy., customs, and P.O., Br. Honduras, Sept., 1891; 3rd clk., treasy. and customs, 1894; 2nd clk., col. sec.'s office, 1897; asst. treas., N. Nigeria, 22nd Aug., 1900; ag. chief asst. treas. on various occasions; ag. treas. from Nov., 1910.



PHILLIPS, WILLIAM LAMBERT COLLIER.—B. 1858; B.A. (Dunelm); dep. clk., gen. assembly, Barbados, 1879; comsnr. of probate, 1882; clk. gen. assem., 1891; col. treas., 1899.



PHILLIPS, WILLIAM NATHANIEL.—B. 1861; entl. civ. serv., Barbados, Dec., 1883; chief clk., savings bank, Dec., 1886; offr. of customs, Sept., 1890; ag. actuary, savings bank, Apl. to July, 1892; 2nd clk., treasy., Aug., 1892; chief clk., treasy., Sept., 1897; ag. col. treasur., Feb. to Nov., 1910, and July to Sept., 1911.



PHILP, HON. ROBERT.—B. 1851; M.L.A. of Queensland, since 1886; sec. for pub. wks., 1893-6; sec. for pub. instr., 1894-5; for rlys., 1895-7; for mines, 1893-9; treasur., Mar., 1898, to Dec., 1899; premier, Dec., 1899, to Sept., 1903; and Nov., 1907, to Feb., 1908.



PICKERING, C. H.—Town mag., E.A.P., 1910.



PICKERING, WM.—Ck. of wks., P.W.D., Gambia, 22nd Mar., 1899.



PICKFORD, W.—Dist. comsnr., E.A.P., 21st Aug., 1903.



PICKWOAD, CECIL ARTHUR.—B. 1876; ed. Bedford Modern schl.; 3rd customsoffr., Br. Hond., June, 1895; 2nd ditto, Nov., 1895; several times acted as clk. in treasy., cust. and post.off.; 3rd clk., treasy., and cust. and clk. to quarantine bd., May, 1897; 2nd clk., Sept., 1900; asst. auditor, N. and S. Nigeria, Dec., 1901; local auditor, G. Coast, Dec., 1902; local auditor, Lagos-S. Nigeria, May, 1905; ditto, new Col. and Prot. of S. Nigeria, 1906.



PICKWOAD, HOWELL.—Ed. at Bedford Mod. schl.; clk., atty.-gen.'s off., Br. Hond., Nov., 1895; 3rd cust. offr., 12th Aug., 1898; 4th clk., treasy. and cust., and clk. to comsnrs. of currency, 27th Dec., 1901; 2nd grade cust. and excise offr., Aug., 1903; col. branch of exchequer and audit dept., 21st Oct., 1904; asst. treas., E. Africa Prot., 26th June, 1905.



PIDCOCK, HENRY.—Ed. at Royal Naval schl., New Cross, London; Imperial Brit. E. Africa Co., 1892; comdr., E. Africa Prot., ss. "Juba," 1st July, 1895; asst. collr., Nov., 1896; port offr., 1st Apr., 1897; holds nominal appt. of asst. supt. of police.



PIERIDES, LUKE G. Z.—Ck. to cons., Larnaca, Cyprus, Dec., 1884; treasy. clk. Larnaca, June, 1887; official mem. of local adminstr. comte., hon. sec. and treas., hosp. bd., 1894-1902; mem. of bd. of educntn., 1890-1904; chief clk. to comte., 1903; inspr. of weights and measures; sec. Zygi Impr. comte.; hon. sec., Carob soc.; sec. to agric. shows, 1908 and 1909.



PIERIS, PAUL'S EDWARD, Samarasinghe—wardhana, M.A., Trin. Coll., Camb., Barrister-at-law, Inner Temple, 1886; Ceylon civ. ser., 1896; asst. to gov't. agt., 1898; pol. mag., Panadura, 1899; dist. judge Ratnapura, 1899; asst. to gov't. agt., 1901; ag. dist. judge, Matara, Mar., 1902; asst. to gov't. agt., Galle, June, 1903; asst. St. Louis exhib., Feb., 1904; dist. Kegalle, Mar., 1905; ditto, Kalutara, 1906.



PIGGOTT, SIR FRANCIS TAYLOR, Kt. (1905).—Barrister-at-law; employed by special service in 1887; legal adv. to pr. Japan, Nov., 1887; sec. to att.-gen. Sir (afterwards Lord Russell of Killowen) Behring Sea arbitn., 1883-4; proc.-gen., 1894; ag. ch. just., 1895 to 1897; ch. just. Kong, 27th Apr., 1905; reed. thanks of gov't. for ser. in connection with loans, 1902; author of "Nationality and Colonialization," "Exterritoriality," "Extra-Territorial Rights," "Foreign Judgments and Jurisdiction of Torts," and "Imperial Statutes applicable to the Colonies."



PIGOTT, FRANCIS JOSEPH, M.I.C.E., engrnr., P.W.D., Ceylon, 1887; ag. mun. Colombo, 1897; prov. engrnr., S. Pro-ditto, E. Prov., 1903; asst. D.P.W., 1903; col. engrnr. and surr.-gen., Penang, S. Prov., 1903; ag. col. engrnr. and surr.-gen., S. Prov., to Apr., 1908; mem. of exec. couns., Singapore, 1907; ag. col. engrnr. and surr.-gen., Sept., 1909; confirmed D.



PILOT, WILLIAM.—I.S.O. (1904), D.D., F.R.G.S.; fell. Aug. Coll., Cant.; ordained by Bishop Wilberforce, Oxon. prin. Queen's Coll., St. John's, 1867; sec. of Eng. schl., 1875; pres. of incor. higher educn., 1893; pres. of incor. non-sec., 1903; pres. of historical soc., 1903; commissary, 1905; exam. chap. to E. Newfd.; reed. thanks of H.M. Govt. for report on educn. in Newfd.; reed. th. H.M. Govt. for service in connctn. with Patriotic Fund.



PINDER, JOHN HOTHERSALL.—Ed. at Caius Coll., Camb., M.A. (2nd cl. class admitted solicitor (Eng.) 1887; ch. regtr., 1901; called to the bar, Linc.'s Inn, 1901; Comsnr., Lagos, 1904.



PINKETT, F. P.—Solr., admitted 2nd cl. class clk., secretariat, Lagos, 1895; dist. clk., 1897; trav. comsnr., 1903; ag. prov. exec. Prov.; mem. exec. and legis. couns., S. Prov., 1906.



PINTO, MAURICE SALVADOR.—B. 1878, Madras; Barrister-at-law; cadet, Col. ser., Oct., 1896; off. asst. to gov't. agt., E. Jan., 1898; Sabaragamuwa, Dec., 1900; pol. mag., Tangalla, Sept., 1900; pol. mag., Panadure, Dec., 1900; Avisawella, Dec., Galle, Sept., 1905; comsnr. of requests, Nov., 1907; dist. judge, Jaffna, Jan., 1908.

PITOT, LÉON EMILE.—B. 1866; govt. survr. and supt. of pub. wks., Seychelles, 11th Apr., 1889; govt. engr. and architect, Mauritius, Apr., 1891; gen. man. of rlyws. and engineer, Mauritius, 14th Sept., 1896.



PITTMAN, EDWARD FISHER, A.R.S.M.—B. 1849; entd. mines dept., N.S. Wales, 1877; held positions of mining survr., geological survr., and chief mining survr.; lecr. in mining at Sydney Univ., 1893-1902; under-sec. for mines, N.S. Wales since Sept., 1902, and govt. geologist since Sept., 1901; author of "The Mineral Resources of New South Wales," 1901, and many geological reports and papers.



PITTS, HON. JAMES STUART, C.M.G. (1907).—B. 1847; M.L.C., Newfoundland, from 1883; also mem. of exec. coun., 1883, 1889, 1894, and from 1899.



PLAGEMANN, CONRAD O.—Ck., Bassetterre waterwks., St. Kitts, 1882; clk. S. P. waterwks., 1885-1894; asst. surv. of roads and pub. wks., 1888-1891; clk., Bassetterre town improvment commrs., St. Kitts, 1891; ag. sup. pub. wks., St. Kitts-Nevis, 1893; inspr. of weights and meas., 1893; town clk., Bassetterre, 1903; ag. sup. pub. wks., and M.L.C., St. Kitts-Nevis, May, 1911.



PLANT, GEORGE FREDERIC.—B.A., (Oxon); graduated, class. hona., 1900; cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., 1901; off. asst., Kurunegala, 1902; off. asst., Galle, 1904; pol. mag., Avissawella, 1905; dist. judge, Ratnapura, Apr., 1906; ditto, Matara, Dec., 1906; asst. govt. agt., Kalutara, May, 1909.



PLANT, ROBERT.—Inspr. of native educn., Natal, 18th Oct., 1888; senr. inspr. of native schls., 1st July, 1904.



PLATT'S, W.A.F.—Asst. dist. commsr., E.A.P., 15th Feb., 1907.



PLAYFORD, THE HON. THOMAS.—Mem. house of assm., S. Australia; held office as commsr. of Crown lds. and immigrn. at various periods between Feb., 1876, and June, 1881; commsr. pub. wks., June, 1884, to Feb., 1885; commsr. of Crown lds. and immigrn., Feb., 1885, to June, 1885; treas. and premier, 1887 to 1889, and again 1890 to 1892; mem. of fed. convention, 1891; mem. of Kingston ministry, 1893; agt.-gen. for S. Australia in London, 1894 to 1898, and representative of col. at col. confee., Ottawa, 1894; mem. H. of Assm., S. Australia, 1899 to 1901; mem. of Senate, Australian parliament, 1901-1906; min. of defence, Commonwealth, 1905-1906; has ret. from politics.



PLOWMAN, GEORGE THOMAS, C.M.G. (1908).—Ck. and shorthand writer, col. sec.'s office, Natal, 1890; 1st clk., 1891; ch. clk., 1894; sec. to civ. ser. bd.; asst. under-sec., 1898; sec. to prime min., July, 1901; sec., lands and works (now rlyws. and harbrs.), Nov., 1901; mem., civ. serv. bd., 1901; sec. to prime min.; acctg. offr., rlyws. and harbrs., 1st July, 1905; prov. sec., Natal Prov., 1910.



PLUMPTRE, GEORGE BERESFORD.—B. 1869; ed. Trent Coll.; served with 33rd squadron, I.Y., S. African War, Jan., 1900, to Sept., 1902 (medals, Queen's 4 clasps; King's, 2 clasps); inspr. land settlement dept., O.R.C., 1st July, 1903.



PLUNKET, 5TH BARON (created 1827), WM. LEE.—PLUNKET.—B. 1844; G.C.M.G. (1910); K.C.V.O., J.P., Dublin and Wicklow; honorary attache to the embassy at Rome, 1889-92; Constantinople, 1892-4; priv. sec. to lord-lieut. of Ireland since 1900; gov. and commodr.-in-chief, New Zealand, 1904-1910.



POGUE, ROBERT HAMMOND.—B. 1863; 3rd class clk., col. sec.'s office, Gibraltar, Feb., 1883 (after compet. exam.); transf'd. to pol. office, Jan., 1886; 3rd class clk., P.O., 1889; 2nd class, Jan., 1891; 1st class clk., col. sec.'s office, Nov., 1893; ag. regist. of births, marriages and deaths in June, 1895; 1st cl. clk., treasy. and port depts., and regist., marine ct., July, 1895; 1st cl. clk., col. treasy., and clk. to regist. of shipping, 1898.



POIRIER, FRÉDÉRIC.—B. 1832; apr., 1870, volr., proc.-gen.'s office, Mauritius; 1870, copying clk., ditto; 1872, sg. clk., ditto; 1873, astt. clk., jun. dist. magistracy; 1874, 2nd clk., proc.-gen.'s dept.; ch. clk., 1886; in 1876, sec. to a comitee, to inquire as to the central gaol; in 1882, sec. to a comitee of inquiry as to the working of the central civil status depts.; curator of vacant estates, June, 1890.



PONTIFEX, SYDNEY CLAUDE OVERTON.—B. 1871; apptd. to cust., Br. Guiana, 1891; 5th class offr., 1892; 4th ditto, 1894; 3rd ditto, 1898; transf'd. to cust., So. Nig., 1899; ag. P.M.G., Apr., 1900; asst. collr. cust., Feb., 1901; ag. collr. and ag. P.M.G., July, 1902, to Feb., 1903, and Apr. to Nov., 1904; prov. collr. of cust., Oct., 1906.



POOLE, H.—B. 1887; apptd., after compet. exam., clk. of the 2nd div. of the civ. ser., and assigned to the C.O., May, 1907.



POPE, Sir JOSEPH, K.C.M.G., (1912), C.V.O. (1908), C.M.G. (1901), I.S.O. (1906).—B. 1854; entered civ. ser. of Canada in 1878 as priv. sec. to the late Sir John A. Macdonald, prime min. from 1882 till his death in 1891; astt. clk. of the Queen's Privy Coun. for Canada, 1889; under-sec. of state and dep. registr.-gen. of Canada, 1896; author of the Memoirs of Sir John A. Macdonald; Royal Tour in Canada, 1901, and other works; attached to the staff of the Br. agt. on the Behring Sea arbitration at Paris, 1893; agt. of Canadian govt., at joint high commrs., Quebec and Washington, 1898-99; deputies by govt. to arrange Royal tour in Canada, 1901; assoc. sec. to Alaska boundary tribunal, London, 1903; recd. C.V.O. for services on the occasion of the Quebec tercentenary celebrations, 1908; holds 2nd cls. of Japanese Order of the Sacred Treasure; under-sec. of state for external affairs, 1909.



POPE, PERCY W. T.—B. 1856; ed. at Prince of Wales Coll., Charlottetown, P. E. Is.; apptd. Dominion auditor at Charlottetown, 1883; asst. rec.-gen., 1st Jan., 1887.



POPPLEWELL, H. B.—Asst. dist. commsr., E.A.P., 1910.



PORRAL, ALBERT, I.S.O. (1903).—B. 1846; supernum. clk., Crown land office, Gibraltar, Nov., 1862; 2nd class clk., Jan., 1875; 1st class clk., Jan., 1883; sec. to comm. to inquire into the organisation of the pol. force, 1887; contracting offr. in 1890; sec. to the Crown lands bd., with a seat at that hd., Jan., 1891; ag. contracting offr., June to Oct., 1892; commn. of Crown lands, 1894; offl. trustee in bankruptcy, 1907; is also Imp. Russian consul, and manager of the Anglo-Egyptian bank.



PORRAL, JOHN.—Ck., port office, Gibraltar, Aug. to Sept., 1874, and July, 1877, to May, 1878; writer in H.M.'s dockyard, Sept., 1874, to July, 1877; 3rd clk., col. sec.'s office, June, 1878; 2nd clk., 1883; 1st class clk., Jan., 1890; ch. clk., Dec., 1891.



PORTAL, Dr. E.—Asst. govt. med. officer, Seychelles, July, 1892; govt. med. officer, Mauritius (Rodrigues), 1901; asst. med. supt., Barkly, and lunatic asylum, 1st July, 1905.



PORTELLI-CARBONE, ALFONSO M.D. (Malta Univ., 1883).—L. M. (Rot. Hosp., Dub.), 1890;

police physician for Zurrico, Safi, Crendi, and act. pol. phys. for Micabba and Chiricop, and sanitary inspr. for the 6th country dist., Aug., 1884; dist. med. offr. for Valetta, Sept., 1885; is a mem. of the Br. Med. Assoc. (Mediterranean branch), 1888; fell. Br. Gynaecol. Soc., and mem. Internl. Med. Cong., Berlin, 1890, and Rome, 1894 (obst. sec.).



PORTER, W. HENRY, I.S.O. (1911).—Clk. pres.'s office, Dominica, Nov., 1874; treas. clk. and excise offr., Nevis, 1878; 1st landing waiter and quarantine offr., St. Kitts, May, 1881; ag. treas., Dominica, Feb., 1884, to Oct., 1887; ag. mag., dist. F., Nov., 1887, to Feb., 1888; treas., Dominica, July, 1890; adminstr. govt. of Dominica, Apr. to Sept., 1904, June, 1905, to Apr., 1906, etc.; is a mem. of exec. and legis. couns. and chmn. of quarantine board.



PORTER, W. T.—Ed. at Univ. Schil. and Jesus Coll., Camb., B.A. (law), 1901; called to the bar, Inner Temple, Jan., 1901; joined N. E. circuit, and pract. at York, Leeds, Bradford and W. Riding of Yorks sessions; mag., E. Africa Prot., 19th May, 1907; ag. adminstr. gen., July to Nov., 1907; town mag., Mombasa, Aug., 1907, to Sept., 1908; 1st cls. mag. for provinces of Kisumu and Naivasha, Sept., 1908, to Feb., 1909, town mag., Nairobi, 23rd Feb., 1909; pres., dist. ct., Cyprus, 26th Oct., 1911.



POTTER, HENRY YARLEY DEIGHTON.—B.1875; ed. at Edinburgh Acad.; asst. engr., with Messrs. Blyth and Westland, consulting engrs. to North British Rly. Co., 1895; asst. engr. to Mr. John Strain, Glasgow, 1896; asst. engr., Caledonian Rly., 1897; draftsman, dir. of wks. dept., Admiralty, 1898; asst. engr., P.W.D., F.M.S., 21st Nov., 1901; state engnr.'s astt., Perak, 14th Feb., 1902; asst. engr., Larut and Matang, Perak, 1st Jan., 1903; exec. engr., 3rd grade, 1st Jan., 1906; ag. exec. engr., 2nd grade, Perak, June, 1906; ditto, Mar., 1909; ditto, Pahang, Jan., 1910.



POTTER, THOMAS IRWIN.—Ed. Queen's Royal Coll., Trinidad; ag. asst. clk., col. hosp., 18th Dec., 1882; clerical astt., Crown lands off., 10th Apr., 1883; clk., survey dept. (in addition to former post), 1st Dec., 1884; ch. clk., Crown lands off., 16th Aug., 1897; ch. clk. and astt. inspr. of schls., 1st Nov., 1898; warden, La Brea and Oropuche (owing to spec. knowledge of asphalt question); ch. offr. of customs, Brighton, La Brea, 1st Jan., 1899; harb.-master, Brighton harbour, La Brea, in addition to wardenship, 1st July, 1899; J.P. for county of St. Patrick; mem. of society of arts, and dormant mem. Zoological society of Lond.; ag. sub. int., crown lands, 1st Sept. to 31st Oct., 1901, and from 10th Oct., 1905, to Jan., 1906; ag. harb.-mast., June to Dec., 1906; stip. justice, La Brea, and Oropuche in conjunction with wardenship, 5th June, 1907; ag. harb.-mast., May to Nov., 1908; ag. sub-intendant, Nov., 1908, to April, 1909; ag. adminstr. gen., 25th Apl., 1909; ag. offl. recvr. and adminstr.-gen., 1st Feb. to 13th Dec., 1910; ag. regist.-gen., 1st Apl. to 30th June, 1911; regist.-gen. (provisionally), 1st July, 1911.



PUTTINGER, DAVID, I.S.O. (1904).—B.1843; ed. Pictou Acad., Nova Scotia; clk., govt. rlys., Halifax, 1863; cashier, 1871; statn. mast., Halifax, 1872; gen. storekeeper, 1874; gen. supt., 1879; gen. man., govt. rlys., Canada, 1892; mem. govt. rlys., managing bd., 1909; astt. chmn., 1910.



POTTS, HENRY WILLIAM.—Prin. of Hawkesbury Agric. Coll., Richmond, N. S. Wales, since May, 1902.



POTTS, MOSES A.—Ed. S. Leone Gram. served in H.M.'s commissariat, S. Leone, Jan., 1853, till Jan., 1860; ag. 2nd clk., treas., Jan., 1865, to Jan., 1866; extra clk., Jan., 1866; land tax clk., Aug., 1869; 2nd clk., treas. after a compet. exam., Sept., 1870; census gen., Dec., 1886, to Feb., 1887; charity gen., 1890.



POWELL, HENRY.—Student, Royal Gard. Kew, June, 1888, to Apr., 1890; curator, Bot. Gardens, St. Vincent, May, 1890, to Nov., 1903; ch. of economic plants div., Apr., 1903; ch. of economic plants div., Apr., 1903; apptd. 3rd astt. in treas., Brit. E.A. Prot., 1st Dec., 1901; 2nd astt., 1st Apr., 1903; treas. (chief acct.), Somaliland Prot., 2nd Dec., 1903.



POWELL, ROBERT ALBERT, A.M.I.C.E.—Roy. Coll. of Science, Dub.—Dist. engrnr., P.W.D., Ceylon; ag. 2nd financial and office astt., 1892; dist. engrnr., Oct., 1893.



POWELL, ROBERT BRANKS.—Priv. sec. lieut.-gov. of B. Columbia, 1900-1904; in charge of arrangements in connection with visit of Prince and Duchess of Cornwall and York to B. Columbia, 1901; cadet, Fiji civ. serv., Oct., 1904; employed in native dept., Nov., 1904; astt. to consnr., Colo. N. and E., Feb., 1906; emp. in gov't. off., and on Western Pacific highl., May, 1905, to Oct., 1906.



POWER, EDMUND LE POER.—Dist. comm., Somaliland Prot., 1st Nov., 1902.



POWTER, GILBERT EDWARD.—Ed. at Imp. Brit. East Africa Co., 12th Oct., 1897; senr. 2nd treas. astt., E.A.P., 1st July, 1897; ag. astt. treas., 1st July to 11th Nov., 1897; 27th Nov., 1897, to 27th April, 1898; 27th July, 1900, to 5th Feb., 1901; sec. comm., 30th Sept., 1900; ag. dep. treas., July, 1903, to 6th Jan., 1904; visited Mombasa prison, 24th July, 1902; ag. May, 1904; sen. astt. treas., 1st July, 1903; ag. postm.-gen., 16th Mech. to 28th July, 1904; ag. dep. treas., 7th July, 1906, to 19th July, 1907; ag. treas., 22nd Dec., 1906, to 19th July, 1907; treas. offr. in charge of Mombasa treas., 15th July, 1909; sec. to commrs., 1st Sept., 1909.



PRANKERD, HORACE ARTHUR.—Ed. at Ipswich and Queen's Coll., Colchester (scholar, 2nd class Tripos), B.A., 1896; master, Loreto, to July, 1907; then at Lausanne and Freiburg-in-Baden; astt. sec., N. Nigeria, Oct., 1910; astt. sec., 1911.



PRATT, CHARLES E. J. BLYTH.—Ed. at Coll.: 2nd lieut., 4th batt. Sherwood Foresters, Derbyshire regt., Jan., 1887; lieut. to Prince of Wales North Stafford regt., May, 1890; instructor of musketry, Jan., 1890; instr. mouth div. submarine miners, R.E., Apr., 1890; astt. inspr. Sierra Leone frontier pol. Astt. inspr., Apr., 1896; J.P. for S. Leone.



PRATT, EDWARD.—Ed. at Shrewsbury F.M.S., Oct., 1898; ag. astt. dist. offr., May, 1899; ag. collr. of land rev., Kuala Lumpur, Feb., 1901; passed cadet, May, 1902; offr., Lower Perak, Jan., 1903; astt. inspr., Tanjong Malim, Sept., 1903; treas., Batu Gajah, Jan., 1904; ag. astt. inspr., Kuala Kangsar, Nov., 1904; ditto, Kuala Lipis, Dec., 1904; ditto, Kuala Lipis, 1907.

PRENDERGAST, HON. SIR JAMES, K.T. BACH. (1881).—B. 1828; is grad. of Univ. of Camb.; called to bar (Mid. Term.), 1857; admitted a barrister of the sup. ct. in N. Zealand, Dec., 1862; atty.-gen., 1865; ch. just. of N.Z., 1875-1899.



PRENDERGAST, JAMES EMILE PIERRE.—Ed. at Seminary of Quebec, and Laval Univ., Quebec; B.A., 1878; LL.B., 1881; returned for La Verendrye, Manitoba, Aug., 1885; again Dec., 1886; on formation of cabinet by Hon. Thomas Greenway, Jan., 1888, was given portfolio of prov. sec.; re-elected in said constituency; elected for Woodlands, 1888; judge of sup. ct., N.W.T., 1902; ditto, Saskatchewan, 1907; puisne judge, court of King's Bench of Manitoba, 1910.



PRESCOTT, ARTHUR STANLEY.—Appd. after compet. exam., supplementary clk., supreme ct., Gibraltar, 1895; 3rd cls. clk., 1899; asst. regier. and deputy clk. of arraigns, 1911.



PRICE, FERDINANDO HAMLYN.—B. 1855; Ed. Rossall and Camb.; writer to the govt. of Ceylon, Mar., 1878; extra office asst. to the govt. agt. for the cent. prov., Sept., 1879; ag. asst. collr. customs, Trincomalee, May, 1880; ag. asst. govt. agt. Nuwara Eliya, Nov., 1880; priv. sec. to lieut.-gov., Mar., 1881; ag. office asst. to govt. agt., cent. prov., June, 1881; priv. sec. to lieut.-gov., July, 1883; ag. asst. govt. agt., Negombo, Dec., 1883; ag. asst. col. treas., Jan., 1884; ag. office asst. cent. prov., Dec., 1885; ag. asst. govt. agt., Kegalle, Mar., 1886; ag. chmn., mun. coun. and mayor, Colombo, Sept. to Dec., 1889; asst. govt. agt., Kegalle, Dec., 1891; chmn. mun. coun. and mayor, Colombo, June, 1896; sent on special duty to Bombay, Feb., 1897; ag. govt. agt., Seribaragamuva, Apr., 1898; again mayor, Colombo, Oct., 1898; spec. serv. as agt. govt. W. Prov., Nov., 1900; again mayor, Colombo, Mar., 1901; govt. agt. prov. of Uva, Oct., 1901; asst. govt. agt., Trincomalee, Oct., 1905; ag. govt. agt., N. Prov., Apr., 1906.



PRICE, HERBERT HENRY.—2nd clk. to asst. commr., Northern Div., Bech. Prot., 1910.



PRICE, J. F. N.—Served in Bochuana and Border police, S. Africa, 1895; 2nd lieut., Bedfordshire regt., 2nd Dec., 1896; A.D.C. and priv. sec. to Sir F. Cardew, K.C.M.G., gov. of S. Leone, 23rd Oct., 1897; clk. of exec. coun., S. Leone; in S. Leone during Mendi and Timini rebellion, 1897 to 1899 (awarded medal); on spec. serv. with W.A.F.F., Lokoja, May to Oct., 1899, when invalided; served with details, 2nd Batt., Bedfordshire regt., Dublin, Shorncliffe and Colchester; passed 4th in musk. at Hythe, 1900; captain, 20th June, 1900; adjut., and quarter-master, 22nd Dec., 1900; served with 3rd Batt. King's Own Yorkshire L.I., Chatham, Malta and Gozo, June, 1901 to Mech., 1902 (awarded medal); asst. adjut. instr. of musk., 1902-1903; dist. supt. of police, N. Nigeria, 3rd Oct., 1903; staff offr., 1st May, 1905; passed lower standard in Hausa, Feb., 1908; passed in criminal law at R.I.C. depot, Dublin; passed in internat. law and Mohammedan law at Impl. Inst.; passed in C. 1, 2, 3, 4 at Preston, Lancs, 1911.



PRICE, SIR THOS. REES., K.C.M.G. (1908); C.M.G. (1901).—B. 1848; served in various positions in the Vale of Neath and G.W. rly. companies, England, 1863 to 1880; dist. traffic supt. at Grahamstown, Cape govt. rly., July, 1890; asst. traffic man., West system, C.G.R., Dec., 1880; ditto, Port Elizabeth, Feb., 1881; traffic man. of East system, 1st July, 1882; ag. ch. traffic man., 11th Nov., 1891; traffic man., North system, 1892; C.G.R. agent in Transvaal and O.F.S., 7th Oct., 1892; ch. traffic man., 1st Nov., 1893; ag. gen. man., 1896; gen. man., C.G.R., 16th May, 1901, to 11th Aug., 1902; gen. man., C.S.A. rly.; mem. of rly. and harb. bd., Union of S. Africa, 1910; is a mem. of geog. soc. of Lisbon.



PRICE, WALTER CROMWELL, B.A.—Ed. Rathmines Sch., Dublin, and at Dublin Univ. and Schol. of Engineering, Queen's Coll., Galway; asst. to James Price, A.M.I.C.E.; engaged on Galway harbour works, 1880; Lock Erne drainage, 1882; Irish light rlys., 1883-1884; Bandon water wks., 1885-1886; dist. engrnr., P.W.D., Ceylon, 1887; in charge of irrigtn. wks., 1888-1890; ag. prov. engrnr., North-Central Prov., 1896; ditto, Uva Prov., 1902; ditto, Northern prov., 1902; prov. engrnr., North-Western Prov., 1904; ditto, Central Prov., 1907; mem. of mun. coun., Kandy, and also of san. bd., Kandy, 1910.



PRINCE, PROF. EDWARD ERNEST., F.R.S.C., &c.—B. 1858; ed. Modern Schl., Leeds, and St. Andrews, Camb., and Edin. Univs.; apptd. demonstr., zool., Edin. Univ., 1885; naturalist, Scotch fishery bd. laboratory, St. Ands.; prof. of zool. and comp. anat., Royal Infirmary Med. Coll., Glasgow, 1890; fishery expert, Irish Deep Sea Survey, 1893; vice-pres. Internat. Fisheries Congress, Washington, Paris, and St. Petersburg, 1903-06-09; vice-pres., biol. sect., Brit. Assoc., 1909; ditto, Royal Soc. of Canada, 1908; mem. of internat. relations coun., American fish. soc., 1910; Canad. mem. of internat. fish. congress, Rome, 1911; life mem. of British Science Guild; mem. of internat. fisheries com.; repres. Canada, under Fisheries Treaty, 1908; chmn. of many fishery comms.: lobster, 1898; Pacific salmon, 1907; Bay of Fundy Shad, 1908; Manitoba fisheries, 1909; Alberta and Sask. fisheries, 1910-1911; chmn. of biol. bd. of Canada; comsrr. of fisheries for Canada, apptd. 1892.



PRING, ROBERT DARLOW.—Puisne judge, N.S. Wales, since 1902.



PRINGLE, ALFRED ERNEST.—Mast., high schl., Malacca, Oct., 1885; headmast., Malay Coll., Singapore, Aug., 1894; headmast., govt. Outram schl., Singapore, Aug., 1895; sub-instr. of schls., Malacca, Jan., 1896; ag. supt. of educn., Penang, Dec., 1906; confirmed, Jan., 1907.



PRINSEP, HENRY CHARLES.—Ed. Cheltenham Coll.; went to W. Australia, 1866; apptd. J.P. in 1867; ag. clk. and draftsman in lands dept., 1874; priv. sec. and A.D.C. to admstr., Nov., 1884, to June, 1885; ch. draftsman, lands dept., 1890; ch. clk., 1892; under-sec. for mines, 1894; ch. prot. of aborigines, May, 1898.



PRIOR, WM. BURGESS.—Mem. provisional N. Borneo Assoc.; res. E. Coast dist. Br. N. Borneo, Aug., 1881; prot. of coolies, E. Coast, 1884; mem. E. Coast coun., 1883; Br. consular agt., 1880; res. and mag., Gold Field dist., Feb., 1887.



PRITCHARD, MAJOR C. G.—1st comsn. R.A., 23rd Nov., 1891; promoted capt., 4th Dec., 1899; adj., Hong Kong volunteers, Jan. to July, 1901; comdt. and adj. (local major), 2nd Apr., 1902.



PRITCHARD, WILLIAM OWEN.—Med. offr., E. Africa Prot., 15th Feb., 1904.



PROBYN, SIR LESLIE, K.C.M.G. (1909); C.M.G. (1903).—Ed. at Charterhouse, and in France and Germany, called to the bar, Mid. Tem., 1884; joint author of "The Jurisdiction and Practice of the Mayor's Court," and other law books; atty.-gen., Br. Honduras,

1893; atty-gen. of Grenada, May, 1896; also ag. col. sec. in 1897-8; ag. admstr. on several occasions; gov. secretary, S. Nigeria, 12th Apr., 1901; gov., Sierra Leone, 14th July, 1904; gov., Barbados, 20th Oct., 1910; assumed govt., 13th Feb., 1911.



PROUT, W. T., C.M.G. (1905), M.B., C.M. (Edin.)—Asst. poor law med. offr., Mauritius, 1885; surg. supt., immigrant ship "Dundee," 1887; asst. col. surg., Gold Coast, 1888; dist. commr., Gold Coast, 1890; col. surg., Gambia, 1893; ag. chief mag., Gambia, 1893; med. offr. in charge of base hosp. during campaign against Foday Sila; col. surg., S. Leone, 1895; title altered to prin. med. offr., 1901; J.P.; pres., quarantine bd.; nominated mem. of city coun.; med. offr. of health, Freetown; M.L.C.; fellow of roy. med. soc., Edin., and corresponding mem. of the epidemiological soc. of Lond.; author of article "Yaws" in "Diseases of Warm Climates" (Davidson); Fil. Volonious (Archives de Parasitologie, May, 1901); "Filariasis in S. Leone" (Brit. Med. Journal, 1902); and other papers.



Prowse, Daniel Woodley, C.M.G. (1912), K.C., LL.D.—Central dist. ct. judge, Newfoundland, 1869; sec. to fisheries bd., 1902; author of a "History of Newfoundland," 1895.



PRYCE, Howard Lloyd, C.M.G. (1911).—Trav. commr., Gambia Prot., Oct., 1896; attached to Gambia field force, 1901 (medal and clasp); ag. ch. mag., Gambia, July to Oct., 1903; 1st cls. trav. commr., Jan., 1904.



PTOLEMY, WM. John, I.S.O., J.P.—B. 1850; ed. at Smithville gram. schl., Ontario; served with G.W. Rly. Co. of Canada, 1873-1875; C.P.R. Dominion govt. telegraph construction, 1875; mercantile life, 1876-1882; entd. govt. serv. as acctnt., treasy. dept., Manitoba, 1883 to 1885; municipal commr., 1886; dep. prov. treas., 1886 to date.



PUGH, J.—Med. offr., E.A.P., Jan., 1910.



PUGHE, S. R.—B. 1877; apptd., after compet. exam., clk. of the 2nd div. of the civil ser., and assigned to the C.O., Aug., 1897; promoted, with gratuity, Aug., 1904; confi. clk., Dec., 1907; minor staff clerk, 1911.



PUGSLEY, Hon. William, K.C., D.C.L.—B. 1850; educ. schls., Sussex, N.B., Univ. of New Brunswick, B.A. (1868), and Univ. of Lond., B.C.L., D.C.L.; called to the bar, N.B., 1872; reporter of the supreme ct., 1873-83; Q.C. by Dom. govt., 1891; elec. to legis., N.B., 1885; speaker, 1887; solr.-gen., 1890; resigned, 1892; re-entrd. legis., 1899; attorney-gen., 1900; premier, 1907; sworn of the priv. council for Canada and min. of pub. wks., 1907; re-elec. to H. of C., Sept., 1911; resig. portfolio on defeat of Laurier govt., Oct., 1911.



PURCELL, Gilbert Kenhelm Treffry.—Ed. Exeter Coll., Oxford; B.A. 1888; M.A. 1893; called to bar, Linc.'s Inn, Nov., 1890; mem. of western circ., also practised at cent. crim. ct.; apptd. asst. to atty-gen. Leeward Islds. (St. Kitts), Mar., 1898; official mem. of exec. and legis. couns. of the presidency of St. Christopher and Nevis; ag. atty-gen., Leewards, Aug.-Oct., 1900; apptd. ag. 1st puisne judge, June, 1901; puisne judge, G. Coast, 11th June, 1901.



PURDON, Andrew.—B. 1875; ed. at Ebury and Conway colls., N. Wales; cadet, H.M.S. "Conway"; sub-lieut., R.N.R., Apl., 1905; lieut., 1908; qualified at Whale Island and H.M.S. "Vernon"; asst. marine supt., N. Nigeria Marine, 11th Sept., 1909; whilst on leave took special course of instruction in hydrographical survey at R.N. coll., Greenwich, 1911.



PURVES, James McLennan.—Govt. forest, Nyassaland, May, 1900; ag. head, forestry, botanic dept., 1906; ch. forest offr., 1910; dir. of agric., Aug., 1911.



QUARTEY, Robert Emmanuel.—B. 1880; outdoor offr., customs, Accra, 1881; 4th cls. customs and treasy., 1883; 2nd cls. audit offr., 1885; 1st cls., 1887; audit clk. to local audt., Jan., 1889; has several times acted as auditor; transf. to post and tel. dept., 1900; ag. ch. clk. and acctnt., 1903; in charge of post and tel. dept., 1903; sent to Axim on spec. duty, 1903; on spec. duty at Pram Pram, 1904; ag. ch. clk. and acctnt., 1905 and 1906; postmstr., Jan., 1907; taking spec. course of int. at G.P.O., London, 1907.



QUEBEC, 5th Bishop of, Right Rev. Andre Hunter Dunn, D.D., D.C.L. (Consec. 1821-1839; late scholar of C.C.C. Camb., B.A., wrangler, 1863; M.A., 1866; hon. D.D., 1893; hon. D.C.L., Bishop's Univ., Lennott, 1907; deacon, 1864; priest, 1865; asst. cur. St. Mark's, Notting Hill, 1864-70; dita Mary's, Acton, 1870-72; vicar of All Saints', Acton, 1872-92.



QUEENSLAND (NORTH), Bishop of, Rev. George Horsfall Froudsham, D.D. (Durham); B. 1863; curate of St. Tees, Leeds, 1887-1891; senior curate, St. Mary's, Ilkley, 1891-1896; priv. chaplain to bishop, Brisbane, 1891; rector of Toowong, Queensland, 1896-1902; bishop of N. Queensland, since 1902.



QUENTRALI, Thomas.—Mining eng., Kimberley, Cape, July, 1889; inspr. of Kimberley, July, 1891.



QUICK, Hon. Sir John, Kt. Bach., LL.D.—B. 1852; elec. to first H. of R., Commonwealth of Australia, 1901; re-elec. in 1906; postmstr.-gen., C. of A., June, 1909.



RADCLIFFE, Chas. Amatas, B. 1866; Comdr., R.N., ret.; naval cadet, 1873-1884; comdr., 1905; served in Soudan war (promoted, medal and clasp "Suskin," bronze star); served in Mediterranean, E. Asiatic, Pacific, and Channel Is. stations, 1877-80; mast. attendant, S. Stltltns., Jan., 1903; harmbr., Penang, Apr., 1903; ag. mast. attendant, S.S., Dec., 1903; mast. attendant, Dec., 1904.



RADFORD, William John.—Charity hosp.; M.R.C.S. (England), 1885; L.R.C.S. (London), 1890; F.R.G.S., 1900; hon. St. John's ambulance sec., 1896; med. E. Africa Prot., 1st June, 1898; sen. med., 1910.



RAE, James Maclure.—Admitted to Bar, 1877; notary public same year; J.J. res. just., Crooked Is. dist., Oct., 1878; commr. at Cockburn harbour, Turks and Caicos Islds., July, 1880; ag. judge of the sup. ct., ex officio auditor of the Turks and Caicos Islds., 1882, to May, 1883, and Mar., 1884, to Oct.; asst. commr., Grand Turk, 1885; sup. Bahamas, Nov., 1887; ag. atty-gen., Jan. to Feb., 1894; ag. ch. just., Feb., and Mar.; ag. atty-gen., June, 1896, to Jan., 1897; to Feb., 1898; Sept. and Oct., 1898; Oct., 1900; 11th to 24th June, 1901; 1st to 3rd Aug., 1902; ag. ch. just., 4th Aug., Nov., 1902; ag. atty-gen., 15th June to 1904; ag. ch. just., 21st Nov., to 4th Dec. and 2nd to 16th Nov., 1908; ag. atty-gen., May to 25th Aug., 1908; ag. ch. just., 13th Feb., 1909; ag. atty-gen., Sept., 1909; ag. ch. justice, from 17th Aug. to Nov., 1911.

RAE, Wm. Charles.—B. 1859; clk. col. sec.'s ff., Mauritius, after exam., Nov., 1876; clk. of the exec. coun., and of coun. of govt., Mar., 1894; compiler of Handbook on the constn., practice, and proceedings of the Coun. of Govt., 1896; ch. lk. col. sec.'s office, Aug., 1900; 2nd asst. col. sec., 9th Nov., 1903; postmr. and supt. of telegraphs, 1st July, 1905.



RALPHS, Edwin, F.R.G.S., F.C.S., F.E.I.S., J.R. San. Inst.—B. 1872; cd. St. Mark's Coll., Chelsea; 1st cls. in Queen's scholarship, in final teachers' exams. (education dept.), and in archbishop's divinity exam.; honours in science, South Kens. exams.; asst. master (junior) Queen's Coll., Hong Kong, 1898; senior grade, 1901; Normal mast., 1906; ag. second master, Apr., 1903, to Mar., 1904, and Apr., 1908 to Apr., 1909; 2nd mast., 8th Apr., 1909; ag. head mast. and mem. of advisory comte., Tech. Inst., 5th July to 5th Nov., 1909, and from 11th May, 1910, to 23rd Oct., 1911; ag. mast., pol. schl., Hong Kong, May, 1902, to Mar., 1904; hon. examinr. in chemistry to Hong Kong Coll. of Med., 1901, 1902 and 1903; dir., Hong Kong Technical Inst., from 1907; also mem. of exam. comte. for "Teachers' Classes," Tech. Inst., 1909-1911; J.P., 1910.



RAMGEORGE EDWARD—Lieut., 4th batt., Prince of Wales', North Staffordshire Regt.; served in S. Africa, Oct., 1902, to July, 1903 (medal, with 3 clasps); ag. priv. sec. and A.D.C. to gov. of Newfoundland, 9th Sept., 1903.



RANA-NATHAN, PONNAMBALAM, C.M.G. (1889), K.C.—B. 1851; ed. at the Acad., Colombo, and Pres. Coll., Madras; barr.-at-law, Inn. Tem.; advce., sup. ct., Ceylon, 1873; mem. of the legis. coun., 1879; mem. of the lawcom. apptd. to report upon certain codes dealing with the laws of Ceylon, 1879; served also on the coms. apptd. at his instarce to report upon the Thoroughfares Ordinance, 1881; obtained the introduction of P.O. savings bank in Ceylon, 1881-83; was one of the select comte. of the legis. coun. apptd. to report upon retrenching the public expenditure of the island, 1882-83; a mem. of the coun. of legal educn., 1884; mem. of the Ceylon coun. of the Col. and Ind. Exhibn., 1886; mem. of the Cent. Irrigtn. Bd., 1888; and of the select comte. to report upon the incidence of the grain taxes, 1889; mem. of the coms. to inquire into the extension of the rly. to the N. parts of the island, 1890; solr.-gen. of Ceylon, 1892; ag. attv.-gen., 1894; ret., 1905.



RAMSBOTTOM, Hon. A. E. W.—B. 1860; formerly col. treas., O.R.C.; prov. admstr., O.F.S., Union of S. Africa, 1910.



RANFORD, HENRY SAMUEL.—Contract survr., W. Australia, 1872; employed on admiralty survey, 1875; staff-survr., 1884; sen. ditto, 1886; govt. ld. agent., Kattanning, Aug., 1897; ch. ld. agt., 1902.



RANFURLY, 5TH EARL OF (Sir UCHTER JOHN MARK KNOX, G.C.M.G.), Viscount Northland and Baron Welles of Dungannon, co. Tyrone, Ireland, Baron Ranfurly of Ramphorlie, co. Renfrew, United Kingdom.—Born 1856; succeeded his brother 1875; ed. Trinity Coll., Cambridge; J.P., D.L. for co. Tyrone; Knight of Justice of the Order of St. John of Jerusalem; lord-in-waiting to the Queen, 1895-7; governor of New Zealand, 1897-1904.



RANKIN, E.B.W.—Entd. service, Br. Guiana, 1885; 5th asst. survr. clk., regist'r's off., 1892; passed exam. as sworn clk. and notary public, 1895, and acted as such on various occasions; in charge of Berbice off. Aug. to Dec., 1895; 4th astt. clk., 1896; clk. to atty.-gen., 1898; sec., special comte. of legislature on Demerara-Essequibo rly. tariff, 1899.



RANKINE, RICHARD SIMS DONKIN.—B. 1875; clk. treasury, Fiji, Feb., 1894; priv. sec. to Sir George O'Brien, Sept., 1897, to 1901; acted clk. to ex. coun. Sept., 1899, to Mar., 1900; apptd. acct. nativ. taxes, treasury, 1901; priv. sec. to Sir Henry Jackson, July, 1902; priv. sec. to Sir E. im Thurn, 10th Oct., 1904; conf. sec., 1st Jan., 1905; sec. to consul-gen. for W. Pacific; clk. of exec. coun.; ag. sec., W. Pacific high coms., June, 1905, and from Nov., 1907, to 31st Dec., 1908; asst. col. sec. and asst. recvr.-gen., 1st Jan., 1909; recvr.-gen. and comnr. of stamps, pres. of marine bd., mem. exec. and legis. couns., 1910.



RANNIE, CLARENCE RUPERT.—B. 1872; clerical assist., audit dept., Antigua, May, 1889; clk. to col. engnr., Antigua, Mar., 1891; ag. clk. to audr.-gen., Sept., 1894; 2nd clk. to audr.-gen., Leeward Is., Jan., 1895; audit clk., Dominica, Mar., 1897, to Aug., 1900; cashier, treasy., Antigua, Sept., 1900; ag. 2nd outdoor offr., treasy., 1st Aug. to 31st Oct., 1902; 2nd indoor offr., treasy., 14th Nov., 1901; ag. 1st indoor offr., 23rd Nov., 1904, to 20th July, 1905, 16th May to 15th Aug., 1908, 1st May to 31st Oct., 1909, and from 1st to 31st Aug., 1910.



RASON, HON. SIR CORINTHWAITE HECTOR, KT. BACH. (1909).—B. 1859; ed. at Brighton, Eastbourne and Reading; M.L.C. for Swan, W. Aust., 1889; M.L.A. for S. Murchison, 1897-1901; ditto for Guildford since 1901; min. of works, 1901; min. of works and rlyws., 1902-4; prem. of W. Aust., 1905; pres. of Royal coms. on mining, 1898, and of Royal coms. on immigr., 1906; agt.-gen. in London for W. Aust., 1906-1909.



RAT, JOSEPH NUMA.—B. 1848; colonial scholarship, Trinidad, 1866; Warneford scholarship, King's Coll., Lond., 1867; seventimesprizeman, literature, divinity and medicine in King's Coll., 1867-1871; matri., Lond. Univ., 1868; prec. science, M.B. Lond. Univ., 1869; M.R.C.S. (Eng.), 1873; asst. col. surg., G. Coast, Feb., 1887; dist. med. offr., Dominica, Aug., 1889; ag. med. offr., public institutions, Dominica, 1890; dist. med. offr., St. Kitts, Oct., 1892; mag. and med. offr., Anguilla, Dec., 1897; dep. judge, court of summary juris., Leeward Is., 1899; dist. med. offr., Nevis, Jan., 1905; M.L.C., Dominica, 1888-1889; chrmn., town improvement comsrs., St. Kitts, 1896-1897; mem. poor law bd., St. Kitts, 1896-1897; has translated several military drill books into the Hausa language for the G. Coast gov't.; has also written numerous papers on Leprosy, Yaws, etc., grammars of the Carib and Hausa languages, and a translation of the Gospel of St. Mark into the French patois of the W. Indies.



RAWSTORNE, HENRY CLANCY.—Asst. offr., civil status, Mauritius, Jan., 1874; clk., stip. ct., Flacq, Mar., 1875; asst. clk., dist. ct., Port Louis, July, 1875; joint clk., ditto, Oct., 1876; inspr. of pol. force, May, 1877; inspr. inland rev., Mar., 1880; and supt. of distilleries, Mar., 1893; ag. supt. inland rev., May to Oct., 1895; supt. of distilleries and inland rev., 1st July, 1905.



RAY, GEORGE CECIL LINGARD.—Entd. Br. Cent. Africa admstr., June, 1893; apptd. asst. collr. in W. Shire dist.; led punitive expdn. agst. Chief Malolo, 1895; judicial offr., 1897; collr. of Mlanji dist., 1897-1901, during which period acted as political offr. accompanying Shirwa expdn., and recd. B.C.A. medal and

clasp; also led punitive expdn. agst. Chief Namwada; collr. and vice-consul, S. Nyasa dist., 1901; 1st cls. asst., 1902; ag. vice-consul at Chinde, E. Africa, Apr. to Oct., 1903; returned to S. Nyasa dist. as collr., vice-consul and dist. mag.; ag. vice-consul, Chinde, May to Nov., 1906.



RAYMOND, WILLIAM HENRY.—Sub-inspr. of pol., S. Aust., 1st Jan., 1904; inspr. of pol., 1st July, 1904; comsrr. of pol., 1st Jan., 1910.



RAYNER, Sir THOMAS CROSSLEY, K.T. (1899).—K.C., Br. Guiana (1903).—B. 1860; ed. at Owens Coll.; matric., Lond., 1878; barr., Mid. Tem., 1882; dist. comsrr., Gold Coast Col., 1887; acted as judge, 1889; mag., Trinidad, 1890; ag. puisne judge, June to Oct., 1891; chmn. of coms. of inquiry into registry of sup. ct., Jan., 1892; ag. comsrr., Tobago, Sept. to Dec., 1892; ag. puisne judge, Trinidad, Dec., 1892, to Sept., 1893; puisne judge, G. Coast, Jan., 1894; ch. just., Lagos, 1895; atty.-gen., Br. Guiana, 1902; chnclr. of diocease of Guiana, 1903; compiled new edition of laws of Br. Guiana, 1904-5.



READ, EDWARD INSKIP, F.R.C.S.I.—Entered govt. service, Trinidad, Feb., 1882; ag. dist. med. offr., S. Nararima and town, and Port of San Fernando, 1882-3; asst. surg., col. hosp., Port of Spain, 1884; surg.-in-charge, San Fernando hosp., 1887; ag. health offr. of shipping, inspr. of immigr. and dist. med. offr., Port of Spain, 1891; in charge of col. hosp., Port of Spain, Nov., 1892; clinical asst., Royal Westminster Ophthal. Hosp., 1893; dist. med. offr., Santa Cruz; examiner to widows' and orphans' civ. ser. fund, 1897; ophthalmic surg. to health office dept., 1900; dist. med. offr., Tacarigua, 1900; D.M.O., Port of Spain West and Diego Martin, and med. offr. of leper asylum, 1909.



READ, HERBERT JAMES, C.M.G. (1907).—B. 1863; M.A., Brasenose Coll., Oxford; 1st class math. mods., and 1st class math. finals; clk., higher div., W.O., Feb., 1887; 2nd class clk., C.O., Jan., 1889; asst. priv. sec. to Mr. Chamberlain, Sept., 1896; priv. sec. to Mr. (now Sir E.) Wingfield, Feb., 1898; 1st class clk., Oct., 1898; principal clk., 1st Apr., 1905; British delegate at African liquor confce. at Brussels, 1899; one of the Brit. delegates on boundary comsrr. at Berlin for the settm't of Anglo-German frontier in E. Africa, 1906; one of the Brit. plenipotentiaries at African liquor confce. at Brussels, 1906; mem. of hon. man. comttee. of sleeping sickness bureau, 1908; chmn. of deptm't. comttee. to enquire into S. African med. staff, 1909; visited E. Africa, 1911-12.



READ, THE VEN. ARCHDN. J. H., D.D.—1st Archdeacon of P. E. Is., 1860; ecclesiastl. comsrr., 1858; formerly of St. John's Coll., Camb., and B.D., 1852; D.D., 1857, of King's Coll., Fredericton, N.B.; rector of Milton, 1865.



REAL, HON. PATRICK.—B. 1847; called to the bar, Queensland, 1874; frequently acted as dist. ct. judge, and for some years was Crown proser. in cent. dist.; mem. of Royal comm. on establishment of a Queensland Univ., 1891; judge of sup. ct., Queensland, 1890.



REDDIE, COLIN SPITTAL.—Imperial Brit. East Africa Co.; collr., E. Africa Prot., 1st July, 1895; prov. comsrr., 1910.



REDDIN, RICHARD.—B. 1837; educ. privately and at Central Acad., Charlottetown, P. E. Island; barrister of the sup. ct. for some years prior to 1892 when he was apptd. to the office of surrogate and judge of probate for Prince Edward Island.



REECE, EARLDY BRANWELL.—B. 1876; pub. service, St. Lucia, Apr., 1892, as supernumerary clk., govt. off.; 3rd clk., Apr., 1893; 2nd clk. and acct., treas., Apr., 1894; ag. ch. clk. six occasions, 1895-9; honours graduate, 1896 (diploma), Ont. business coll., Canada (affil. ch. accts.), Canada; apptd. chief clk. and bookkeeper, treasury, Gold Coast, 26th April, 1901; introduced double entry system of accounts; the treasury in conformity with fin. inst., June, 1901; acctnt., Jan., 1902; sen. asst. treas., June, 1905; ag. chief acctnt., G. Coast govt. rly., Feb., 1907; chief acctnt., 1st June, 1907; treas., G. Coast, 1909.



REECE, FREDERICK ST. AUBYN.—Cllk., P.O. Barbados, 1873; 2nd clk., 1875; resig. 1877; landing waiter, St. Lucia, 1883; col. postmr., St. Lucia, 1885.



REECE, REV. JAN. EBENEZER.—B. 1847; ed. at St. John's Coll., Camb.; B.A. in 1868; M.A. in 1874; ag. curate of St. Michael's Cathedral, Barbados, and priv. sec. to Bishop Parry, 1872; asst. master of Harrison Coll., and curate of St. Michael's Cathedral, 1877; curate of St. Bartholomew's, 1878; curate of St. Luke's, 1882; bishop's chaplain, 1884; inspr. of schls., 1886; canon of St. Michael's Cathedral, 1905.



REECE, I. RICHARD.—Ed. at St. John's Coll., Camb.; B.A. in 1870; called to bar, Inn. Feb., 1871; J.P., Barbados, 1873; coroner for parish of Christchurch and St. George, 1873; ag. postmaster and serjeant-at-arms, 1874; ag. pol. mag. of St. Michael's parish, 1875; ag. judge of ass. ct. of appeal, 1875-7; comsrr. of probate, 1877; ag. solr.-gen., 1880; registr. of friendly building societies, 1880; ag. judge of the ass. ct. of appeal, 1880-82; ag. atty.-gen. and ex-officio mem. exec. and comsrs.; ch. just. (on two occasions for special purposes) and chancellor of the diocease; sole comsrr. to report on a complaint of the vestry of St. Michael (Barbados) against Bridgetown Water Works Co.; comsrr. to report on working of courts of inferior juris. (Barbados); comsrr. to investigate charges against rioters (Barbados); Grenada, 1883, judge of ass. ct. of appeal, 1883; ag. ch. just., St. Vincent, 1884; local comsrr. of incumbered estates (St. Vincent), Oct., 1884; comsrr. to examine and report on the govt. schl., St. Vincent; comsrr. to perform special duty in Grenada at the request of S. of S. res. mag., Jamaica, 1888.



REES, LEWIS CHAS. MORRIS PARKER.—B. 1876; ed. Merchant Venturers Tech. Coll., Bristol; art. pupil to Messrs. Foster and La Trobe, architects' survs., Bristol, 1892; asst. borough engnr., Islington, 1897; ch. asst. borough engnr., Margate, 1900; prin. land survr., W.P.W., Hong Kong, 1902; also sec., squatters' bd., 1910.



REVEE, HENRY, C.M.G. (1900), A.M.I.C.E.—B. 1854; passed C.S. exam., Victoria, 1881; instdt., Melbourne Univ., 1870; cadet, Victorian survey dept., 1873; cadet, N.S.W. survey dept., 1874; survr., 1878; survr., Fiji survey dept., May, 1880; staff survr., Jan., 1881; ag. comsrr. for wks., July, 1881, to Feb., 1885; col. engnr., St. Lucia, 1887; dir. of survey, Windward Is., 1891; mem. legis. coun., St. Lucia, 1891; special mem. exec. coun., St. Lucia and St. Vincent, 1891; col. engnr., Gambia, 1894; mem. exec. coun., 1895; ch. English comsrr., Anglo-French bndry, comsrr., 1895-6, 1898-9; director of pub. wks., Lagos, Aug., 1901; ag. col. sec., Jan. to May, 1902; ag. gov'r., May to July, 1902; ag. col. sec., 1902 and 1903; ag. gov'r., 1902; deputy gov'r., 1903; ret., 1904.

REEVES, Hon. William Pember.—Born Canterbury, N.Z., 1857; ed. in Colony; prov. scholarship holder, 1868, and 1872; N.Z. scholarships in classics and English, 1874; Somes Scholar, Christ's Coll., Canterbury; first elected mem. of H. of Reps., 1887; joined Ballance Min., 1891, holding the portfolios of educn., just. and labour; contd. in off. in Seddon Min. to Jan., 1906; author of following N.Z. Acts relating to labour:—Employers Liability, Contractors and Workmen's Lien, Workmen's Wages, Conspiracy Act Amendment, Factories, Shipping and Seamen's Amendment, Shops and Shop Assistants, Industrial Conciliation, Servants' Registry and Vagabonds Attachment, the most important being the Adjust. Concil. Act, providing for compulsory arbitration in labour differences when negotiations between employers and employed fail; agt.-gen. or N.Z. in London, 1896; holds also the offices of stock and loan agent for N.Z.; comsnr. under N.Z. Public Revenues Act; custodian of N.Z. Public Trust Fund Securities, &c., &c.; represented N.Z. at Internat. Commer. Congress at Philadelphia, 1899; mem. of Pacific Cable Comte., 1899; high comsnr. for N.Z. in London, June, 1905; resigned, 1908, on apptmt. as director of London schl. of economics; mem. of senate, London Univ.; author of the "Long White Cloud," "State Experiments in Australia and New Zealand," and other publications relating to N.Z.



REIBEY, The Hon. T.—Speaker of house of assm., Tasmania, mem. for Westbury; mem. of the exec. coun., July, 1876; was leader of the Opposition, Mar., 1875, to July, 1876; and Aug., 1877, to Dec., 1878; premier and col. sec., July, 1876, to Aug., 1877; col. sec. in Mr. Crowther's ministry, Dec., 1878, to Oct., 1879; elected speaker, July, 1887-1891; held off. without portfolio, 1894-99.



REID, Alexander, I.S.O. (1914).—Ent. the govt. ser., Tasmania, 1858; under treasurer, 1895.



REID, Arthur William.—Ed. at Leicester and Stafford; asst. store dept., Mersey rly., Liverpool, Jan., 1886; chief in 1889; asst. loco. supt. (stores), Uganda rly., 1897; sen. asst., 1899; chief storekeeper, 1903.



REID, The Rt. Hon. Sir G. H., P.C. (1907); G.C.M.G. (1911); K.C.M.G. (1909).—Min. of pub. instructn., N.S.W., Jan., 1883, to Mar., 1884; M.L.A. for E. Sydney; leader of Opposition, 1891; premier, 1894-9; leader of Opposition in the Commonwealth parlmt. from the inauguration of the Commonwealth, 1901-4; premier and min. for external affairs, Aug., 1904, to July, 1905; represented N.S.W. in London at H.M.'s Diamond Jubilee; high comsnr. for the Commonwealth of Australia in London, 1910.



REID, Irvine Kemit.—M.B., C.M. (1884), M.D. (1887), D.P.H. (1st class honours in practical hygiene) (1891), Abdn. Univ.; J.P. (1904); mem. of Roy. Med. Soc., Edin.; mem. of Soc. of Med. Offrs. of Health; house surg. and sec., W. Norfolk and Lynn hosp., King's Lynn, 1886; surg., res. med. staff, Col. hospital, Georgetown, Br. Guiana, 1887-89; govt. med. offr., Is. of Wakenaam, Rio Essequibo, 1889; med. offr., penal stltmnt., Massaruni; and res. surg. pub. hosp., Bartica, 1892; med. offr., Mara dist., 1893; ditto, Peter's Hall dist., and mem. med. bd., 1894; med. offr., Cotton Tree dist., 1895.



REID, Hon. John Dowsley.—B. 1859; ed. pub. schl., Prescott, Queen's Univ., and Royal Coll. Physicians and Surgeons, Kingston, Ontario; physician; elec. to H. of C., Canada, 1891, 1896, 1900, 1904, 1908 and 1911; mem. of privy coun. for Canada, and min. of customs in Mr. Borden's cabinet, Oct., 1911.



REID, Thomas.—B. 1881; ed. Clongowes Wood, and Queen's Coll., Royal Univ., Dublin (B.A.); cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Nov., 1905; off. asst. to govt. agt., E. Prov., Apr., 1907; mun. mag., Colombo, Dec., 1909; landing surv., customs, Colombo, Aug., 1910.



REILLY, Robert O'Malley.—Sub-inspr., Bechuanaland Prot. police, 1904; passed Cape civ. ser. lower law exam., 1909.



REITZ, Hon. F. W.—B. 1845; ed. in Cape Colony and at Edin. Univ.; called to the bar, England, 1868; chief just. of O.F.S.; state sec. of S.A.R.; pres. of O.F.S.; pres. of Senate, Union of S. Africa, 1910.



RENDLE, Anstruther Carvew.—Ed. at Marlborough Coll., Christ's Coll., and St. Mary's hosp.; B.A. (Camb.) 1888; M.R.C.S. (Eng.); L.R.C.P. (Lon.); M.B., B.C., M.D., (Camb.); D.P.H.; conjoint bd., 1895; med. offr., E. Africa and Uganda Prots., 12th Jan., 1906.



RENNER, William, M.D. (Brux.), M.R.C.S. (Eng.), L.K. and Q.C.P., L.M. (Ireland).—Ed. at the Liverpool Coll., and Univ. Coll., Lond., and Liverpool, Rotunda, Dublin, and St. Jean hosp., Brussels; mem. of the Pathological Soc. of London; late ophthalmic asst. to Prof. Streatham, Univ. Coll. hosp., Lond.; ag. surg. S. Leone, 1882-83; asst. col. surg., Freetown, 1886; in charge of lun. asyl., and incurable and smallpox hosp., Kissy; J.P., 1891; deputy coroner for pol. dist. of Freetown, 1891; surg.-capt., late S. Leone vol. corps, and reed. W. African medal and clasp, 1898-99; has acted on several occasions as col. surg., pres. of quar. bd., inspr. of health, dep. harb.-mast., inspr. of health and shipping, and prim med. offr.



RENTON, Alexander Wood, M.A., LL.B. (honours), Edin.—Forensic prizeman; Lord Rector's essay prizeman; Bacon scholar, Gray's Inn, 1882; b. 1861; called to the bar, 1885; puisne judge, Mauritius, Aug., 1901; chmn., local comtee. of soc. of comp. legis., 1902; chmn. of mountain reserves comsn., 1913-4; ag. procureur and advocate-gen., Aug., 1904; puisne judge, Ceylon, Aug., 1905; author of "Wood Renton on Lunacy"; joint author of first edition of "Edmunds on Patents"; editor of Law Journal; editor of "Encyclopedia of the Laws of England"; editor of "The English Reports"; joint editor of 2nd edition of "Burges on Colonial and Foreign Laws."



REW, Charles Edward Daniel Oldham.—Ed. at Marlborough Coll., and the Roy. Mil. Coll., Sandhurst; 2nd lieut. Nov., 1890; major, West India Regt., Aug., 1906; retired pay, Dec., 1906; A.D.C. to maj.-gen., Sir H. Beengough, K.C.B., ag. gov. of Jamaica, Mar. to Dec., 1893; brigade signalling offr., Jamaica, 1892-5; served in expdtu. agt., Fodye Kabba, River Gambia, 1891-2 (medal with clasp); Northern Territories, Gold Coast, 1898 (clasp); special serv. offr., Ashanti Field Force, 1900; specially employed in raising Yorubas for the G. Coast Regt. in N. Nigeria, and Lagos Hinterland, Jan. to Aug., 1901; apptd. company commdr., G. Coast Regt., W.A.F.F., Aug., 1901; major, 2nd command, Dec., 1904; prov. comsnr., Ashanti, Feb., 1907.



REYNOLDS, A. E.—B. 1881; apptd., after compet. exam., clk. of the 2nd div. of the civ. ser., and assigned to the C.O., Aug., 1900.



RHOADES, Edmund Lushington.—Ed. Rugby Schl.; lieut. and comdr., naval dept., B. Cen.

Africa Prot., 1894; 1st offr., marine transport dept., 1904.



RHODES, FRANK.—B. 1866; joined post and tel. dept., O.F.S., Sept., 1888; postmnr. and telegraphist, Boshof, Sept., 1888; ditto, Bethlehem, Apr., 1893; ditto, Jagersfontein, Mar., 1895; 2nd supervisor, G.P.O., Bloem., Dec., 1895; inspr. of telegraphs, Jan., 1898; sec., posts and telegraphs, O.R.C., Mar., 1900; ag. P.M.G. and gen. man. of telegraphs, O.R.C., Feb. to July, 1901, and Mar. to July, 1906; retired.



RICE, CECIL N.—Ed. Harrison Coll., Barbados; supernum. clk., admstr.'s office, St. Vincent, 1890; ag. 2nd clk., apr. to July, 1891; Dec., 1892, to Feb., 1893; 2nd clk., and sec. to gen. bd. of health, June, 1893; ag. ch. clk., and clk. of exec. and leg. couns., med. regr. and man. of govt. printing dept., on several occasions, 1895-1908; assisted in relief work after hurricane, Sept.-Dec., 1898; port. offr. and cust. offr., 1898; ag. sec., hurricane loan bd. on different occasions, 1899-1908; ag. sec., bd. of educ., 1907-08; 2nd clk. to gov't. Windward Is. (Grenada), Aug., 1901; ch. clk., Nov., 1901; relieving offr. and sec. to Capt. A. H. Young, C.M.G., on spec. miss. to St. Vincent after volcanic eruptions, 1902; spec. ment. by gov. and S. of S. in desps. for services rendered in connection with relief work after volcanic eruptions, 1902; priv. sec. to ag. gov't., Windward Is., 1906-1907 and 1909; clk. to exec. coun., Grenada, 1911.



RICHARDS, HON. ALBERT ELSWOOD, M.A.—B. 1848; ed. at Upper Canada Coll. and Toronto Univ.; called to the bar, Ontario, 1874; called to the bar, Manitoba, 1882; bencher of law soc., Manitoba, 1883 to 1899; judge, King's Bench ct., Manitoba, 1899 to 1906; judge of ct. of appeal, Manitoba, 1906.



RICHARDS, T. H. HATTON.—Associate to ch. justice, W. Australia, 1881; clk. to ch. judicial comsnr., Western Pacific, 1883; assoc. to ch. jus. and clk. sup. ct., Fiji, Nov., 1883; also marshal, vice-admiralty ct., 1884; ag. priv. sec. to Sir W. C. F. Robinson, gov'nr. of S. Australia, and clk. to exec. coun., July, 1885; A.D.C., May, 1886, and also in Melbourne, Mar., 1889; priv. sec. to Sir W. Macgregor, admstr. of Br. N. Guinea, and clk. to exec. and leg. couns., Aug., 1889; also a res. mag.; treasr. and collr. of customs and a mem. of the exec. and leg. couns., 1890, and mem. native regulation bd. as 1st registr.-gen., 1891, initiated a system of land registn. in the island and generally organised the dept.; agt. gov't. sec., Feb. to Sept., 1892; asst. col. sec., Gold Coast, May, 1893; ag. ch. asst., col. sec., Mar. to July, 1894, and clk. to exec. and leg. couns., again from Sept., 1895, to Feb., 1896; clk. of couns., Oct., 1896, to Mar., 1897; invalided, 1897; asst. sec. to gov't., Cyprus, 1900; ag. comsnr., Lamuca dist., Aug. to Oct., 1904, and May to Oct., 1905; ag. chief sec. to gov't., 20th June to 17th Nov., 1908, 20th May to 13th Nov., 1910, and from 4th July to 11th Oct., 1911.



RICHARDSON, EDMUND L.—Jun. clk., col. sec.'s office, Tobago, May, 1874; ch. clk., Oct., 1879; ag. registr. of deeds, sup. ct., July, 1880, to June, 1881; ch. clk., audit office, July to Dec., 1881; 2nd rev. offr. and landing waiter, St. Lucia, Dec., 1881.



RICHARDSON, THE HON. EDWARD, C.M.G. (1879).—B. 1831; entered the N. Zealand parlmt. in 1871 as representative for the city of Christchurch; min. for pub. wks., 1872; held that office through various changes of ministries till Jan., 1877, when he was compelled to retire on account of ill-health; again took office as min. of wks., Sept., 1884, to Oct., 1887.



RICHARDSON, JAMES A.—Copyist regisr.'s office of Br. Guiana, Dec., 1875; sworn clk., July, 1883.



RICHARDSON, JOSEPHUS HAROLD.—Entd. N. Zealand govt. insurance dept.; comsnr. of ditto since 1890.



RICHMOND, JAMES, C.M.G. (1866).—Engrnr., irrigation wks., Jamaica, 1874; engrnr., 1876-90; asst. dir. pub. wks.; director, Jamaica govt. rly., since 1890; j.p.



RIDDLICK, CHARLES.—Sub-inspr., R. pol., 1894 to 1900; lieut., Sierra Leone W.A.F.F., 1900 to 1904; asst. dist. comm. Nigeria, 1904-1906; dep. inspr.-gen. of Africa Prot., 5th Jan., 1906; lieut.-gtn. Essex regt., 1902; capt., 1906; inspr.-certif., schl. of musk., Hythe, 1898; p.m. (capt.), Chelsea, 1903.



RIDGEWAY, THE RT. HON. SIR J. G.C.B. (1906), G.C.M.G. (1900), K.P.C. (Ireland).—B. 1844; ret. from 2nd class with the rank of col., 1889; under-secr. dept., India, 1881-5; comsnr. for delimit. Afghan frontier, 1885-7; under-secr. to lord of Ireland, 1887; lieut.-gov. of the Isle of Man, 1893; gov't. of Ceylon, Dec., 1893-96; of comsnr. sent to S. Africa on Trans. constitution, 1906; mem. of hon. man. of sleeping sickness bureau, 1908; chan. dirs., Br. N. Borneo Co., 1910.



RIDLEY, A. A.—Clerical asst. in priv. Br. Guiana, 10th Oct., 1878, to 31st Aug., 1888; 6th class offr. of customs, 1st Sept., 1888; 1st Aug., 1888; 4th class, 12th July, 3rd class, 1st Aug., 1898.



RIDLEY, HENRY NICHOLAS, C.M.G. M.A. (Oxon); F.R.S.; asst. in botanic Museum, 1880 to 1888; dir. of game forests, S. Sttlmts., 25th Sept., 1888; visit of inspection to Cocos-Keeling and Is., 1890.



RIES, BERNARD SAMUEL.—Asst. clk. dept., B. Guiana, Dec., 1877; on priv. offr. of med. offr. to immigr. dept., Feb. and Apr. to May, 1881; 5th cls. clk., Apr., 4th cls. clk., Mar., 1893; 3rd cls. clk., July, 1894.



RIGBY, WALTER.—Served with R.N. Matabeleland, 1896; Cape med. staff., 1897; 1 clasp; Impl. Light Kitchener's Fighting Scouts, Boer war medal, 4 bars; King's 2 bars, 1899-1906; asp. of pol., E. Africa Prot., 16th May, 1904; asp. of pol., E. Africa Prot., 15th Oct., 1904; asp. of pol., 1910.



RIND, WALTER LOCKHART.—B. 1867; Rossall schl. and Univ. Coll., Oxon; B.A. 1890; priv. sec. and clk. to administrator councils, Seychelles, June, 1900; priv. clk. to gov't., Nov., 1903; and asp. of Jan., 1906; ag. aud., Oct., 1906; and collr., 1909; ag. auditor, and mem. and leg. couns., Aug., 1909; ag. crown-pr. legal adviser and pol. mag., Apl. to Nov., 1909; chmn. of bd. of directors, Carnegie pub. compiled Vol. III. of "Laws of New Revised, 1899-1907."



RISLEY, JOHN SHUCKBURGH.—B. 1877; Marlborough and Magd. Coll., Oxford exhibitioner; 2nd class classical med., 2nd class jurisprudence, 1890; open st. Inns of Court, 1892; called to the bar, M.A. and B.C.L. 1894; author of "The..."

RISSIK, HON. J. F. B.—Formerly min. for lands and native affairs, Transvaal; provincial dmstr., Transvaal Province, Union of S. Africa, 910.



RITCHIE, GEORGE LE HARRIVIER KERR BAINBRIDGE.—Natal Civ. Serv., 1891; lieut., 1st batt. N.R.R., 1892; served with Mashonaland Field Force, 1896, attached to Rhodesian Horse, present at the relief of Ft. Charter, Ft. Salisbury, Mazoe, and Hartley Hills, ment. in desp. (medal and clasps); asst. collr., Nyasaland Prot., Dec., 1897; 2nd grade resident, Apr., 1907.



RITTER, GUSTAVE A., C.M.G. (1902).—Ck. to the judge of the sup. ct. of Mauritius, 1864; regvr. V.-A. ct. 1873; marshal of V.-A. ct., 1882; unoff. nominated mem. of legis. coun., May, 1891.



RIVERS, GEORGE F.—B. 1884; apptd., after compet. exam., ck. of the 2nd div. of the civ. ser., and assigned to C.O., 16th July, 1902.



ROBB, DAVID.—B. 1860; 2nd ck. asst. and shorthand writer, legis. assem., Natal, Feb., 1894; ck. asst. and Hansard reporter, legis. coun., Mar., 1894; has acted as ck., legis. coun., and as sec. to govt. commis.



ROBERT, FREDERIC.—Admitted a solicitor of sup. ct. of Mauritius, 1885; ag. mag., Rodrigues, from Nov., 1895, to Dec., 1896, June, 1897, to Sept., 1898, and Apr., 1900, to June, 1901; dist. ck. and sen. civil status offr., Plains Wilhems, Curepipe division, 15th July, 1901; ag. regvr.-gen., May to Oct., 1903; ag. mag., Rodrigues, last Apr., 1904; ag. dist. and stip. mag. of Mauritius, 20th July, 1904; ag. mag., Lesser Dependencies, 19th Sept., 1904, confirmed as such, 11th Sept., 1905; confirmed as dist. and stip. mag., Mauritius, 1st Oct., 1907.



ROBERTS, A. B.—B. 1854; entd. civ. ser., O.F.S., 1878; landroos of Fauremsch, 1883; res. mag., Bloemfontein, 1896; rlwy. auditor, O.F.S.; served as war secretary, O.F.S.; entd. Transvaal civ. ser., 1903; res. mag. and native commnr., Potchefstroom, 1908; prov. sec., Transvaal Province, Union of S. Africa, 31st May, 1910.



ROBERTS, CHARLES JAMES, C.M.G. (1852).—B. 1846; ed. at Sydney Gram. schl.; alderman of Se-dney, 1877; J.P., 1878; mayor and ch. mag., 1879; comnr. at the Sydney Internat. Exhibn., 1879-80; comnr. for N.S. Wales at Melbourne Exhibn., 1880-81; at Amsterdam Exhibn., 1883; at Calcutta Exhibn., 1883-84; and at Col. and Ind. Exhibn., 1886-7; M.L.A., 1885 and 1888; postmr.-gen., 1887; in the Parkes ministry; mem. Centennial Celebration Comsn., N.S.W., 1888.



ROBERTS, HON. ERNEST ALFRED.—Mem. H. of R., C. of A.; hon. min., 1911.



ROBERTS, GEORGE FORSE.—B. 1881; ed. Univ. Coll., London; telegraphist, G.P.O., Sept., 1897; 2nd div. ck., exchequer and audit dept., Apr., 1900; cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Dec., 1905; off. asst. to govt. agt., Uva Prov., Apr., 1907; pol. mag., Panadure, Jan., 1909; Jaffna, Dec., 1909.



ROBERTS, J. C., F.I.P.S.—Offic. shorthand writ., Barbados, June, 1895.



ROBERTS, JACOB THOMAS.—B. 1874; ed. at C.M.S. Collegiate schl., Lagos; joined civ. ser. and apptd. 6th cls. ck., qrtmr.'s off., Hausa force, 3rd Aug., 1899; asst. storekpr., med. dept., 1st Jan., 1900; ag. med. storekpr. and warden, Lagos hosp., 4th Nov., 1903, to 3rd Jan., 1904; 4th cls. ck., med. dept., 1st Apr., 1904; 3rd cls. ck., audit off., 1st Feb., 1905; 2nd cls. ck., ditto, 1st Jan., 1907; 1st cls. ck., ditto, 1st Jan., 1908; in charge of audit off., Ebute Metta, 21st Jan. to 26th Feb., 1908; asst. chief ck., audit off., 1st Jan., 1911.



ROBERTS, PERCY HAMER.—Prison offr., Br. Guiana, 19th Nov., 1901; served penal settlmt., Massaruni, and at Essequibo and Georgetown county prisons; clerical asst., Georgetown and Essequibo prisons; gaoler, G. Coast, 5th Mar., 1911; keeper, James Fort prison, 1st June, 1911.



ROBERTS, ROBERT.—B. 1872; apptd. to cust. serv., B. C. Africa Prot., July, 1904.



ROBERTS, THOMAS WEBB.—B. 1880; ed. Hertford Coll., Oxford; cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Oct., 1902; pol. mag., Matara, Aug., 1905; Panadure, Sept., 1906; dist. judge, Chilaw, Feb., 1900.



ROBERTSON, A.—Med. offr., E.A.P., June, 1907.



ROBERTSON, DONALD.—B. 1860; cadet in post office, N. Zealand, 1873, and filled various offices until his appt. as sec. of the postal and telegraph dept. in 1907.



ROBERTSON, GEORGE HAWTHORN MINOT.—B.A. Oxon.; cadet, S. Sttlmts., Oct., 1908; sent to China to study Hokkien, June, 1909.



ROBERTSON, WALTER BANNERMAN.—B. 1854; ed. at dist. schls., Marshfield, P. E. Island, high sheriff of Queen's Co., 1896 to 1902; collr. of cust. for the port of Charlottetown, Apil., 1902.



ROBERTSON, W. C. F.—Ed. Trin. Coll., Dublin; exhibitioner, 1885 and 1887; classical scholar, 1888; classical moderator, 1899; inspr. of schls., G. Coast, 1898; director of educn., 1899; ag. controller of cust., 1899; compiled census rept., 1901; ag. sec. for native affairs, 14th June to 19th Nov., 1905; prov. consnr., 20th Nov., 1905; sec. for native affairs, 15th May, 1907; ag. col. sec., 4th July to 25th Sept., 1908; chief asst. col. sec., 22nd Jan., 1909; ag. col. sec., 1909; deputy gov., Jan., 1910; ag. col. sec., Sept., 1910.



ROBERTSON-EUSTACE, ROBERT WILLIAM BARRINGTON.—Ed. at Shrewsbury; capt., reserve of officers and late 4th Batt. S. Stafford Regt.; served in the S. African War with Canadian Mounted Rifles and A.S.C. (medal and six clasps); asst. dist. supt. of pol., E. Africa Prot., 10th May, 1904; sup't. of pol., 1910.



ROBINSON, FRANKLIN.—B. 1878; M.A., Durham Univ.; cadet, S. Sttlmts., Oct., 1902; ag. head of Malay Coll., Malacca, Apr., 1903; demarcation offr., Malacca, 4th Dec., 1903; passed final exam. in Malay, Jan., 1904; mag., June, 1904; passed cadet, July, 1904; ag. dist. offr., Jasim, Dec., 1905; ag. dep. regiar. of sup. ct., sheriff, mag., comnr. of ct. of requests, regiar. of marriages, and chmn. of bd. of licensing justices, Malacca, Sept., 1907; ag. 3rd mag., Penang, Dec., 1907; ag. dist. offr., Prov. Wellesley, Mar., 1908; 3rd mag., Singapore, Mar., 1910.



ROBINSON, J. ALEX.—J.P. and notary pub. for the col. (Newfild.), ed. Vict. Coll., Jersey, and New Kingswood, Bath; prin. of Carbonbear grm. schl., 1883-92; elected for Bonavista, 1897; col. sec. of Newfild. and mem. of exec. coun., 1897; accepted leadership of legis. coun., Dec., 1897; May, 1898, returned to H.A. for dist. of Trinity: mem. treasy. bd., 1898.



ROBINSON, JAMES REGINALD WYNDHAM.—B. 1880; ed. at Marlborough and New Coll., Oxford; 2nd cls. mods., 1901; 3rd cls. lit. hum.,

1903; apptd. after open exam., clk. in higher div., chief sec.'s office, Dublin, 18th Oct., 1904; 2nd cls. clk., C.O., 14th Aug., 1905; sec. to veterinary comttee, 1907; sec. to dept.intl. comttee. on W. African med. staff, 1909.



ROBINSON, MAJOR SIR THOMAS BILBE, K.T. BACH. (1910).—B. 1853; formerly major in command of 1st Queenslanders, and senior offr. in Cent. Queensland; man. and dir. of various public companies; J.P., Queensland, 1887; pres. of Rockhampton chamber of commerce; Queensland commr. for Franco-British exhibn.; agt.-gen. for Queensland, 1910.



ROBINSON, T. M.—Postmr., telegraphist, gaoler, and offr. for the sale of ammunition, Ixopo, Natal, Nov., 1883; sub-distributor of stamps, Nov., 1889; J.P. for Ixopo div., 1902.



ROBINSON, VICTOR GEORGE MELLOR, J.P. (Natal).—Asst. teacher, ed. dep., Natal, 1st Feb., 1890; clk., Eshowe magistracy, 22nd Aug., 1892; gov't. off., 1st Nov., 1892; treas'y., 27th Oct., 1893; res. commr.'s off., 1st Oct., 1895; 1st clk., 27th Nov., 1897; 2nd cls. clk., chief mag. and civ. commr.'s off., prov. of Zululand, master, chief mag.'s ct., and regis., chief mag.'s and high cts., 30th Dec., 1897; sec. to chief mag. and civ. commr., 1st Oct., 1900; 1st cls. clk., 1st Nov., 1900; junior mag., 1st Jan., 1904; acted as mag., Eshowe; transfd. to treas'y., 9th Jan., 1905; under-treas., 1st May, 1906; mem. civ. ser. bd.; sec. pub. debt commrs.



ROBINSON, W. A.—B. 1874; ed. Appleby schl. and Queen's Coll., Oxford: 1st classical honours, 1893; 1st cls. lit. hum., 1895; B.A. 1895; 2nd cls. mod. hist., 1896; apptd., after compet. exam., 2nd cls. clk., C.O., 11th Oct., 1897; priv. sec. to Sir M. O'Malley, 1st Apr., 1905; 1st cls. clk., 10th Jan., 1907; asst. sec. to Impl. confee., 1907; asst. sec. to Impl. confee. on naval and mil. defence, 1909.



ROBINSON, SIR WILLIAM, G.C.M.G. (1897), K.C.M.G. (1883), C.M.G. (1877), F.R.G.S. —B. 1836; clk. in the C.O., Jan., 1854; asst. junior, Nov. 1854; 3rd class, June, 1858; was priv. sec. to Mr. Herman Merivale from June, 1858, to May, 1860; to Lord Blachford from May, 1860, to Mar., 1862, when he was promoted to be an asst. senior; priv. sec. to the Right Hon. Edward Cardwell from Apr. to June, 1864; apptd., Nov. 1869, to represent the C.O. on the E. African Slave Trade Coms.; sen. clk., July, 1870; prin. clk., Sept., 1872; one of the col. comttee. for the Vienna Universal Exhibn. of 1873, and special commr. for the Crown cols., and supt. of the col. ct. at that exhibn.; edited the report upon the Br. cols. represented there; was one of the comttee. for securing a permanent col. museum in London; lieut.-gov. of the Bahama Is., Oct., 1874, and gov., 1875; lieut.-gov., Windward Is., 1880; gov., 1881; gov. of Trinidad, 1885; gov. of Hong Kong, 1891; received thanks of bd. of trade, 1877, and of H.M.'s govt., Nov., 1878, in reference to administration of Bahamas; received also thanks of H.M.'s govt., Dec., 1887, for satisfactory settlement of Venezue- lan difficulty arising out of the "Henrietta" and "Josephina" cases; ret. 1898.



ROBISON, CHAS. CARR.—Ed. Dulwich Coll. and St. Paul's, Stony Stratford; served with several banking companies, etc.; attached to treasury, Sarawak, 1901; supt. of cust., 1902; postmr.-gen., shipping-mast. and supt. of cust., 1904.



ROBSON, HUGH AMOS.—B. 1871; called to the bar, 1892; dep. atty.-gen., N.W.T., 1898-99; K.C., 1909; judge, King's bench, Manitoba, 1910.



ROBSON, WILLIAM.—Trained at botanic gardens, Kew; curator, botanic garden, Montserrat, Apr., 1905; hon. sec., perm. exhibn. comttee.



ROBSON, WM. JOHN.—Ed. at Bishopsgate schl. and Trinity coll., Camb.; served Africa (Queen's medal and four clasps); audit clk. (in charge), Transvaal, 1st Nov.; asst. aud.-gen., Apl., 1901; aud.-gen., 1902; aud.-gen., B. Guiana, 13th May.



ROCHE, HON. WILLIAM JAMES, M.D.—B. 1859; ed. pub. schl., Lucan, Ontario high schl., London, Ontario, Trinity med. Toronto; grad. M.D., with 1st cl. hons., W. Univ., London, Ontario, 1883; 1st cl. in medicine of that Univ.; LL.D., 1911; 1883 to Minnedosa, Man., where he is a physician; territorial rep., for Manitou- coun., 1885-1901; has held highest dist. I.O.O.F., Manitoba; elec. to H. of C., g.e. 1896; re-elec. g.e. 1900, 1904, 1908; conservative whip for the West, 1901-1911; of the privy coun. for Canada, and sec. in Mr. Borden's cabinet, Oct., 1911.



ROCK, JOHN CHRISTOPHER WILSEY—B. 1882; ed. Harrison Coll., Barbados; Coll., Oxford; cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., 1905; off. asst. to govt. agt., S. Prov., 1906; Sabahragamuwa, Jan., 1908; p. Panadure, Dec., 1909.



ROCKETT, E. D.—B. 1863; apptd. after compet. exam., clk. of the lower (pow) of the civ. ser., and assigned to the C.O., 1889; supt. of printing dept., 1894.



ROCKS, M. J. W.—Formerly clk. distr. commrs., S. Leone; afterwards Gambia, 1891-8; 1st clk., traff. branch, govt. rly., 1901.



RODD, A. J.—B. 1886; apptd. after asst. library attendant, C.O., 11th cls. library attendant, 18th Feb., 1911.



RODEN, ROBERT BLAIR.—B. 1880; at the bar, Gray's Inn, 1902; clk., police Antigua, 1890; 2nd clk. to the gov't., 1881; acted on several occasions as clk. to the legis. and exec. comttee, dist. mag., Antigua; also acted as clk. to different govs., Leeward Is., in 1883 and 1896; mag., coroner and J.P., Nevis; mem. St. Kitts and Nevis legis. comttee., fed. leg. coun., Leeward Is., Bridgetown, Barbados, 1903; ag. judge, Bridgetown, on several occasions; ag. ct. of appeal, 1903-4, and from 1911; justice, Glendairy pris., 1904; ag. ch. Vincent, mem. of ex. and leg. couns. bd. of educn., and legal adviser to govt., Nov., 1909.



RODESSE, MAURICE.—B. 1871; pres. several puisne judges and ch. justices, S. Ct., from 20th May, 1889; acted as dep. regis., sheriff and dep. regis., Singapore, several occasions since 1893; confirmed as supernumerary regis., 1st Jan., 1902; ag. offl. in addition to own duties, Sept. to Oct., 1909.



RODWELL, CECIL HUNTER, C.M.G.—Ed. Eton and King's Coll., Camb.; served on staff of high commr. for S. Afr., Dec., 1900; Imperial sec., Mar., 1904.



ROE, AUGUSTUS S.—Called to the bar, W. Australia, 1872; special commr. sup. pol. mag., Perth, Oct., 1897.



ROGER, CAPT. ARCHIBALD.—Ensign, Lanark militia, Aug., 1859; gazetted to W. I. regt., Nov., 1860; lieut., Aug., 1861.

ROGERS, HON. BENJAMIN.—B. 1837; M.L.C., P.E.I., 1878-1893; pres. of coun., 1890-93; mem. of amalgamated coun. and assem., 1893-97, 900-04; mem. of several admstns., and prov. ec., treas., and min. of agric., 1900-04; licut.-gov., P.E.I., 1910.



ROGERS, CLAUDE SOMERSET.—B. 1867; obtnd. higher standard certif. at Imp. Forest schl., Dehra Dun, India, with medals for forestry and forest engrnr., 1893; apptd. to Indian forest dept. as forest ranger, 26th May, 1893; promoted to extra ass't conserv. of forests, 4th grade, 26th Mar., 1894; passed exam. in Burmese language, higher standard, 1897; promoted to 3rd grade, 3rd Sept., 1897; 2nd grade, 27th Nov., 1899; forest officer, Trinidad, 24th Mar., 1901; capt. and adjutant, Trinidad Light Horse, 1908.



ROGERS, JOHN ARTHUR.—B. 1868; entered P.W.D., Gold Coast, 1893; survr., under ordnance, of 1895, May, 1897; offl. mem., Accra town coun., 1901; appraiser for town coun., Cape Coast, 1905; appeal ditto, Accra and Sekondi, 1905; served in Ashanti expdt., 1893; received the rks of headquarters staff; 2nd lieut., G.C. vol., 28th July, 1899; lieut., 17th Aug., 1900; capt., 30th Oct., 1904; cert., army form E 511, Chelsea barracks, Mch., 1900; col. aux. forces, long serv. medal, 1909; insp. of works, N. Territories, Jan., 1908; ag. dist. engrnr., P.W.D., Cert. Prov., 1909.



ROGERS, RICHARD EDWARD ELMORE.—Govt. printer and comptroller of stationery, S. Australia, 1st June, 1910.



ROGERS, HON. ROBERT.—B. 1864; ed. Lacroute, Berthier and Montreal, Quebec; in business in Southern Manitoba for several years, and later at Kenora, Ontario; unsuc. cand. for H. of C. in Lisgar, Manitoba, at g.e. 1896; mem. of Manitoba legis., and min. of pub. works for 11 years; mem. of privy coun. and min. of interior in Mr. Borden's cabinet, Oct., 1911; mem. of H. of C. for Winnipeg by acclamation, 1911.



ROHRWEGE, FRANK, C.M.G. (1899).—B. 1878; ed. at Radley and Brasenose; called to the bar, Inn. Temp., Hilary, 1885; joint author of "Parochial Assessment Rules"; a dist. comsnr., Lagos, 1894; ag. Queen's advoc., 1894; D.C., Ed. dist., 1895; pol. mag., 1886; resigned.



ROLANDO, FRANCOIS ADOLPHE.—B. 1845; reg'istr. and offr. of civil status, Seychelles, 6th Jan., 1890; ag. judge and stip. mag., 17th July, 1891; ag. stip. mag., 17th Nov., 1891; Crown atty., Mauritius, 10th Sept., 1897; ag. recvr. of regist'n. dues and conservator of mortgages, 1st Oct., 1905.
