TUCKETT, GEORGE HENRY.—Imperial service, 1891; postmaster, B.C.A. Prot., asst. agt. and P.M.R., Chinde, 1898; ag. service-consul, Chinde, 1899; ag. P.M.G., B.C.A. Prot., 1900-1; ditto, Nyassaland, 1910; master and acctnt. to armed forces, Nyassaland, 1910; deputy P.M.G., Nyassaland, 1911.



TUDOR, DANIEL THOMAS, K.C.—B. called to the bar, Gray's Inn, Nov., 1890; dr.; also practised on West. Circ.; atty. Grenada and St. Vincent, July, 1903; both colonies, May, 1908; acted as chief also as col. sec. of Grenada on several occasions; admstd. govt. of St. Vincent, June, 1907, to 1908; and govt. of Grenada, May and June, and Mar. to May, 1910; commr. to consolidate revise the Laws of Grenada, 1911; ag. legal C.O., May to Oct., 1911; chief justice, same Nov., 1911.



TUDOR, HON. FRANK GWINNE.—B. M.P. for Yarra, Victoria; pres. of Melb. trades hall coun., 1900-1901; elec. to H. of R., C. of A., 1901; min. of trade and C. of A., Apr., 1910.



TUPPER, THE RIGHT HON. SIR C. (creat. 1888), P.C. (1907), G.C.M.G., K.C.M.G. (1879), C.B. (1867), M.D., L.R. Edin. (1843).—Born 2nd July, 1821; is an D.C.L. of Acadia Coll., Nova Scotia; gov. of Dalhousie Coll., Halifax (appd. of Parlmt., 1862); pres. of the Canadian assoc. from its formation, 1867, until mem. of exec. coun., and prov. sec. N.S., 1860; and from 1863 to June, 1867; prime min. prov. from 1864 until he ret. from his govt. on the Union Act coming into force July, 1867; deleg. to England on public from N.S. govt., 1858 and 1865; from the De- govt., Mar., 1868; leader of the deleg. from the union confce. at Charlottetown, 1864; in Quebec in same year, and to final col. in London, to complete terms of union, 1867; patent of rank and precedence from Her Majesty Queen Victoria as an exec. coun., N.S.; the P.C., June, 1870, and pres. of that body 1st July, 1872, when apptd. min. of int. rel. of customs, Feb., 1873; resig. office with Sir Macdonald, 5th Nov., 1873; min. of pub. wks., 1878; min. of rly. and canals, 1879; repre. Cumberland in parlmt. for 29 years in N.S. from 1856 until confederation in 1867, and Commons from that year until he resig. his cabinet and was apptd. high commr. for Canada in London, May 24th, 1884; acted as exec.

or Dominion at the Antwerp Exhibn., 1885; and Col. and Ind. Exhibn., London, 1886; resumed office in Canadian ministry as finance min., 1887; ne of H.M.'s plenipotentiaries at fisheries conferece at Washington, 1887; re-apptd. high commnr., May, 1888; joint plenip., with the Marquis of Dufferin and Sir J. A. Crowe, for negotiating a commercial arrangement between Canada and France, 1892; of S. for Canada, Jan., 1896; premier, Mar. to June, 1896; leader of opposition in H. C. of, 1896-1900.



TUPPER, HON. SIR CHARLES HIBBERT, K.C.M.G. (1833).—B. 1855; son of Sir C. Tupper, mem. of S. bar; grad. Harvard law schl.; mem., house of commons, Canada, 1882-1900; min. of marine and fisheries, 1888-1890; deleg. to Washington in connection with Behring Sea difficulty, 1890; Br. gt. for the arbitration with the U.S. on the ehring Sea question, 1892-3; min. of just., 1895; sig. 1896; mem. of priv. coun. for Canada.



TURGEON, WILHELM FERDINAND ALPHONSE, C., B.A.—B. 1877; ed. at New York city and avul univ., Montreal; barrister; atty.-gen. of uk., 23rd Sept., 1907; elec. to Sask. legis., 1907; elec., 1908.



TURLAY, HON. HENRY.—B. 1859; M.L.A., Queensland, 1893-1902; elected to the Senate, C. A., 1903; pres. of Senate, July, 1910.



TURNER, THE RT. HON. SIR GEORGE, P.C., C.M.G. (1897), LL.D.—B. 1851; premier and eas. of Victoria, 1894-9 and 1900-1; represented col. in London at H.M.'s Diamond Jubilee 1897; pres. of conf. of premiers at Melbourne, 1899; joined 1st Commonwealth ministry as assessor, Jan., 1901; treas., in 2nd (Deakin) ministry; treas. in 4th (Reid-Turner) coalition ministry, 1904; retired from politics, 1906.



TURNER, GEORGE.—M.R.C.S., L.R.C.P. (Lond.), M.B., D.P.H. (Cantab.); lecturer on hygiene, Guy's hosp., 1882-1895; examnr. for P.H., roy. coll. of phys. and surgs., Lond., 190-1895; employed by L.G.B. to report upon phthisis, 1884; and by L.C.C. to inquire into idemies of enteric fever and the sanitation of ver Lea, 1894-95; med. offr. of health, Cape, 95-1900; mem. of Cape med. coun., 1898-1900; of govt. rinderpest experimental statn., Kimberley, 1897-98; med. offr. of health, Transvaal, 1st Aug., 1900; M.L.C.; census commnr., annual, 1904; del. for Transvaal and O.R.C., ternat. Leprosy. cont., Bergen, 1909.



TURNER, JAMES POPSON.—B. 1871; clk., pub. library, St. Kitts, 1890; clk., regist.'s off., St. tte, 1897; comnr. to administer oaths, 1898, 95-1900; mem. of Cape med. coun., 1898-1900; of govt. rinderpest experimental statn., Kimberley, 1897-98; med. offr. of health, Transvaal, 1st Aug., 1900; M.L.C.; census commnr., annual, 1904; del. for Transvaal and O.R.C., ternat. Leprosy. cont., Bergen, 1909.



TURNER, WILLIAM.—Ed. at Abdn. and Edin. wra.; M.A. (Abdn.), 1876; M.B. Edin., 1879; p., 1881; res. phys., roy. hosp. for sick chldrn., 1879; non-res. phys., roy. infirmy., Edin.; res. accoucheur, Glasgow maternity hosp.; mem. roy. med. soc., Edin., fell obstetrical Edin.; ast. surg. civil hosp., Gibraltar; also surg. civ. prison, med. offr. lunatic, and dist. med offr., 1882; pub. vaccinator, urg., 1888; surg. to col. hosp., Oct., 1889.



TUTCHER, WM. JAMES, F.L.S.—B. 1867; at Merchant Venturers' schl., Bristol; ed Royal Gardens, Kew, 1888; ast. supt., botan. and forestry dept., Hong Kong, 1891; astg. supt. in 1893, 1894, 1897, 1900 to 1901, 1902 to 1903, 1905, 1906, 1907, 1908 and 1909; supt., 1910; J.P., 1911; late hon. lecturer on botany, coll. of med. for Chinese author of "Gardening for Hong Kong."



TWEEDIE, HON. LEMUEL J., K.C., LL.D.—B. 1849; ed. at Presbyterian Coll.; admitted to bar, New Brunswick, 1871; mem. of legis., 1874-1878, 1886-1907; has represented Northumberland ever since, except during 1878 to 1882; surr. gen., 1890; prov. sec., 1896; premier, 1900; represented N.B. at the King's Coronation, 1902; holds Canadian Militia long service medal; lieut.-gov. of New Brunswick, 2nd Mch., 1907.



TYLER, JAMES ERNEST.—Govt. printer, S. Stltmtns., 1st July, 1905.



TYRELL, FRANCIS GRAEME.—B. 1876; ed. Pembroke coll., Oxford (B.A.); cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Oct., 1900; ag. priv. sec. to H.E. the governor, Aug., 1901; priv. sec. to H.E. the offr. admtrg. the gov't., Apr., 1902; off. ast. to gov't. agt., Cent. prov., Jan., 1903-Dec., 1904; ag. ast. gov't. agt., Nuwara Eliya, Oct., 1904; seconded supt. of pol., N.W. prov., Aug., 1905, cent. prov., Mar., 1907; dist. judge, Badulla, Dec., 1908; ast. gov't. agt., Matale, Feb., 1909.



TYSER, SIR C. R., KT. BACH. (1909).—Ed. at Rugby and Trin. Coll., Camb., M.A. (1872); called to bar, In Tem., 1873; ast. ag. judic. commnr. and leg. advsr., Cyprus, 1880-1; atty.-gen., Leeawards, 1886-9; pres. dist. ct., Kyrenia, Cyprus, 1895; puisne judge, Cyprus, Jan., 1902; ch. just., 1906; author of "Marine Insurance Losses," 1894; wrote translation of Omar Hilmi Effendi's Evkaf Law, 1899; and of the Mejelle, 1901.



TYSEN, FRANCIS DASHWOOD.—Ed. at Melbourne Church of England Gram. schl., and Trin. Coll., Melbourne Univ.; lieut. 2nd Scottish Horse, S. African War; inspr. of pol., E. Africa Prot., May, 1905; ast. dist. supt. of pol., 1st July, 1906; supt. of pol., 1910.



UNIACKE, CAPT. ANDREW GORE, D.S.O.—Served with N.W. mtd. pol., Canada (including Yukon expdn.), 1893-1898; served in S. African war, with Canadian forces and M.I., 1899-1902 (2 medals, 8 clasps, D.S.O.); dist. supt., N. Nigeria police, 1903; served with expdn. against Okpotos, 1903-4 (W. African medal and clasp); commnr. and ag. dep. inspr.-gen., N. Nigeria police, 1911.



UNIACKE, G. L.—Served as trooper in mtd. pol., W. Australia, 1895 to 1899; private in 2nd contingent W. Austn. M.I., S. African war, 1899 to 1901 (Queen's medal and 5 clasps); reed. commnr. in 4th Batt. King's Own (R. Lancaster Regt.), 1902; seconded for serv. with N. Nigeria Regt., W.A.F.F., 6th Sept., 1902; served in the Kano-Sokoto campaign (medal with clasp), 1903; company commdr., N. Nigeria regt., 1908; noted for brevet-majority, 1909; ast. res., N. Nigeria, 1910, with astp. dated 6th Sept., 1910; still holds commnr. as lieut. in 3rd Batt. King's Own (R. Lancs Regt.), special reserve.



URICH, FREDERICK WILLIAM, C.M.Z.S., F.E.S.—Ed. in Trinidad, Real Gymnasium, Coblenz, and Geneva Univ.; ledger keeper, govt. printing dept., Trinidad, Jan., 1895; acctnt., rly. extensions, Aug., 1895; 2nd clk., educ. dept., Jan., 1899; store-keeper, P.W.D., Mar., 1901; acctnt., educ. dept., Sept., 1903; also clk. to coll. coun., Oct., 1906; ch. clk., educ. dept., and ast. inspr. of schls., Dec., 1906; mem. of bd. of management and hon. sec. to Victoria

Inst., 1894 to 1895, and 1899 to 1901; ag. sec. to agric. soc'y., May to June, 1894; ag. sec. to bd. of educn., Feb. to Apr., 1900; ag. statistical clk. and librarian, col. secretariat, Apr. to Oct., 1907; ag. forest offr., Apr. to Oct., 1908, holds a comm. as lieut. in local forces, Trinidad, since 1897; capt. and adjt., T.L.I.V., 1908; seconded to dept. of agric. as entomologist, 1909.



URQUHART, CHARLES FRDERIC ROBERT HILDYARD.—B. 1867; entd. Crown Agent's off., Jan., 1885; supt. of stock transfer off., 1895; reg. of inscribed stocks and head of stock dept., 1905.



USHER, HENRY CHAS., I.S.O. (1903).—B. 1838; clk., col. sec'y's office, Honduras, June, 1859; in public treas., July, 1865; provost-marshal, July, 1869; pol. mag., now called dist. mag., Belize dist., Nov., 1878; in charge of the public treas., June, 1886, to July, 1887, and Apr. to June, 1889; and of Belize gaol, May to Aug., 1872; has acted as regsr. of shipping, surv. of shipping, inquisitor of wreck and casualty, and inspir. of pol.; was marshal of the V.A. ct., is ex-officio judge of the summary ct., and also coroner of the col.; commr. of currency under Ord. No. 32 of 1894; ag. col. treas., collr. of cust. and postmr., harbr., and suptd. of mercantile marine on many occasions from 1883 to 1900; cr. officio regsr. of births and deaths, 1885 to 1892; suptd. fire brigade, 1886 to 1895; commr. on special duty to the Cays, Aug. to Sept., 1889; ag. col. sec., Aug., 1890; ret., June, 1903.



UTIDJIAN, H. A. S.—English translator to Turkish Adm'y., and translator and priv. sec. to Admiral Augustus Hobart Pasha, 1874-76; joint treas. and acctnt., T. Squadron, Cretan waters, 1876; dragoman and transr. under Mr. Walter Baring, 2nd sec. to H.B.M.'s Embassy, Constantinople, during sittings of special comm., apptd. to try the authors of the Bulgarian atrocities in 1876-77; 2nd in charge and res. Turkish professor, student dragomans establishment under H.B.M.'s embassy, Constantinople, Jan. to Aug., 1878; translator of state documents, Cyprus, since 21st Aug., 1878; acted as attache to commr., Nicosia, and as asst. collr. of tithes in 1878-1880; Turkish examiner, 1879-1907; Turkish translator to leg. coun., Cyprus, 1883; transr., land registn. comm., 1901; sec. to Moslem secondary educ. bd., 1902-1904; apptd. to examine and report on general state of Turkish instruction in Idadi schl., 1905; 4th cls. Mejidieh and Osmanlieh orders.



VALANTIN, W. ADOLPHE.—Asst. clk. and messenger, Queen's advoc.'s chambers, S. Leone, Jan., 1878; acted as asst. sec. to Br. consuls. on the N.W. Liberian Bdry. Comsn. in 1879; clk. to crown solr., June, 1880; acted as clk. to ch. just., 1882; clk. to Queen's advoc., 1883; dep. sheriff, Mar., 1890; clk. to ch. just., Aug., 1891; dep. coroner, July, 1896; clk. atty.-gen.'s chambers, Dec., 1897; curator, intestate estates, Jan., 1902.



VALLÉE, LÉONCE JOSEPH.—Asst. accnt., Couva extension, Trinidad, 1879; storekr., San Fernando extension, 1880; paymr., Guaraçara extn., 1882; asst. clk. locomotive dept., 1884; ch. clk., 1887; ch. cashier, rly., 1894; ch. storekr., 1894.



VANDER BEEK, J. N., I.S.O. (1903).—Extra clk., col. sec'y's office, Singapore, Sept., 1871; 8th clk., Jan., 1873, and attached to govt. house; 6th clk., Dec., 1875; guardian of govt. house, May, 1877; 5th clk., col. sec'y's office, Apr., 1879; 4th clk., June, 1879; 3rd clk., June, 1880; clk., govt. house, Dec., 1883; financial asst., pol., 1905.



VAN DER MERWE, JOHANNES LOEWEN.—Served under govt. of late S. A.R. as mining comm. from 1885 till British occupation, 1st Sept., 1894; mining comm'r., Barberton, 1885; ag. spec. lic. drost, Barberton; chrmn., diggers' comm., Barberton; chrmn., Barberton hosp. bd.; mun. comm'r., Johannesburg, 1893; chrmn., Johannesburg hosp. bd.; chrmn., Jameson Raid comm., 1895-6; mem. of comm. to inquire into cause of dynamite explosion at Johannesburg, 1896; mem. of dynamite relief comm.; mem. of Johannesburg liquor comm.; pres., Witwatersrand agr. soc'y.; hon. mem. Witwatersrand chamber of mines; served during Anglo-Boer war, 1899-1902; prin. clk., townships (mines dept.), Transvaal, 1903; ag. deputy asst. regsr. of mining rights, 1st district regsr. of mining rights, Johannesburg, 1906; mem. of trading bd., Witwatersrand, 1907.



VAN DER MEULEN, FREDERICK A.—B. 1857; ed. at Blundell's Sch., Tiverton, and Keble Col., Oxford; B.A. (hons. in mod. hist.), 1896; M.A., 1900; barrister-at-law, Gray's Inn, 1900; West circuit; asst. dist. comm'r., Sierra Leone, 1901; solr.-gen., 1908; ag. atty.-gen. and also ag. police and circuit judge on various occasions, 1908-1910.



VAN DE VELDE, MARCEL ARTHUR MAURICE.—Ed. at Mt. St. Mary's Coll., Derbyshire; audit branch of E. and A. dept., 29th May, 1900; asst. audr., E. Africa Prot., 9th Mar., 1903; audr., Uganda Prot., June, 1903; E. Africa June, 1904.



VANE, HENRY G. B.—B. 1861; asst. audr., Perak, Dec., 1884; ag. asst. audr.-gen., S. Ap., 1887; audr., Sungei Ujong and Negri Sembilan, May, 1888; treas., pol. mag., etc., Sungei Ujong, Oct., 1890; audr., Selangor, Dec., 1892; state audr., Perak, Apr., 1895; rev. audr., Perak, Jan., 1900; ag. fin. comm'r., Oct., 1903, to Oct., 1904; ag. fin. audr., cent. audit off., Jan., 1904; ag. finance comm'r., Oct., 1906, to 31st Jan., 1907; treas. F.M.S., 26th Nov., 1906.



VAN EEDEN, WALTER CLARENCE.—Entd. cust. dept., B. Guiana, 1891; lieut., B.G. militia, 1897-1900; Hythe schl. of musk. certif. for musketry and maxim guns, 1899; attached to batt. Dorsetshire regt., and gained certif. of proficiency, 1899; asst. inspr. of constab., G. Coast, 30th June, 1900; Ashanti war, medal and gratuity 1900; offr. condg. dist. of Bole, 1901; lieut., 6 batt. Dorsetshire regt., Aug., 1901; lieut., G. Coast regt., W.A.F.F., 1901; certif. E. 511, sch. of instr., Chelsea barracks, Dec., 1901; on expdt. against the Fra Fras, 1902; offr. commdg., Black Volta dist., 1902; transf. to cust. dept., G. Coast, 3rd Aug., 1903; supervisor in charge, Accra cust. dist., 1904; supervisor in charge, S. dist., W Frontier preventive service, 1906-7; supervisor in charge, Axim cust. dist., 1907, 1908 and 1909; harbrmr., Axim, 1909; attached to Impl. customs, London, during May, 1909; 1st cls. supervisor, 24th Feb., 1909.



VAN SOMEREN, ROBERT ABRAHAM LOGAN.—Ed. at Edin. Univ. and Royal Coll. of Surg. Edin.; M.B., Ch.B.; spec. univ. certif., Edin. trop. diseases, and certif. of London Schl. of Trop. Med.; med. off., E. Africa and Uganda Prots., 10th Oct., 1905.



VAN ZIJL, JAMES STRATEN.—Controller, P.O. savings bank, late O.F.S., Sept., 1897; ditto O.R.C., Mar., 1900.



VARDON, JOSEPH.—M.L.C., S. Aust., 1900; comm'r. of pub. wks. and min. of industry, 1894; ch. sec. and min. of industry, 1st Mar. to 28th July, 1905; res. seat in coun., 11th Oct., 1905; returned in Dec., 1906, to Commonwealth

VAUDIN, WILLIAM MARSHALL.—B. 1866; ed. at Harrow and Trin. Coll., Cambridge (M.A.); admt. Ceylon cir. ser., Oct., 1889; off. asst. to govt. agt., Ratnapura, Aug., 1891; fiscal, Cent. Prov., and off. asst. to govt. agt., Kandy, Jan., 1896; asst. collr. of cust., Trincomalie, May, 1898; asst. govt. agt., Vavuniya and Mullaitivu, Sept., 1898; dist. judge, Batticaloa, June, 1900; asst. govt. agt., Trincomalie, Feb., 1902; April, 1906; Aug., 1906; Kegalla, May, 1907; govt. agt., N.C. Prov., June, 1906; Oct., 1907; dist. judge, Kurunegala, Mar., 1909; govt. agt., N.C. Prov., Sept., 1909; ditto, Cent. Prov., 1911.



VAUGHAN, CHARLES STEWART.—B. 1866; ed. Harrow and Trin. Coll., Cambridge (M.A.); admt. Ceylon cir. ser., Oct., 1889; off. asst. to govt. agt., Ratnapura, Aug., 1891; fiscal, Cent. Prov., and off. asst. to govt. agt., Kandy, Jan., 1896; asst. collr. of cust., Trincomalie, May, 1898; asst. govt. agt., Vavuniya and Mullaitivu, Sept., 1898; dist. judge, Batticaloa, June, 1900; asst. govt. agt., Trincomalie, Feb., 1902; April, 1906; Aug., 1906; Kegalla, May, 1907; govt. agt., N.C. Prov., June, 1906; Oct., 1907; dist. judge, Kurunegala, Mar., 1909; govt. agt., N.C. Prov., Sept., 1909; ditto, Cent. Prov., 1911.



VAUGHAN, CRAWFORD.—M.H.A., South Australia, 1905; treas., and comsnr. of crown lands and immigration, 3rd June, 1910.



VAUTIER, JOHN FRANCIS.—B. 1863; clk., repatriation dept., O.R.C., 30th Dec., 1902; acctnt., govt. relief dept., 1st Nov., 1903; examr. of acc'ts, treas., 1st July, 1904; book-keeper to treas., 4th Apr., 1906.



VECCHIO, THOMAS JOSEPH.—Marshal, sup. ct., bankruptcy, etc., and V.-A. ct., Gibraltar 1866; also interp., 1866-76.



VELLA, TOMMASO.—Entd. Malta service, Dec., 1865; clk., May, 1896; dep. collr. of cust., 1892; dep. postmr., 1896; collr. of cust. and aspt. of ports, Sept., 1902; postmr.-gen., May, 1903; mem. of ex. coun. and coun. of govt., 1903.



VILLACOTT, PHILIP NORTHCOTT, M.B. Lond. (hons. in for. and obst. med.) 1895; B.S., 1896; M.R.C.S., L.R.C.P. (Lond.), 1896; F.R.C.S. (Eng.), 1901; house surg., res. obstetric and clin. med., Guy's hosp.; asst. curator of museum, St. George's hosp.; civ. surg., S. African field force, 1901 to 1902; capt., S.A. Constab., 6th June, 1902; transfd. to O.R.C. govt. serv. as res. med. offr., National hosp., Bloemfontein, 1st Dec., 1905; fellow of R. Inst. of pub. health; deleg. from O.R.C. to 2nd Internat. Congress on School Hygiene.



VENNING, G.—B. 1879; apptd., after compet. exam., asst. clk., and assigned to local govt. bd., May, 1899; after further compet. exam., apptd. clk. of the 2nd div. of the civ. ser., and assigned to W.O., 8th Jan., 1900; transfd. to C.O., 16th Apr., 1903.



VERNON, J.—Employed in rly. dept., N.S. Wales; chief acctnt. in treas.; auditor gen., N.S.W., and deputy auditor gen. in N.S.W. for Commonwealth of Australia, Nov., 1902.



VERNON, ROLAND VENABLES.—B. 1877; ed. at Clifton and Oxford; scholar of Balliol, 1895-97; 1st cls. rhods., 1897; prox. acc. Hertford schrl.; Craven schrl., 1897; Jenkyns exhib., 1899; 1st cls. lit. hum., 1897; apptd., after compet. exam., clk. in sec.'s dept. inland revenue, Nov., 1899; 2nd cls. clk., C.O., Aug. 13th, 1900; sec. to Trinidad riot coman., 1903; mem. of managing comitee of E. I. O.; assist. priv. sec. to Lord Elgin, Jan., 1908; priv. sec. to Col. Seely, 16th Apr., 1908; ag. 1st cls. clk., 1st Jan., 1911; priv. sec. to Lord Denman, gov.-gen. of Australia, 1911.



VERRAN, HON. JOHN.—M.H.A., S. Australia, 1901; premier and comsnr. of pub. wks., 3rd June, 1910; also min. of mines, 13th Oct., 1910.



VERTUE, GEORGE ELFORD BANNERMAN.—Apptd. 3rd asst., Nyassaland Prot., Jan., 1901; 2nd grade res., Oct., 1906.



VICKERS, EDWARD.—B. 1842; Emmanuel Coll., Camb.; B.A., 1863; called to the bar, In. Tem., Jan., 1868; advoc. in the high ct., Bombay, Dec., 1868; res. mag., Jamaica, Mar., 1883; acted on several occasions as puisne judge, 1894 to 1904; jun. puisne judge, 1st Apr., 1904.



VICTORIA, RIGHT REV. GERARD HEATH LANDER, Lord Bishop of Victoria, Hong Kong.—B. 1861; ed. at Trin. Coll. and Ridley Hall, Camb., B.A., 1884; M.A., 1888; D.D., 1907; consec. at Lambeth Parish Church, 29th June, 1907; curate of St. Bride's, Liverpool, 1884 to 1888; vicar of St. Benedict's, Liverpool, 1888 to 1896; of Litherland, 1896 to 1905; of St. Cyprian's, Liverpool, 1905 to 1907; chrmn., Litherland schl. bd., 1898 to 1903; chaplain to Liverpool dist. lay readers, 1892 to 1905.



VIGORS, CHARLES THOMAS DOYNE.—Ceylon writer, 1878; pol. mag., 1883; asst. collr. of customs, Trincomalee, 1884; ditto, Galle, 1886; ag. off. asst. to govt. agt., S. prov., from Sept., 1886, to Mar., 1888; ag. dist. judge, Kegalla, Apr., 1888; Tangalla, Dec., 1889; landing survr. cust., Colombo, Nov., 1888, resumed duties, Feb., 1890; ag. pol. mag., Kandy, May, 1894; asst. govt. agt., Matare, May, 1894, resumed same, Jan., 1896; Kalutara, May, 1898; govt. agt., Uva, Aug., 1900; asst. govt. agt., Kalutara, 13th May, 1902; ag. chmn., mun. coun. and mayor of Colombo, May, 1903; asst. govt. agt., Kalutara, Nov., 1903; govt. agt., N. Cent. Prov., May, 1904; ag. govt. agt., W. Prov., June, 1906; govt. agt., N. Cent. Prov., Aug., 1906; ag. govt. agt., W. Prov., Dec., 1906; dist. judge, Kurunegala, June, 1908; prin. collr. of cust., Jan., 1909; ag. postmr.-gen., Sept., 1909; ag. govt. agt. and fiscal, W. Prov., 1909; prin. collr. of customs, Jan., 1911.



VILLIERS, FRANCIS JOHN, C.M.G. (1880).—B. 1851; entered the C.O., Sept., 1869; priv. sec. to the admstr. of Griqualand W., Oct., 1875, and clk. of the coun.; ag. col. sec., May, 1877, to Oct., 1880; mem. of legis. coun., 1879; engaged on special service in connection with the annexation of the prov. to the Cape Col. from Nov., 1880, to May, 1881; audr.-gen., Br. Guiana, 1882; ag. govt. sec., at various times between 1883 and 1896; ret., 1898.



VIRET, ALFRED PERCHVAL.—B. 1865; rev. offr., Dominica, May, 1882; sec. bds. of health and quarantine, Aug., 1884; sec. to local comtee., Ind. and Col. Exhib., 1886; confill. clk. to pres., and clk. exec. coun., May, 1886; govt. offr., treas. and quarantine offr., June, 1891; 1st cl. supervisor of cust., G. Coast, Oct., 1897; asst. col. treas., S. Leone, July, 1899; acted as col. treas., S. Leone, from July to Oct., 1899, and from Jan. to Sept., 1901; acted as col. P.M.G., from June to July, 1900, and from Oct. to Mar., 1902; apptd. collector of customs, 3rd Nov., 1902; ag. col. treas., Nov., 1902, to Apr., 1903, and from May to Aug., 1904; selected in May, 1905, to carry out transfer of the Isles-le-Los to France, under Anglo-French convention of 1904.



VITALIS, NICHOLAS.—Ch. interp. and clk. to coman., Larnaka, Cyprus, July, 1878; ditto, Nicosia, Mar., 1879; clk. and interp. to Queen's advoc., Feb., 1882; regisr., supreme ct., Cyprus, 1905.

WADDELL, HON. THOMAS.—B. 1854; M.L.A. for various districts in N.S.W. since 1887 (with only short interval); col. treas., 1901-4; premier, 1904; col. treas., 1907.



WADE, HON. CHAS. GREGORY, K.C.—Called to the bar, Inner Tem., 1886; Crown proscr., New S. Wales, 1891; proscr. for West. circuit and cent. crim. ct., 1894, and resigned, 1902; ag. dist. ct. judge and chmn. of sess. on various occasions; M.L.A. for Willoughby, New S. Wales, 1903; M.L.A. for Gordon, 1904; atty.-gen. and min. for just., Aug., 1904; premier of N.S.W., 1907-1910.



WAGNER, WILLIAM QUINN.—B. 1849; ed. at S. African Coll., Cape Town; sec. to the Krigsraad under pres. Burgess, in the first Secooceni war, 1876; filled various ag. appts. in Landdrost's off., Rustenburg, subsequently becoming postmaster and town clk. of that place; served in various capacities under O.F.S. govt., 1881 to 1900; mine inspr., Jagersfontein, 1891 to 1900; supt., refugee camp, Heilbron, O.R.C., May, 1901, to Mar. 1902; joined mines dept., Transvaal, May, 1902.



WAIT, WALTER ERNEST.—B. 1878; ed. Fettes and Edinburgh Univ. (M.A.); cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Oct., 1902; addl. asst. to govt. agt., N. Prov., and adml. comsrr. of requests and pol. mag., Mannar and Puttalum during pearl fishery, Feb., 1905; asst. land stltnt. offr., May, 1905; lieut., Ceylon Planters' Rifle Corps.



WAKEMAN, GEORGE HERBERT.—Ed. Bradfield Coll., Berks, and Camb.; admitted solr., sup. ct., England, July, 1891; asst. land offr., Hong Kong, June, 1900; J.P., Dec., 1900; ag. dep. land offr. and offr. recvr. in bankruptcy, Apr. to Dec., 1901; ag. land offr. and offr. recvr. in bankruptcy, Jan. to Nov., 1902, and Jan. to Aug., 1905; comsrr. for oaths, sup. ct., Hong Kong, and comsrr. for taking ackmnts. of married women, Aug., 1905; land offr. and offr. recvr. in bankruptcy, Aug., 1905; ag. regisr. of trade marks and patents, Aug., 1910; ag. regisr. of sup. ct., offr. admstr., offr. trustee and regisr. of companies, Sept., 1910, to Aug., 1911.



WALCOTT, HENRY BARCLAY.—B. 1866 excise and customs offr., St. Lucia, 1884; treasy. acctnt., 1890; ag. ch. clk., treasy., 1891; ag. ch. clk. and acctnt., St. Vincent, 1892; ag. treasy. acctnt., Grenada, 1892; ch. clk., audit office, Dec., 1893; ag. postmtr., 1895-6; ag. ch. of pol. and excise, 1897; 2nd audit clk., col. sec.'s off., Br. Honduras, 1897; auditor, Feb., 1898; ch. asst. treaser., Gold Coast, Jan., 1900; ag. treasy. and mem. ex. and legia. couns., dir., pub. offr.'s guarantee fund, mem. bd. of educn., July, 1900, to Jan., 1901, and May to Oct., 1902; ag. comsrr. of police and supt. of prisons, 1901-1902; pres. Accra town coun., 1901-1902; treas. and collr. of cust., regisr. of shipping, pres., quarantine bd., chmn. poor relief comtee, mem. of bd. of educn., mem. ex. and leg. couns., Br. Hond., Mar., 1903; J.P., Apr., 1903; ag. col. sec., 22nd July to 6th Aug., 1905, 10th Nov., 1905, to 12th Aug., 1906, and from 8th May, 1908; collr. of cust. and detaining offr., M.S. Act, Trinidad, 1909.



WALKER, HENRY.—2nd asst. land dept., Br. N. Borneo, Jan., 1883; asst. supt., lands and pub. wks., Kudat, July, 1883; comsrr., land, and recorder of lands, May, 1884; mem. coun., Oct., 1883; ag. supl., P.W. dept., Jan., 1887.



WALKER, HOPSON PUCKNEY, B.A.—Jesus Coll., Camb., 1883; LL.B. (Lond.), M.A. (Melb.); barrister-at-law (Mid. Tem.), 1888; ch. clk., sup. ct., Melbourne, Dec., 1883.



WALKER, JAMES HUTCHINSON.—Ed. A. Univ., M.A. (nat. sci. hon.), 1876; M.B. (highest hon.), Murray scholar, and gold med. 1878; M.D. 1884; asst. prof., botany, Abdn. prin. med. offr., N. Borneo, Aug., 1881.



WALKER, JOHN C.—4th batt. Yorkshire regt., Coorga Nagpore rifles; served with Yorks. regt., S. Africa (two medals with 5 clasps); asst. offr., Somaliland, Sept., 1905; mentions despatches, 1906; asst. res., N. Nigeria, 1907.



WALKER, LT.-COL. R.S. FROWD, C.M.G.—B. 1850; entered Sandhurst, 1869; ensign, foot, 1871; capt., June, 1881; hon. lieut.-col., A.D.C. to gov., S.S., 1878-9; attached to armed pol., Mar., 1879; dep. commr. of the force, Feb., 1880, and in command from Nov., 1880; on various occasions as pol. mag., asst. res. and sec. to gov.; has received the thanks of several times for his action in dealing with cain and coolie disturbances; in command of expednry force, 1892 and 1894; ag. sec. to Perak, Oct., 1894, to Aug., 1895; organised States Guides, 1896; and since commr. regt.; ag. Br. res., Selangor, Sept., 1896; Jan., 1900; ditto, Perak, Apr., 1900, to May, 1901; ret. 1910.



WALKER, WILLIAM HENRY, B.A.—Appd. 3rd class clk., govt. genl.'s office, 1887; promoted to 2nd cls., 1892; 1st cls. ch. clk., 1908; chf. clk., dept. of external affairs, 1909.



WALL, JAMES HORNE DARRELL.—R. clk. and storekeeper, Holberton Inst., 1878; Nov., 1891; shortld. reporter to W. Ind. Coms., 1897; aud. def. force sects.; ag. aud. gen., Leeward and fedrl. accnt., 1899; also clk. to trade and income tax rec., Sept., 1899; ch. clk. to aud. gen. and fedrl. accnt., May, 1900; ag. treas. of Antigua and fedrl. May-Oct., 1909, and Aug., 1910.



WALLACE, LAWRENCE AUBREY.—1910.—Acting admstr., N.E. Rhodesia, May, 1907; ag. admstr., N.W. Rhodesia, 1909.



WALLACE, SIR WM., K.C.M.G., C.M.G. (1897).—Senior ex. offr., Roy. Navy, 1886; later as agt.-gen., until 1900, when territs. were handed over to H.M. govt.; numerous treaties with native potentates with the Sultan of Sokoto, 1894; commr. served with over 30 expdtions.; deputy high and senior res., N. Nigeria, 1900; admstr. May to Dec., 1901, May to Nov., 1903, Dec., 1905, and July, 1906, to Apr., 1907; African medals, 5 clasps, coronation; received Murchison medal from R.G.S.; important services rendered to geography; many years' residence in Nigeria; ret. 1910.



WALLACE, WILLIAM HENRY.—Edser., 1882; sec. of mines, Tasmania, 1888.



WALLACE, WILLIAM THOMAS EWART.—4th batt., The King's regt.; S. Africa, Feb., 1900, to Sept., 1902; supt. of telegr. S. Nigeria, 1903-5; asst. supt. of telegr. Africa and Uganda Prots., 21st Dec., 1905.



WALLER, DESMOND DALMULPY.—Asst., E. Africa Prot., 12th May, 1895; asst., 23rd Sept., 1899; offr.-in-charge migtn., Nov., 1902; prot. of imigtn., 1904.



WALLIS, CAPT. C. BRAITHWAITE, F.R.G.S.—Ed. privately and at M. Oxford; 2nd lieut., 2nd Manchester regt.; lieut., 1895; capt., 1897; appd. to frontier force, Jan., 1898; ag. dist.

WALTON, HON. SIR EDGAR HARRIS, K.C.M.G. (1911).—M.L.A., Cape, for Port Elizabeth, since 1898; treas.-gen., Feb., 1904, to Feb., 1908; mem. of S. African National Convention in connection with S. Africa Bill, 1909; is proprietor and editor of Eastern Province Herald.



WALTON, GEORGE LAIRD, M.I.M.E., M.I.N.A.—B. 1868; ed. Liverpool coll.; B. of T. Ist cl. certif.; engnr. marine dept., Lagos, 1899; supt. engrnr., 1902; senr. engrnr., S. Nigeria, 1907; supt. engrnr., 1907.



WALTON, GEORGE O'DONNELL.—Matriculated a student of Lond. Univ., June, 1891; called to the bar, Mid. Tem., 17th Nov., 1893; ag. on several occasions as pol. mag., Barbados; judge of the petty debt court of Bridgetown; judge of the asst. ct. of appeal; ag. pol. mag., Bridgetown and dist. “A” from 21st July, 1902, to 14th Feb., 1903; pol. mag., dist. “F,” 9th Dec., 1902; ag. chief just., St. Lucia, 18th May to 29th Oct., 1908.



WALTON, J. E. LAWSON.—Asst. dist. comsrr., E.A.P., 1910.



WARD, C. E.—Asst. dist. comsrr., E.A.P., 7th Aug., 1909.



WARD, DANIEL, K.C.—Sen. mod. and gold medallist in law, hist. and polit. sci., Trin. Coll., Dublin, 1881; M.A., Dublin, 1887; LL.D., Cape of Good Hope, 1891; called to the bar, Mid. Tem., 1881; crown prosecutor, Br. Bechuana-land, 1884; asst. legal adviser, atty-gen.'s off., Cape Colony, 1898; asst. legal adviser, atty-gen.'s off., Transvaal, 1902; legal adviser, 1903; mem. of legis. coun. of the Transvaal, 1903; 2nd puisne judge, O.R.O., 23rd Mar., 1904; author of “Practice at Parliamentary Elections,” “The Marriage Laws of the Cape Colony,” “Digest of the Criminal Law,” etc.



WARD, JOHN CORBET.—I.Y., S. Africa, 1900-02 (Queen's medal and 4 clasps; King's medal and 2 clasps); Transvaal civ. ser., 1902-04; dep. regar., E. Africa Prot., 1906; regar. of documents, 1906.



WARD, RIGHT HON. SIR JOSEPH GEORGE, Bart. (1911), P.C. (1907), K.C.M.G. (1901).—Prime min., col. treas., postmtr.-gen., comsrr. of electric telegraphs, and min. of defence, New Zealand; rep. New Zealand at Impl. confce., 1907 and 1911; mem. of Imp. confce. on naval and mil. defence, 1909; rep. New Zealand at the Coronation of H.M. King George V., 1911.



WARD, W. F.—Assoc. Roy. Schl. of Mines, Lond. (1876).—Analyst, etc., to the govt. of Tasmania, 1882; asst. to Dr. T. Percy and Prof. W. C. Roberta-Austen, etc., in chemical and metallurgical laboratories of Roy. Schl. of Mines, Royal Mint, and Normal Schl. of Science, S. Kensington (1876-80); special apptmt. to Potosi Gold Mining Co., Venezuela (1881); in charge of chemical testing of smoke-consuming appliances at exhibition, S. Kensington (1881).



WARLORD, ALEXANDER TURNER.—B. 1866; served with S. Stiltsn. pol., 1889-1890; joined B.N. Borneo constab. as storekeeper and orderly-room elk., 1st July, 1890; whilst connected with constab. performed the following duties on various occasions; ag. chief gaoler, sub-editor and in charge of P.W.D., 16th June, 1894; in charge of govt. printing office, 1st Sept., 1894, and of P.W.D., 5th Dec., 1894; second in command of Dyak Jubilee contingent, 1897 (medal); resigned, 30th April, 1898; second in command of Dyak Coronation contingent, 1902 (medal); rejoined the ser. as capt.-supt. of civ. pol., and inspr.

of sanitary bd., Sandakan, 2nd Oct., 1902; served in S. African War, wounded and shot four times (medal with five clasps); bronze medal for saving life; B.N. Borneo Company's medal, Mat Sallah expedition (with clasp "Punitive"); apptd. U.S.A. consul agent, Sandakan, 1st July, 1904; J.P. for B.N. Borneo; gen. pub. prosecutor for N. Borneo, 1907.



WARING, EDWARD LENNON.—Ed. at St. Paul's schl. and Crystal Pal. Engnr. Compy. Schl.; astt. engrnr., Uganda rly., 1900-03; astt. ch. survr., E. Africa Prot., 27th July, 1903; dep. dir. of surveys, cadastral branch, 1st Apr., 1906.



WARNER, GEORGE BRUNTON.—Extra clerical astt., G.F.O., P.M. Burg., from Sept. 1st, 1881, to Feb. 16th, 1892; 3rd class clk. civ. ser., and filled the post of 7th clk., G.F.O., Feb. 16th, 1882; as 6th clk., Jan. 18th, 1883; clk., col. engineer's dept., Jan. 13th, 1886; border customs offr., De Jager's Drift, Jan. 8th, 1887; issuer of native passes, Dundee div., Jan. 16th, 1888; sheep inspr., De Jager's Drift, May 7th, 1888; J.P., Dundee div., Dec. 13th, 1892; chief examining offr., Customs Point, Durban, Nov. 21st, 1896; ag. clk. of the court, Newcastle, June 16th, 1900; clk. of the court, Newcastle, Aug. 9th, 1900; J.P., Newcastle div., Aug. 16th, 1900; deputy registrar special court, Newcastle div., Aug. 23rd, 1900, in terms of sec. 25 of Act No. XIV., 1900; has acted as astt. and ag. mag. of Newcastle on many occasions; also for the following periods:—Ag. astt. mag. from Nov. 19th, 1900, to March 24th, 1901; ag. mag. from June 6th, 1901, to Sept. 8th, 1901; ag. astt. mag., Sept. 9th, 1901.



WARREN, A.—Apptd. astt., treasy., O.R.C., 23rd July, 1900; astt. book-keeper, funds dept., 1st July, 1903, acctnt., funds dept., 1st July, 1906.



WARREN, Lieut.-Gen. Sir CHARLES, R.E., K.C.B., G.C.M.G. (1885), K.C.M.G. (1883), C.M.G. (1878).—B. 1840; ed. Chelt. Coll.; was specially employed in various military and administrative capacities in Griqualand W. and the Cape Col. in 1876-8; lieut.-col. for distinguished service; admin. std. govt. of Griqualand W., 1879 to 1880; served in Egyptian campaign, 1882, and brought to justice the murderers of Prof. Palmer and his party; H.M.'s special commr. in Bechuanaland, 1884-5, with local rank of maj.-gen., comdg. expedn.; apptd. to command at Suakim, with rank of maj.-gen., and as gov.-gen., 1886; commr. of metropol. pol., 1886-8; C.R.E., and in command of troops with rank of maj.-gen., Singapore, 1889 to 1894; commanding a div. in war against Transvaal and Orange F. S., 1899-1900.



WARREN, ERNEST, D.Sc. (Lond.)—Demonstrator of zoology at Univ. Coll., Lond., 1894; life mem. of convocation of the Univ. of Lond., 1898; astt. lecturer and museum curator at Univ. Coll., Lond., 1899; elected fellow of Univ. Coll., 1898; astt. prof. of zoology at Univ. Coll., 1900; mem. of the faculty of science, Univ. of Lond., 1902; dir. of Natal govt. museum, 1st Feb., 1903.



WARREN, PHILIP DAVID, C.M.G. (1908); Assoc.Inst.C.E., F.R.G.S., F.Met.Soc.—B. 1851; astt. survr., Ceylon, 8th Feb., 1878; dist. survr., 1st Oct., 1879; office astt. to survr.-gen., 16th June, 1885; astt. survr.-gen., 26th Mar., 1897; survr.-gen., 23rd June, 1904; M.L.C., Ceylon, 1907-8; ret. 1910.



WATKINS, FREDERICK HENRY, I.S.O. (1904).—B. 1869; acted as rev. offr., St. Lucia, 1882; inspr. of schl., St. Vincent, 1883; head grain schl., St. Vincent, 1887; inspr. of Leeward Is., 1889; ag. pol. mag., Grenada, 1890; reported on, St. Lucia schl., 1898; adj. Kitts-Nevis volr. forces, 1897-9; commr. of serrat, Jan., 1900; commr., Turks and Caicos Mar., 1906; ag. judge of sup. ct., June-Oct., 1908, and in 1909-11.



WATKINS, OSCAR FERRIS.—Ed. at borough and All Souls, Oxford, B.A., 1910; served in South Africa with Oxford Light Infantry (43rd), March, 1900, to 1901 (Queen's Medal and 4 clasps); S. Afr. constab., Mar., 1902, to Apr., 1904; and col. sec.'s office, Transvaal, May, 1904, to 1907; astt. dist. commr., E. Africa Prot., June, 1908.



WATSON, E. C.—M.H.A., Trinity, 1888-9; astt. fisheries, 1898; dep. min. for fisheries, 1898.



WATSON, ERNEST CHARLES.—B. 1874, Shrewsbury; called to the bar, Middlesex, 1897; 3rd cls. rec., N. Nigeria, July, 1897; atty.-gen., Sept. to Nov., 1904; astt. atty.-gen., Nov., 1905; ag. ch. just., Mar. to Oct., 1905; May to Aug., 1907; Feb. to Apr., 1908; Sept., 1909.



WATSON, REGINALD GEORGE (1911).—Ed. at Haileybury; cadet, 1883; priv. sec. to Sir C. C. Smith, attached to land office, Malacca, 1888; astt. prot. Chinese, Singapore, 1888; ditto, 1888-9; dist. offr., South, prot. W., 1889; ag. dist. offr., Balik Pulau, 1890; astt. prot. of Chinese, Penang, 1888; ag. prot. Penang, July, 1890; prot. of Chinese, Penang, 1891; ag. sec. to govt., Perak, Sept., 1892; sen. mag., Selangor, July, 1893; to govt., Selangor, Apr., 1899; ag. sec. to Perak, June, 1899; senior mag., Sept., 1899; sec. to res. Perak, May, 1902; commr. of lands and mines, F.M.S., 27th Feb., 1904; lands and surveys, 1906; federal sec., 1909; ag. res.-gen., 26th Feb., 1910.



WATSON, HON. ROBERT.—B. 1881; M.H.A., Newfoundland; ed. at St. Paul's and Rugby; elected for Trinity, 1897, 1899, and 1909; mem. exec. coun.; col. st. parly. head of depts. of post office, educn., rly., pub. health and ph., 1909; mem. exec. comtee., Diocese of London, 1910; ag. premier, 1910; attended Imperial and the Coronation, 1911; hon. cnsm. Royal Col. Inst.



WATSON, THOMAS GREENLEES (1907).—B. 1859; ed. at Wesley College, Melbourne; clk., administrative branch, Vict. rly., 1875; astt. clk. of commr. acctnt., legia. assem., 1882; clk. of commr. and sergeant at arms, 1890; 2nd clk. of commr. and clk. of private bills, 1891; clk. astt. of legia. assem., 1902; clk. of legia. assem., Vict. rly., July, 1902; clk. of legia. coun. and clk. of commr. accounts, Oct., 1910; has also served as prov. speaker, 1885-1888; sec. to parly. comtee., on rly., 1890-1901; gen. sec. and exec. offr. of Victoria for organising electors during visit of Duke and Duchess of Cambridge to York to open first parlmt. of commonwealth, May, 1901 (spec. thanked by H.R.H. the gov., prime minister, premier of Victoria, citizens of Melbourne); clk. of interchamber of premiers, etc., Melbourne, Oct., 1904; thanks of legia. assem. for services in connection with Jubilee of parlmt. of Victoria, 1906; ed. George V.

author of "Fifty Years of Responsible Government in Victoria, 1856-1906."



ATT, ISAIAH.—B. 1861; joined Coldstream Guards, 1880; served in Egyptian campaign; sgt.; clasp for Tel-el-Kebir; Khedive's star long service medal; srgt.-major of 1st Victoria Battalion, Melbourne, Nov., 1888, to June, 1893; ret. Coldstream Guards in 1901; clk. to col. sec., land Is., and srgt.-major of vols., 22nd Jan., Lieut., 15th July, 1905; capt. and adjutant, May, 1906.



ATT, JAMES.—Ed. at Oxford; classical schlr., Col. Coll., 1889; B.A. 1895; apptd. asst. dist. mwr., Southern Nigeria, 1899; dist. comsnr., 1902.



ATT, HON. WM. ALEXANDER.—M.H.A.; wr. of Victoria since Jan., 1909.



ATTLEY, ERNEST CHARLES.—Ed. gram. schl., St. Kitta, Crawford Coll., Maidenhead, and London nat. Coll.; called to bar (Leeward Is.) Aug., 1897; St. Kitta, 1885; loc. comsnr. of encumbered estates ct., 1886; visiting just. of the gaol, escheator-gen., St. K.-N., 1889; ag. asst. to attorney-gen., 1900; mem. ex. and leg. couns., and atty.-gen., Aug., 1901.



ATTS, FRANCIS, C.M.G. (1904) D.Sc., F.C.S., C.B. 1869; analytical chemist, Antigua, 1889; mem. legis. couns., 1897; analytical agricultural chemist, Jamaica, May, 1898; ward Is., May, 1899 (in connection with the trial dept. of agriculture for the W. Indies); subsequently made that of govt. chemist supt. of agric. for the Leeward Is.; mem. couns., Leeward Is., Oct., 1899; mem. exec. Antigua, Dec., 1903; Imperial comsnr. of in W. Indies, 1909; author of numerous arts and papers on W. Indian agriculture, etc.



AY, RT. HON. SIR SAMUEL JAMES, Bart.—B. 1836; ch. just., S. Australia, Mar., 1870; Lieut.-gov., Jan., 1891; Hon. D.C.L. (Oxon), LL.D. (Adelaide), 1892; hon. LL.D. Univ., Kingston, Canada), 1895; LL.D. (Melbourne), 1901; called to the bar, S. Australia, 1861; Q.C., 1871; mem. of house mem. and atty.-gen., 1875; vice-chancellor of Univ. of Adelaide, 1877 to 1883, and chanc. 1883; admstd. the govt. S. Australia ten 1877 (twice), 1878, 1883, 1889, 1893-4, 1895, 1902-3; mem. of the judicial comtce. of P.C., 1897.



EBB, FRANK.—Apptd. 3rd asst., Nyassaland May, 1901; 2nd grade res., Mar., 1908.



EBB, FREDERICK WILLIAM, C.M.G. (1894).—sec. clerk, legis. coun., N.S. Wales, 1851; G.P.O., 1853; clerk, legis. assm., dept., 1860; clerk, assm., 1877-86; clerk, 1888; apptd. J.P. 1888; sec. to National Australasian



WHEAR, JOHN FREDERICK.—B. 1867; ed. at public schools and at Prince of Wales Coll., P.E. Island; admitted as a barrister and attorney-at-law, 1890; served for four years as a city councillor in Charlottetown; elec. to the legis. assembly in 1900; as a mem. of the exec. coun. was associated with the late premier A. Peters and the present lieut. governor Rogers as delegates from the P.E.I. govt. for the settlement of provincial claims against the federal govt.; apptd. postmaster of Charlottetown, 1904; post office insp., 1st Apr., 1911.



WHEELER, CHARLES HENRY, M.D. (Queen's Univ., Irel.), L.M.R.H.D.—Surg. in the navy, Aug., 1881; dist. surg., Krian, Perak, Jan., 1886; J.F. for Krian, 1887.



WHEELER, RICHARD PATRICK.—P. 1880; apptd. typist, Imperial military railways, O.R.C., 1st Nov., 1900; ditto, refugee camps, 17th July 1901; ditto, treasy., 15th Nov., 1902; clk. and typist, treasy., O.R.C., 1st July, 1906.



WHEELER, W. C.M.G. (1904)—Treas. Br. Cent. Africa Prot., 28th Feb., 1892.

WHITE, Aubrey.—B. 1845; ed. Royal schl., Dungannon, and gram. schl., Carrickmacross, Ireland; forest ranger, Ontario, Canada, 1877; crown lands agt., 1879; inside ser. of dept., 1882; dep. min. of lands and forests, Ontario, 1887.



WHITE, Ernest Contley.—Clerk to armed forces, B.C. Africa, Apl., 1900; asst. collr., Nassau Prot., March, 1904; 2nd grade res., Jan., 1911.



WHITE, Lt. Col. Frederick, C.M.G. (1902).—B. 1847; clk., dept. of just., Canada, 1869; transfd. to dept. of S. of S. as clk.-in-charge of mounted pol. branch, Apr., 1876; ch. clk., Sept., 1878; comptroller of N.W. mounted pol. force of Canada, Nov., 1878; dep. head, July, 1883; priv. sec. to Rt. Hon. Sir Macdonald, 1880 to 1882; comnr. of N.W. Territories, 24th Aug., 1905.



WHITE, Field-Marshal Sir George S., V.C., G.C.B., G.C.S.I. (1898), G.C.M.G. (1901), G.C.I.E. (1893), G.C.V.O. (1909).—B. 1838; commander-in-chief, India, 1893-8; Q.M.G., 1898-9; commanding troops in Natal at outbreak of S. Afr. War, 1899; defended Ladysmith, Nov., 1899, to end of Feb., 1900; gov. Gibraltar, 1900-1905.



WHITE, James, F.R.G.S.; Grad. R.M.C., Kingston, Canada.—B. 1863; entd. civ. serv., Canada, 1884; geographer and ch. draughtsman, geo. surv., 1894; ch. geographer, dep. of Interior, 1899; sec., comnr. of conservation, 1909.



WHITE, Wallis Harry Brinsley.—Ed. at Bruton and Linc. Coll., Oxford; asst. master, St. Andrew's Coll., Grahamstown and Graaff Reinet Coll.; 1st class teacher's cert., Cape Colony; served during S. African War in Brabant's Horse (Queen's medal and four clasps); inspr. of schls., O.C., 5th Jan., 1901; ch. ditto, 1st Feb., 1904; ag. dir. of educn., Aug., 1905, to Feb., 1906, and Apr. to July, 1907.



WHITE, Lieut.-Col. William, C.M.G. (1897).—B. 1830; clk. in G.P.O., London, Feb., 1846; res. Apr., 1854; ch. clk. in money order branch of P.O. dept., Canada (on its establishment), Dec., 1854; sec. of the dept., Jan., 1861, and a comnr. to inquire into the organisation of the civ. ser., June, 1880; author of a "Post Office Gazetteer" of the Dominion; and of the "Annals of Canada," published in the "Canadian Monthly"; is lieut.-col. comdg. 43rd batt. of Canadian militia; and a J.P.; commd. Canadian team sent to Wimbledon in 1884; dep. P.M.G., 1888-1907.



WHITE, W. Arthur.—Apptd. after open compet. exam. for home civil serv. to P.O., Jan., 1890; 2nd div. clk., acctnt.-gen.'s dept., July, 1892; clk., controller's office, Mar., 1898; supt. of registrtn., G.P.O., Singapore, May, 1903; ag. supt. of mails, Oct., 1903; acctnt., postal dept., F.M.S., 1905.



WHITE, William Clarence.—B. 1847; ed. at Cent. Acad., Charlottetown, P.E.I.; regist. of deeds, P.E.I., 1891; regist. of deeds and comnr. of pub. lands, 1901.



WHITE, Hon. William Thomas, B.A.—B. 1866; ed. High Schools, Oakville and Brampton, Ont.; Univ. of Toronto (B.A.), graduate of the Ontario law schl.; apptd. manager National 1903 Co., Ltd., Toronto, 1899; subsequently WA. manager and vice-pres. of the same insti. Assoc. I mem. of the board of governors, Univ. asst. auto.; mem. of the Privy Council for surv., land min. of finance in Mr. Borden's 16th Junct., 1911.



WHITEHEAD, Charles Basil.—Asst. supt. Ceylon, 1904-1905, Sept., 1900; ag. second supt. Ceylon, 1905-1906, June to Sept., 1908, and from —B. 1859; b. Feb., 1879.



WHITFIELD, H. S.—Ck. and examt., ass't dept., W. Australia, 1886; ch. clk., Aug., 1891.



WHITING, John Berry.—B. 1859; entd. public serv., S. Australia, 1873; sec. of children's dept., 1886; sec. and regiar. of stock ag.-gen.'s dept., London, 1903.



WHITINGTON, Peter.—Ck. to acctnt. insolventy ct., and curator of intestate estate, Sept., 1896; 2nd clk., audit off., June, 1897; chief clk., audit off., June, 1875; sec. to succ. dept., Dec., 1896; mem. of pub. ser. classification bd., S. Aust., 1901, to June, 1902; mem. of W. Aust. pub. ser. coman., July, 1902; Dec., 1903; ag. comnr. of audit, S. Aust., May, 1907; comnr. of audit, Nov., 1907.



WHITNEY, Lt.-Col. Hon. Sir James Pinckney, B.A., LL.D., D.C.L., K.C.—B. 1843; entd. pub. schls. and Cornwall gram. schl.; called to bar, 1876; K.C., 1890; lieut.-comdt. royal militia; elec. to Ontario legis., 1888, 1890, 1894, 1898, 1902, 1905, 1908 and 1911; chosen leader of the opposition, 1890; called upon to form a new govt., Feb., 1905; prime min. and atty.-gen.; re-elec. by acclamation; relinquished atty.-gen. generalship, June, 1905, and assumed office of pres. of exec. coun.; deleg. to diocesan provincial and general synod, Church of England in Canada.



WHITRIDGE, Mathew Wm.—Served in N.W. civ. serv., 1898 to 1899; sub-native comm., Umbombo, Swaziland, Feb., 1903, to Mar., 1904; asst. comnr., ditto, 22nd Mar., 1907.



WHITTY, James Lionel.—Ed. Portarlington and gram. schl., Tipperary; passed exam. in Chinyanja; clk. in treasy., Brit. Cent. Afr. Prot., 21st May, 1901; asst. treas., Somaliland Prot., 31st Mar., 1904.



WHYHAM, William Henry, I.S.O. (1861)—B. 1848; entd. R.N., 1864; ret., July, 1873, and joined the Leeward Island colonial yacht "Union"; dist. mag., Dominica, Nov., 1874; nominated mem. of legis. assem., Mar., 1877; dist. mag. and inspr. of prisons, Antigua, Feb., 1878; ag. pres. of Nevis, 1882; hon. comnr. for Antigua at Col. and Ind. Exhibn., 1886; mem. legis. coun., Antigua, 1887; ag.-pres., Dominica Apr. to Nov., 1889; escheator-gen., 1890; ag. comnr., Montserrat, May to Sept., 1894; May to June, 1898; pres. legis. coun., and mem. exec. coun., Dec., 1896; ag. admtr., Dominica, July—Aug., 1896, to Feb., 1897, and Apr. to Sept., 1899; visiting just. gaol, 1898; offl. mem. legis. coun., July, 1898; non-elective mem. legis. coun., L. Is., Dec., 1898; ag. admtr., Dominica, July to Nov., 1900; ag. aud.-gen., L. Is., Nov., 1899, to May, 1900; June-July, 1900; Nov., 1900, to Mar., 1901; apptd. mem. exec. coun., L. Is., 1st Mar., 1902; ag. admtr., Dominica, 29th Aug., 1902, to 4th Feb., 1903; dist. mag., dists. A and B, Antigua, 1st June, 1903; del. to W. India quarantine conf. at Barbados, Apr., 1904.



WHYTE, James Wilkinson.—B. 1832; sol. to lands titles comanrs., Tasmania, 1883; recorder of titles, collr. of stamp duties, regiar. of public trusts, dep. registr. of deeds, 1884; mem. of bd. of advice on stamp duties, 1891; mem. of civ. ser. bd., 1901; ditto to comanrs. of taxes, 1905; comnr. of pub. debts sinking fund, 1903.



WIDDUP, John Chas. Ponsonby.—L.R.C.S. 1869; L.M. and L.R.C.P., 1870; supernumerary med. offr., Br. Guiana med. ser., 1881; gov't med. offr., Canye dist., 1886; health offr., pol. police and port surg., New Amsterdam, 1889; mem. Br. med. assoc.

WIGGINS, CLARE AVELING, M.R.C.S. (Eng.), R.C.P. (Lond.); med. offr., E. Africa Prot., Apr., 1901; med. offr., Uganda Prot., 4th Apr., 1909.



WIGHTWICK, CLAUDE.—B. 1881; ed. at Cambridge schl. and Pembroke Coll., Camb., 3rd cls., class. tripos; asst. res., N. Nigeria, 18th Aug., 1906.



WIGLEY, WILFRED MURRAY.—Ed. at Derby schl.; ag. 2nd mast., St. Kitts gram. schl., 1895; 2nd clk., regiar's off., St. Kitts, 1895; 1st clk., ag. clk., Nevis; ag. clk., legis. coun., 1897; resig. 1898 on entering at Temple; gazetted 2nd lieut., 1st City of London V.G.A., 1898; called to the bar, Mid. Temp., 28th Jan., 1901; nom. mem., Basseterre town bd., 1903; elected dep. chmn., 1905; lieut., St. Kitts def. force, 1905; mag. and coroner, Anguilla, and dep. judge, sum. juris. ct., Sept., 1906; mag., prov.-marshal, etc., Montserrat, Apr., 1909; M.L.C.



WILBRAHAM, D. F., B.A. (Oxon).—Master sup. ct. and regist.-gen., S. Leone, 1896; pol. mag., Oct., 1903; atty.-gen., June, 1908; ag. ch. just., June to Nov., 1902; June to Sept., 1908, Oct., 1909, to Mar., 1910, and Mar. to Aug., 1911; edited revised edition of laws of S. Leone, 1909.



WILBRAHAM, HON. REGINALD FRANCIS BOOTLE.—Ed. at Eton, Trin. Coll., Camb., and St. Mary's Hosp., Lond.; served throughout S. African war (Queen's medal, four clasps; King's medal, two clasps); attached to staff of govt. experimental farm, Potchefstroom, Transvaal, 1906; asst. dist. offr., Somaliland, 6th Feb., 1907.



WILDERS, WILLIAM EDWARD.—Joined R.I.C., Aug., 1887; B. of T. certif. of inspr. of weights and measures, Apr., 1900; inspr. of weights and measures, inspr. of food and drugs, and inspr. of explosives, Ireland, 1901; apptd. to Leeward Is. police force in Montserrat, Apr., 1902; sub.-inspr. of pol., 1905; inspr. of weights and measures, Oct., 1906; ag. inspr. of pol., Dominica, Oct., 1906, to Aug., 1907; ag. inspr. of wks. and roads, Montserrat, Sept., 1907; inspr. of wks. and roads, Montserrat, Apr., 1908; mem. of quarantine, health and schl. bds.; J.P. and mil. instr. to Montserrat defence reserve force; inspr. of pol. and adjutant of St. Kitts-Nevis defence force, Feb., 1909; visiting justice of the gaol, June, 1909.



WILHELM, THOMAS ANDREW.—B. 1853; entld. col. serv., S. Leone, 10th May, 1878; ag. librarian at govt. house for different periods, 1878-1888; clk., treasy., 19th Aug., 1881; accompanied Govr. Pinkett to Talliah war, 1882-1883; ag. 2nd clk., col. secretariat, 1887; ag. ch. clk., ditto, 1887; priv. sec. and accompanied Govr. Rowe on numerous expedts. to the Hinterland, between 1878 and 1888; 2nd clk., regist. gen.'s dept., 1st Oct., 1888; ag. ch. clk., ditto, and dep. regiar. of births and deaths, 1888-1889, and Jan. to July, 1890; ch. clk., off. of mast. of sup. ct. and regiar.-gen., 1890; dep. regiar.-gen., 3rd Aug., 1890; dep. regiar. of births and deaths, Freetown dist., 30th Aug., 1890; asst. inspr. of wks. and roads, survey dept., 1st Feb., 1891; acted at various times as offr. in charge of survey dept., 1891-1894; offr. in charge, survey dept., May to Oct., 1894; ditto, merchants' powder magazine, May to Oct., 1894; ch. draughtsman, survey dept., 15th Mar., 1895; offr. in charge of pub. wks., Moyamba, Mar. to June, 1899; ch. draughtsman, rly. wharf extension scheme, Mar. to Dec., 1901; ag. survr. of Crown lands, July to Sept., 1904.



WILKIE, DAVID.—B. 1880; Ed. at Christ's hosp., London; served in S. African campaign, 1900-1 (medal and 4 clasps); pay and acctng. branch, S.A.C., 1902; clk. to lieut.-gov., O.R.C., Sept., 1903; ag. priv. sec. to lieut.-gov., Apr. to June, 1906; ch. clk., gov.'s off., July, 1907; clk. of exec. coun., June, 1909; ag. priv. sec. to admnstr., O.R.C., Apr.-May, 1910; clk., gov.-gen.'s off., Union of S. Africa, 31st May, 1910.



WILKINSON, ERNEST EDWARD.—B. 1874; apptd., after compet. exam., clk., 2nd div., civ. ser., and assigned to the bd. of agriculture, May, 1894; transfd. to C.O., June, 1896; minor staff offr., ch. clk.'s dept., 1902.



WILKINSON, JOSEPH ERNEST.—B. 1873; clk., stores acctng. dept., Cape govt. rlys., Jan., 1901; joined Impl. mil. authorities, 30th Apr., 1901; clk. and typist, land sttlmnt. dept., O.R.C., Jan., 1902; asst. acctnt., 1902; examr. of accts., audit dept., 1st May, 1903.



WILKINSON, N.—Asst. supt. of wks., S. Sttlmnts., Aug., 1904.



WILKINSON, RICHARD JAMES.—B. 1867; ed. Trin. Coll., Camb. (exhibitioner); cadet, S.S., Oct., 1889; passed final exam. in Malay, July, 1891; ag. dist. offr., Bukit Mertajam, Dec., 1890, to Aug., 1891; ditto, Nibong Tebal, June to Aug., 1892; ag. asst. postmtr.-gen., Dec., 1892, to Mar., 1893; ag. 2nd asst. col. sec., Sept., 1893; ag. sheriff, Singapore, Sept., 1894, to May, 1895; ag. asst. audr. gen., July, 1895; ag. collr. land rev., Singapore, Mar., 1896; 3rd mag., Singapore, Mar. to Apr., 1896; ag. collr. land rev., Penang, Apr., 1896; also ag. supt. of educn., Penang, July, 1896; ag. 2nd mag., Singapore, Apr., 1897; ag. asst. col. sec. and clk. of coun., July, 1897; ag. dist. offr., P.W., Aug., 1897; ag. 2nd mag., Penang, Apr., 1898; ag. inspr. of schls., S. Sttlmnts., Aug., 1898; apptd. asst. postmtr.-gen., Penang, but still ag. inspr. of schls., Jan., 1899; ag. supt. educn., Penang, Aug., 1900; ag. 2nd asst. col. sec., Sept., 1900 to Jan., 1901; dist. offr., Dindings, Jan., 1902; ag. 2nd mag., Sing., Apr., 1903; inspr. of schls., F.M.S., Oct., 1903; dist. offr., Batang Padang, Perak, Nov., 1906; ag. sec. to rea., Perak, Nov., 1906; confirmed, Jan., 1909; ag. res., Negri Sembilan, 25th Feb., 1910; col. sec., S. Sttlmnts., 1911.



WILLCOCKS, LIEUT.-GEN. SIR JAMES, K.C.M.G. (1900, after relief of Coomassie), C.B., 1907; C.M.G. (1899); D.S.O.—B. 1857; Leinster regt.; 1st comsn., Jan., 1878; capt., 1884; major, 1893; tempy, lieut.-col., 1897; tempy, col., 1898; station staff offr., 1st cl., Bengal, July, 1890, to June, 1893; D.A.A.G., Bombay, Aug., 1894, to Nov., 1897; West African F.F., Nov., 1897, active service: Afghan war, 1878-80, medal; Mahood Wuzeree expedition, 1881; Soudan expdn., 1885, Suakin, med. with clasp, bronze star; Burmese expdn., 1885-89, as transport offr., and in charge of field comrkt., also acted as rd. commtd.; desig. Lon. Gaz., Sept. 2, 1887, med. with 2 clasps, D.S.O.; Chin-Lushai expdn., 1889-90, clasp; expdn. to Munipoor as transp. offr.; desig. Lon. Gaz., Aug. 14, 1891; N.W. frontier of India, 1897; A.A.G., Tochi field force, desig. Lon. Gaz., Feb. 11, 1898; 2nd in comnd. W. African F.F., Nov., 1898; officiating comndt., Sept., 1898; in commd. of Ashanti field force, relief of Kumasi, 1900; joined field force in S. Africa, 1902 (medal and clasp); commdg. Nowshera Brigade, India, 1902-7; Zakka Khel expdn., 1908; commdg. a division in India, 1908.



WILLETT, THOMAS GRAHAM.—B. 1883; ed. Merchant Taylors and St. John's Coll., Oxford (B.A.); cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Nov., 1906; off.

WILLEY, ARTHUR.—D.Sc. (Lond.); M.A. (Cantab.); F.R.S.—B. 1867; director of Colombo museum, Ceylon, 25th Apr., 1902; lecturer on biology at Ceylon Med. Coll., 1902-1907; marine biologist, 1907; editor of *Spolin Zeylanica*, 1903.



WILLIAMS, ALFRED.—B. 1863; pupil teacher, pub. schl., S. Australia, 1876; student, training coll., 1881; asst. teacher, pub. schl., 1882; head teacher, 1885; head master, 1889; dir. of educn., 1906.



WILLIAMS, ARTHUR HENRY.—Writer, Crown lands office, W. Australia, 1873; 2nd clk., 1881; clk., gov. s. office, 1883; acted as priv. sec. to Sir Frederick Broome in 1883 and 1884; clk. to coun., May, 1884; ch. clk., P.O., 1889; ch. clk., premier's dept., 1900; clk. to exec. coun., 1902.



WILLIAMS, CHAS. RIBY, C.M.G. (1902).—B. 1857; supervisor of customs, G. C. Col., 1884; on special mission to Aquamoo and Crepey, 1886; dist. commr., 1887; in charge Salagha recruiting expdn.; commr. with Taviewe expeditionary force, and on special mission to King of Buem, 1888; on special mission to E. Wassaw, 1889; controller of customs, Dec., 1890; on special mission to Krobo, 1891; ch. commr., Anglo-German bdry., coman., 1892; treas., Nov., 1895; offr. in charge of headqrs. during governor's absence, Mar., 1900; ag. col. sec. in 1897, 1898, 1899, 1900, 1903, 1904, 1905, 1906 and 1907; retired, Dec., 1909.



WILLIAMS, SIR HARTLEY, KT. BACH. (1894).—B. 1844; second son of Sir E. Eyre Williams, a former judge of Victoria; ed. at Repton and Trin. Coll., Oxon; B.A. 1865; called to the bar, In. Tem., 1867, and immediately went to Australia and commenced practice; judge of the sup. ct. of Victoria, 1881, and is now the sen. puisne judge; was a vice-pres. of the Victorian free educn. league; and is pres. of the Victorian league for promoting the opening of museums, etc., on Sundays; ret. on pension, 1903.



WILLIAMS, JAMES ALEXANDER, I.S.O. (1903).—B. 1856; messenger and copyist, secretariat, Lagos, Dec., 1871; clk. and keeper of debtors prison, June, 1875; 2nd clk., gov. s. office, G. Coast, Dec., 1875; ch. clk., 1877; clk., legis. coun., 1886; dist. commr., Dec., 1890.



WILLIAMS, JAMES ROWLAND.—B. 1860; ed. at Somersetshire Coll., Bath, and Trin. Coll., Oxford; scholar, 1879; 1st cls. class. mods., 1881; 2nd cls. final class. schools, 1883; B.A. 1883; M.A. 1888; inspr. of schls., Jamaica, 1884; ag. asst. col. sec., Nov., 1906, to Feb., 1907; govt. deleg. to Canadian reciprocity confce. at Barbados, 1908; suptdg. inspr. of schls., Jamaica, 1909; nom. mem. legis. coun., 1910.



WILLIAMS, JOHN, F.C.S.—B. 1869; asst. analyst, Br. Guiana, 1893; sen. ditto, 1893.



WILLIAMS, J. L., B.A.—Barrister-at-law; formerly ch. clk. of dept. of atty. gen. and of justice, New South Wales; under-sec. of the dept., July, 1905.



WILLIAMS, HON. SIR JOSHUA STRANGE, KT. BACH. (1911), M.A., LL.B.—B. 1837; ed. at Harrow and Trin. Coll., Camb.; 1st class in law tripes, 1858; jun. optime and chancellor's legal studies medallist, 1859; called to bar, Lincoln's Inn, Nov., 1859; dist. land-registr., Canterbury, N.Z., 1871; regiar.-gen. of land under the Land Transfer Act, 1872; puisne judge, sup. ct., of N. Zealand, Mar., 1875; is chancellor of Univ. of Otago.



WILLIAMS, MYLES.—Clk. to res. commr., Bech. Prot., 1902; ch. clk. and registr., 3rd Feb., 1906; ag. gov't. sec., Nov., 1908, to May, 1909, and from Apl. to Oct., 1911; passed Cape civ. ser. lower law exam., 1909.



WILLIAMS, O. G. R.—B. 1886; ed. Lancsing Coll. and Oxford; exhibitioner, Hertford Coll., 1906; 1st cls. mods., 1907; 1st cls. Lit. Hurn., 1909; Aubrey Moore studentship, 1910; app'td., after compet. exam., clk. in sec.'s off., In. Rev., Oct., 1910; 2nd cls. clk., C.O., Mar., 1911.



WILLIAMS, SIR RALPH CHAMPREYS, K.C.M.G. (1907); C.M.G. (1901).—B. 1848; ed. at Rossall; explored parts of Patagonia and Terra-del Fuego, 1873-4; and Cent. Africa, 1883-4; head of civil intell. dept., Bechuana-land expdn., 1884; author of "The British Lion in Bechuana-land"; Br. consular offr., S. African republic, 1887; Br. agt. there (with letter of credence), 1888; col. treas., and mem. of sanitary commn., Gibraltar, 1890; also contract offr., 1891; and also capt. of the port, 1895; rec'd. certif. and med. from the Italian govt. for services in connection with the wreck of the "Utopia," Mar. 17, 1891; col. sec., Barbados, 1897; res. commr., Bechuana-land Protec., 1901; gov'r., Windward Is., 8th Sept., 1906; gov'r., Newfoundland, 6th May, 1909; assumed govt., 6th Sept., 1909.



WILLIAMS, R. GREGSON.—Ed. at Rossall Schl., Caius Coll., Camb.; B.A. 3rd cls. boas. Science Tripos; Royal Schl. of Mines, A.S.R.M., 1st cls. diploma; post-graduate course, Myso goldfields, India; asst. res., N. Nigeria, 2nd Moh., 1911; ag. inspr. of mines, June, 1911; ag. chief survr., Sept., 1911.



WILLIAMS, THOMAS HENRY.—B. 1852; entd. pol. force, S. Aust., Jan., 1874; inspr. of stock, Aug., 1890; deputy chief inspr. of stock and deputy registr. of brands, July, 1905; chief inspr. of stock and chief inspr. and registr. of brands, Sept., 1911.



WILLIAMS, WILLIAM.—B. 1856; mun. water wks., Cyprus, 1878; surveying on military roads and draughtsman and aspt of wks. under R.E. offrs. when civil wks. were under their charge; draughtsman, chief storekeeper, and asst. aspt. of wks. under civil wks. dept., 2nd divisional engrn., Dec., 1898, and 1st divisional engrn., 1903; ag. offr. in charge of pub. wks. dept. on three occasions, and ag. D.P.W. on two occasions of three to six months' duration.



WILLIAMSON, ALEXANDER.—Educ. Edin. Univ., M.A., 1893; Bruce bursar, 1890-2; 1st prizeman, private inter. law, 1896; called to Scottish bar, 1897; lect. on jurisprudence, 1897; edited Herklots Lectures on Jurisprudence; author of "John Law of Lauriston" "Dictionary of French Legal Words and Phrases" and other books of historical and antiquarian interest; legal adviser, Crown pros. and pol. mag., Seychelles, Sept., 1908; ag. ch. just., May-Aug., 1909, and Apl. to Nov., 1911.



WILLIAMSON, GEORGE ALEXANDER, M.A., M.B., M.D., Aberd. Univ., D.T.M.—B. 1871; dist. med. offr., Cyprus, 1896; membre correspondant de la Société de Médecine de Gand, Belgium, 1901; dip. trop. med., Univ. of Liverpool, 1906; certif. in trop. med. (with distinction), Liverpool, 1900 and 1906; passed lower standard Greek, 1900; author of several articles in *British Medical Journal* and *Journal of Trop. Med.*, and a "Report on Malaria in Cyprus," 1903.



WILLIAMSON, VICTOR ALEXANDER, C.M.G. (1882).—Ed. at Westminster, and Chr. Ch., Oxford, of which he is M.A.; barrister-at-law of the In.

Tem., and goes the N.-E. circuit; one of the Royal comsrs. who in 1872 and 1873 inquired into the treatment of Indian imigrants in Mauritius; served for more than two years in Fiji without remuneration as chmn. of comsnr. for settling titles to land; was mem. of exec. and legis. couns., 1879-81; sec. to roy. comsnr. on London bd. of wks., 1888.



WILLIS, JOHN CHRISTOPHER, Sc.D.—B. 1868; Gonville and Caius Coll., Camb.; held for 3 years from 1890 the Frank Smart studentship for botan. research; was sen. asst. to regius prof. of botany, Glasgow Univ., and lecturer in botany, Queen Margaret's Coll., Glasgow; dir. of Royal Bot. Gardens, Ceylon, Aug., 1896; on special duty to Fed. Malay States, Mar., 1904; organising vice-pres. of Ceylon agric. soc'y.; author of "A Manual and Dictionary of the Flowering Plants and Ferns," and numerous scientific and economic papers; editor of "Annals of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Peradeniya," "Circulars and Agricultural Journal of Royal Botanic Gardens, Ceylon," and of the "Tropical Agriculturalist."



WILSON, C. J.—Medical offr., E.A.P., May, 1911.



WILSON, SIR DAVID, K.C.M.G. (1899), C.M.G. (1891), V.D. (1895).—B. 1838; ed. Trin. Coll., Glenalmond; home civ. serv., 1856-61; priv. sec. to lieut.-gov. of N. Brunswick, 1861-6; special comsnnr. to report upon the salmon fisheries of N.B.; capt. and adjt. 1st York militia, N.B., 1863; also at camp of instruction, 1865-6; major, St. John volt. batt. when on service on the American frontier, 1866; priv. sec. to gov. of Trinidad, 1866-9; supt. of prisons, 1869-70; stip. mag. E dist. of St. George, 1870-8; ag. S.J.P., Port of Spain and W. dist. of St. George, Sept., 1873-4; comnrs. of the N. prov. and sub-intendant of Crown lands, 1873 to 1897; mem. of exec. coun., 1894; ag. col. sec., Trinidad, various dates from Apr., 1873, to Jan., 1897; raised and organised Trinidad volt. force, 1879 to 1890; col. commd. L.I. volrs., 1897-, and is now hon. col.; gov. of Br. Honduras, Jan., 1907; ret. May, 1903.



WILSON, ERNEST GEORGE.—Ed. at Whitgift Coll.; G.N. rly., Apr., 1894, to June, 1901; asst. traffic mnr., Uganda rly., June, 1901.



WILSON, HON. FRANK, C.M.G. (1911).—B. 1859; mem. of city coun., Perth, W. Australia, 1895-98; M.L.A. for Canning, 1897, and for Perth, 1901; min. for rly. and mines, 1901, defeated on seeking re-election; M.L.A. for Sussex, 1904; min. of wks., Aug., 1905; col. treas., min. for educn. and agric., May, 1906; premier and col. treas., 1910-1911.



WILSON, GEORGE, C.B. (1899).—Sub-comsnnr., Uganda Prot., 30th Aug., 1894; dep. comsnnr., 1st Apr., 1902.



WILSON, G. GORDON.—Cadet, S.S., Nov., 1899; ag. 4th mag., Sing., Apr., 1902; passed final exam. in Chinese, Aug., 1902; ag. supt., money order branch and savings bank, Singapore, May, 1903; ag. asst. postmnr.-gen., Penang, 2nd Oct., 1903; supt., money order branch and sav. bank, Sing., but cont. to act in Penang.



WILSON, SIR HENRY FRANCIS, K.C.M.G. (1908), C.M.G. (1902).—B. 1859; ed. Rugby and Trin. Coll., Camb.; foundation scholar, 1878; sen. Bell's Univ. scholar, 1879; Chancellor's medal for English verse, 1880; 6th in 1st class classical tripos, and distinguished in exam. for Chancellor's class, med., 1882; fellow of Trin. Coll., 1884; M.A. 1885; called to the bar (Lincoln's Inn), 1888; sec. to Trinidad judicial inquiry comsnr., 1892; sent to Malta to collect evidence for the Protestant communities in connection with the Marriages Case, 1893; priv. sec. to the Rt. Hon. J. Chamberlain, M.P., S. of S. for cols., June, 1895; legal asst. in the C.O., 1897; went to S. Africa as legal asst. on high comsnnr.'s staff, Feb., 1900; sec. to administration of Orange River Colony, 1901; col. sec., June, 1902; acted as lieut.-gov., Apr. to Aug., 1903, Dec., 1903, to Aug., 1904, and from Aug. to Dec., 1906; mem. of I.C.O., 1903-1907 (represented O.R.C. on rly. comtee.).



WILSON, JAMES PHILLIPS.—M.L.C., S. Australia, 1906; min. of industry and agric., 3rd June, 1910.



WILSON, JOHN PLOWRIGHT.—Entd. serv. of Uganda Prot. from Imperial Br. E. Africa Co. as astl. collr., 1st Apr., 1893; collr., 1st Aug., 1895; sub-comsnnr., 29th July, 1899; I.B. E.A. Co.'s medal, Uganda, 1891-2; East and Central Africa medal, Uganda, 1897-8.



WILSON, LESLIE ORME.—R.M.L.I.; joined Royal Marines as 2nd lieut., 1st Feb., 1895; lieut., 1st Jan., 1896; capt., 1st Apr., 1901; served in H.M.S. "Hibernia" and H.M.S. "Australia"; astl. instructor of musketry, Gravesend, 1901; served with naval brigade in South Africa, 1899-1900 (ment. in desp., D.S.O.; medal with five clasps); A.D.C. to gov. of N. S. Wales, 12th July, 1903.



WILSON, T.—B. 1864; apptd., after compet. exam., clk. in the lower (now 2nd) div. of the civ. serv., and assigned to the G.P.O., Apr., 1882; transf. to the C.O., Dec., 1883; astl. regisr., July, 1896; higher grade, Jan., 1898; staff clk., first grade, 1911.



WILSON, T. R.—Ck. to comsnnr. of Crown lands, co. of Bourke, Victoria, Dec., 1852; ch. clk., med. dept., Mar., 1855; sec. to cent. board of health, Aug., 1865; ch. clk., ch. sec. of office, Jan., 1881; under-sec. Victoria, 1881; J.P., 1883; hon. mem., Br. Med. Assoc., 1890.



WINDHAM, WM.—Ck., res. comsnnr.'s office, Zulu native reserve, Apr., 1883; studt. interp., native affairs office, Natal, Mar., 1884; clk. and regisr. to special comsnnr. for Zulu affairs, Oct., 1885; clk. and interp. to res. comsnnr. and ch. ag., Zululand, June, 1887; sec. to ditto, Jan., 1889; clk., exec. coun., Natal, Sept., 1889; priv. sec. to gov., Natal, Oct., 1889; sec. for Zululand, Dec., 1889; priv. sec. to gov., Zululand, Feb., 1890; govt. sec. Zululand, Feb., 1894; astl. under-sec. for Zululand affairs, 1897; regisr. of deeds and regisr.-gen., Natal, Mar., 1898; (compiled abstract of opinions and court decisions upon transactions in deeds office, 1878-1898); sec. to native affairs dept., Transvaal, 23rd Sept., 1901; M.L.C., 1905.



WINGATE, G. R.—Ed. at Dulwich; astl. collr. of customs, N. Nigeria, 27th Feb., 1904; has acted as collr. on several occasions.



WINGFIELD, MAURICE E., C.M.G. (1912).—Ed. at Winchester and Trin. Coll. Camb.; M.A. 1896; sec. to royal comsnn., hut tax, S. Leone, 1898; ag. treas., collr. of cust., postmnr., and mem. ex. and leg. couns., Falkland Is., 1899-1900; priv. sec. to gov. of Queensland, 1902; priv. sec. to gov. gen. of Australia, 1903-4; astl. astl. sec. of S. African constitutions comtee., 1906; ag. col. sec., Gambia, Mar. to July, 1911; ag. gov., Gambia, 14th July to 18th Aug., 1911.



WINKFIELD, JOHN, M.A. (Oxon.) (Worcester Coll.)—B. 1862; called to the bar, Lincoln's Inn., Jan., 1889; dist. comsnnr., Lagos, 1896; ag. Queen's advocate, July, 1898, to May, 1899; ag. atty.-gen., July-Sept., 1900; atty.-gen., So. Nig., Dec., 1900; compiled laws of S. Nig., 1900-1901; puisne judge, Jan., 1905; ag. ch. just., Lagos, Jan., 1905; ditto,

Calabar, Aug., 1905, to Jan., 1906; ditto, Lagos, May to Oct., 1906; ditto, Calabar, Apr. to July, 1907; ditto, Lagos, July, 1907, to May, 1908; Nov., 1908, to Jan., 1909, and from Mar. to Sept., 1910.



WINTER, Sir Francis Pratt, Kt. (1900), C.M.G.(1892).—B. 1848; ag. atty.-gen., Fiji, 1887-88; ch. judicial offr. and mem. exec. and legis. couns., Br. N. Guinea, 1888; ag. admstr., Sept., 1894, to June, 1895, and Oct., 1898, to Mar., 1899; ret., 1903.



WISE, Bernhard Ringrose, K.C.—Atty.-gen., N.S. Wales, May, 1887, to Feb., 1888, 1899-1901, and 1901-4; mem. of Austn. Fed. Conv., 1897-8.



WISEMAN, R. A.—B. 1886; Ed. Monmouth Gram. Schl. and Oxford; math. demy, Magdalen Coll., 1905-1909; 2nd cl. math. moda., 1906; 2nd cls. hist., 1908; 2nd cls. jurisprudence, 1909; apptd. after compet. exam., clk., sec's dept., Admiralty, Mch., 1910; 2nd cls. clk., C.O., Mch., 1911.



WITTENOOOM, Hon. Sir E. H., K.C.M.G. (1900).—B. 1854; elected M.L.C., W. Australia, 1883; resig. in Dec.; re-elected 1884; resig. 1886; elected, M.L.C., July, 1894; min. for mines, Dec., 1894; agent-gen., July, 1898; resigned, 1901; M.L.C.



WODEHOUSE, Clarence B.—Entd. Sandhurst Coll., 1875; gazetted to 77th Regt., 1876; resigned coman., 1880; local commdt. of police, Cyprus, 1st Jan., 1894; ag. comsnr., Limasol, 12th July, 1894; ditto, Papho, 1st Apr., 1895; comsnr., Papho, 7th June, 1895.



WODEHOUSE, H. E., C.M.G. (1886).—B. 1845; ed. Repton Schl.; Hong Kong cadet, 1867; student interp., 1869; supt. of Chinese pol., 1870; asst. col. sec. and clk. of couns., 1875; pol. mag., 1880; hon. sec. to the local comsnr. in connection with the Indian and Col. Exhibn., and special comsnr. in London, 1886; mem. exec. coun., May, 1895; retired.



WODEHOUSE, Lieut.-Gen. Sir Josceline Henage, K.C.B.(1908), C.B.(1889), C.M.G.(1890).—B. 1852; ed. at R.M.A., Woolwich; comsnr. in R.A., 1872; served in Zulu war, 1879; Afghan war, 1880; Soudan, 1883-1894; gov. of Eng. frontier, 1887-1894; commd. "I" battery, R.H.A., 1894-1898; with Malakand field force (severely wounded), 1898; in action with Egyptian forces at Argin; infantry div. at Toski; Presidency dist., 1888-1899; Secunderabad, 1900-1; Lahore, 1902; Rawal Pindi, 1903; ag. in comd. of W. Comd., 1905; Zulu war (medal, 3 clasps); Soudan war (medal, 3 clasps); N.W. Frontier (medal and clasp); 2nd cls. Medjidiye; 2nd cls. Osmanieh; Egyptian bronze star; Order of Palm, French Govt.; gov. of Bermuda, 1907-1908; late G.O.C. Northern Army, India.



WODEHOUSE, P. P. J.—Ed. Eliz. Coll., Guernsey; first clk., reg.-gen.'s dept., Hong Kong, 1897-1900; passed in Chinese, 1899; census offr., 1900; asst. supt. of police, 1901; attached Punjab police, 1901-2; passed in Urdu, 1902; J.P., 1902; census offr., 1906; passed in Punjabi, 1908; mem. of bd. of examiners, 1907; ag. dep. supt. of pol. and fire brig., Oct., 1907 to Aug., 1908, May to Oct., 1909, and Jan. to May, 1911; census offr., 1911.



WOLFE, E. D. C.—Tonbridge schl. (1890-94); exhib. in mod. langs., Caius Coll., Camb. (1894); exhib. from Tonbridge schl. (1894); 3rd class mod. langs., tripos. (1896); 1st class Pt. I, and 2nd class Pt. II, Law Special (1897); B.A. (1897); cadet, F.M.S., 1898; sent to Canton to study Cantonese (1899); transf. to Hong Kong, 1901; passed cadet, Sept., 1901; registr., land ct., Nov., 1901; ag. 2nd pol. mag., Oct., 1902; ag. ass. registr.-gen., Nov., 1902; sec. to pub. wks. inquir. comm., 1902; collr. of Crown rent, New Territory, Feb., 1903; registr., land ct., Mar., 1903; ag. pol. mag., N.T., and asst. supt. of pol., 1903-4; collr. of Crown rent, N.T., 1904; seconded to Transvaal govt. serv., 1908; ag. 2nd pol. mag., Apr. and May, 1907; ag. inspr. of schls., 1907; ag. registr.-gen., Aug., 1907; asst. registr.-gen., Oct., 1907; ag. inspr. of schls., Oct., 1907, to Mar., 1909; ass. registr.-gen., Mar. to June, 1909; ag. head of sanitary dept., June, 1909; head of sanitary dept., Oct., 1909; ag. dir. of educn., in addition to other duties, July to Nov., 1911.



WOLFERTSTAN, LITTLETON EDWARD PIPE.—Ed. Eton and Clare Coll., Camb.; B.A., 1888; cadet, S.S., Oct., 1889; passed final exam. in Malay, July, 1891; ag. priv. sec. to Sir C. Smith. Jan. to Apr., 1890; ag. dist. offr., Bukit Mertajam, Feb. to Mar., and June to Nov., 1892; ag. dist. offr., S.W. dist., Penang, Mar., 1893; 3rd mag., Penang, Apr., 1895; ag. dist. offr., prov. Wellesley, June, 1897; 2nd mag., Singapore Aug., 1897; sheriff and dep. registr., sup. et. Singapore, 1898, but still ag. 2nd mag., Singapore; ag. dist. offr., Dindings, Feb., 1900; ag. collr. li. rev., Penang, May, 1900; ag. sec. to H. Cr. for Fed. Malay States, May, 1901; ag. sen. dist. ad. Prov. Wellesley, May, 1902; collector of lands and registr. of deeds, Penang, Aug., 1902; as assignee, S.S., Sept., 1903; sen. dist. offr., Prov. Wellesley, Feb., 1907; ag. 1st mag., Penang, Apr., 1907; ag. inspr. of prisons, S.S., Apr., 1909.



WOLFF, ERNEST CHARLES HOLDFORD.—F.M.S. civ. ser.; b. 1875; ed. at Merchiston and Trin. Coll., Oxford; B.A., 1897; cadet, Pahang, F.M.S., Nov., 1897; passed final exam. in Malay, May, 1899; ag. treas., supt. of post and tels., and collr. of stamp duties, Pahang, Jan., 1898; ag. asst. dist. offr., Pekan, May, 1899; ag. sec. to res., Negri Sembilan, May, 1901; sec. to ditto, Oct., 1901; asst. sec. to res., Selangor, Jan., 1903; dist. treas., Telok Anson, Jan., 1905, but still ag. sec. to res., N. Semb.; sec. to res., Negri Sembilan, Oct., 1905; ag. asst. sec. to res.-gen., F.M.S., May, 1906; dist. offr., Kuantan, Sept., 1909, but still ag. asst. sec. to res.-gen.



WOLLASTON, HARRY NEWTON PHILLIPS, C.M.G. (1907); I.S.O. (1903); LL.D., J.P.—B. 1846; apptd. (after exam.), to dept. of trade and custs., 1863; grad. with honrs., in law, Melb. Univ., 1884; called to the bar, 1884, and apptd. counsel to marine bd., Victoria, which apptnt. he held till 1901; promoted to bech. clk. of dept., 1899; apptd. permanent head of Victorian dept. of trade and cust., 1891; compt.-gen. of Commonwealth dept., of trade and cust., and permanent head, 1901-1911; represented Australia at Impl. shipping conference, London, 1907.



WOLESELEY, FIELD-MARSHAL VISCOUNT (created 1885), Sir Garnet Joseph Wolseley, G.C.B. (1880), K.C.M.G. (1870), G.C.M.G. and K.C.B. (1874), Baron (1882), K.P.(1885).—B. 1833; ensign, Mar., 1852; capt., Jan., 1855; major, 90th foot, Mar., 1859; lieut.-col., Apr., 1859; col., June, 1865; maj.-gen., 1874; lieut.-gen., Apr., 1878; gen. 1882; field-marshal, 1895; served with 80th foot in the Burmese war of 1852-53, severely wounded (medal); served with distinction in the Crimea and taking of Sebastopol, with the 90th L.I., and was severely wounded in a sortie, after which he received the Legion of Honour, the 5th class of the Medjidiye,

COLONIAL OFFICE LIST.



was also at the siege and capture of Lucknow; defence of Alumbagh, and numerous actions in India, when he was made brevet lieutenant-colonel in China on the staff of the qtrmr.-gen. throughout the Chinese campaign of 1860, for which he also received a medal and two clasps; qtrmr.-gen. in Canada, Oct., 1867; asst. adjutant-general, headqrs., 1871; apptd. for special service to G. Coast in connection with the Ashantee Aug., 1873; brought the Ashantee war to a successful conclusion, and received the thanks of House of Lords and the House of Commons for his services; was made a G.C.M.G. and a B.E., and a major-gen.; and inappr. gen. of cavalry forces, Apr., 1874; specially apptd. to minister temporarily the govt. of Natal from Sept., 1875; acted as vice-pres. of the S. African conf., Aug., 1876; mem. of Indian council, 1876; comanr. and comdr.-in-ch., July, 1878; gov. and comdr.-in-ch., S. Africa, May, 1879, and high comanr. for Africa; qtrmr.-gen., Apr., 1880; adjt.-gen., 1882; commanded the forces in Egypt, with temporary rank of gen., in 1882, and received thanks of both houses of parlmt., and a gage; and from the Khedive of Egypt the Order of the Osmanieh; commanded the expedit. and other operations in Egypt and Sudan for the relief of Gen. Gordon, 1884-6; received the thanks of both houses of parlmt.; raised to the rank of viscount, and made K.P.; author of "The Soldier's Pocket Book for Service"; comdr.-in-ch. in Ireland, 1890; r.-in-ch., 1890-1900.



D'ISLEY-BOURNE, J.T.—Asst. supt. of E.A.P.O., 1910.



JOD, A.E.—Ed. at Liverpool Coll.; scholar air. Coll., Oxford, 1903; 1st mods.; 2nd sum.; cadet, Hong Kong, 1907; offr. for 1st class of male assisted emigrants, July to Nov., 1908; ag. asst. regis.-gen., Nov., 1908, to Apr., 1909; and in May-June, 1909; passed cadet, pr., 1910; ag. asst. regis.-gen., Apr.-May, 1910; ag. asst. dist. offr., N.T., 18th May, 1910, c., 1911.



JOD, DAVID.—Ed. Gordon's Coll., Aberystwyth; ch. acctnt., P.W.D., Hong Kong, 1891; asst. of accs., corresp., and stores, P.W.D., 1894; so, to comm. on housing the Chinese during plague, 1894; ag. govt. assessor of taxes, July, 1900; May to Oct., 1902; and from Oct., 1906, to Oct., 1906; dir. of W. and O. fund, July, 1906; J.P., 1902.



JOD, FIELD-MARSHAL SIR HENRY EVELYN, G.C.B., G.C.M.G. (1828).—B. 1838; entered army 1852, and the army 1855; served in the Crimea; received the V.C. for his gallantry in driving down the rebels in the Seronge jungles; led the govt. of Natal from Feb. to Dec., 1881; landed the forces in Natal and the Transvaal, as amem. of the roy. comanr. for the settlement of affairs of the Transvaal, 1881, but dissented from the report; commanded the 2nd brigade, v., in Egypt, 1882; apptd. by the Khedive command of the Egyptian troops, 1883; in the Nile expedit., 1884; comdr.-of the forces, Oct., 1886; qtrmr.-gen. of the forces, Oct., 1886; apptd. to command of army corps, 1901.



JOD, HENRY FREDERICK.—B. 1878; apptd. Uganda rly. comtce., 7th Aug., 1897; asst. to C.O. as supplementary clk., 1st Apr., 1897.



JOD, JOHN R.—Ed. City of Lond. schl. and foundation scholar of Jesus Coll., 1896; 1st cl. class. tripes, 1899; B.A., 1899; cadet, Hong Kong, 1899; regis. of land ct., Nov., 1900; ag. pol. mag. in New Territories, May to July, 1902; J.P., 1902; passed cadet, 1902; mem. land ct., 1903-4; asst. land offr. in N.T., Jan., 1905; ag. asst. reg.-gen., Apr. to Aug., 1905; mem. of squatters' bd., May, 1906; ag. 2nd pol. mag., Mar., 1906; dep. regis. and appraiser, sup. ct., Nov., 1908; 2nd pol. mag., 21st Mar., 1909.



WOOD, JOHN T.—M.A. (Oxon); F.R.G.S.; registrar of mining rights, Transvaal.



WOODARD, HENRY.—Govt. storekeeper, B. Cent. Africa Prot., 1893; ch. commissariat offr., 1894; ch. transport offr., 1906.



WOODCOCK, GEORGE ALBERT.—Ed. at St. John's Coll., Battersea; apptd. asst. master Victoria Coll., Hong Kong, 15th Mar., 1890; final bar, Gray's Inn, 1897; ag. sec., sanitary bd., Mar., 1900, to July, 1901; sec. of san. bd., July, 1901; J.P., 1902; called to the bar, Gray's Inn, 5th July, 1905; ag. dep. regis. and acctnt., sup. ct., Hong Kong, Dec., 1908; 1st clk., magistracy, Sept., 1909; sec. to licensing bd., 17th Dec., 1909.



WOODE, BENJAMIN TREGASKIS, M.R.P.S.—B. 1869; ed. at Wesleyan High school, Freetown, S. Leone; jun. clk., Queen's advocate off., S.
